title: Bank-switch helper argument recovery: memory-latch sites resolve to unknown, poisoning discrete-mapper state
description:
Follow-up to grm-3x1 (2026-07-31), which closed the memory-latch REACHABILITY gap and
proved that reachability was never the whole problem. All five moved real-ROM titles now
SEE their latch stores and recover NOTHING from them.

MEASURED (all 12 hash-pinned titles, before -> after grm-3x1):
  title         overlay refs   bank comments   warnings
  contra          0 ->    0       0 ->   0      1 ->  6
  dragonpower     0 ->    0       0 ->   0      3 ->  6
  shenlong        0 ->    0       0 ->   0      1 ->  6
  wizwarr        17 ->   17      11 ->  11      4 ->  8
  megaman      1781 -> 1703     153 -> 151      3 -> 37

TWO DISTINCT SYMPTOMS, one root cause.

(1) NO NEW ANNOTATIONS. Contras board-level "no mechanism write was observed" warning is
gone -- replaced by a per-site warning at c142 ("mechanism write with a genuinely
undeterminable value") plus five "call to bank-switch helper FUN_c13f whose bank argument
could not be recovered at this call site". So the helper IS identified; the ARGUMENT is
not recoverable at any call site. Same shape on dragonpower/shenlong (FUN_ffbe, FUN_8eeb)
-- both GxROM Dragon Ball titles, so likely one shared engine.

(2) MEGAMAN REGRESSED -78 overlay refs / -2 bank comments / +34 warnings. Mechanism:
StoredValueScanner aborts a backward scan when it steps over a mechanism write (class
javadoc: "a base value read further back would predate that write, so falling back to the
in-state would be unsound"). Making more writes visible therefore makes more scans abort.
Watch FUN_c39c: it appears in 11 of the 34 new warnings as an unrecoverable helper.
Site 9067 specifically degraded from "bank -> 6 (bank=6) via FUN_d846" to a warning.

WHY IT MATTERS BOTH WAYS. The optimistic reading is that megamans 1781 refs came from a
model blind to 7 of its 25 switch sites, so shrinking them is a correctness gain. The
pessimistic reading is that we traded correct annotations for warnings. NOBODY HAS
CHECKED WHICH -- that determination is the first task here, and it decides whether
megaman ever gets blessed (it is measurement-only per grm-g73).

LIKELY DIRECTION: the helper-evaluation path already works for megamans absolute sites
("via FUN_d131" etc), so the machinery exists; what is missing is recovering the bank
argument at the CALL SITE when the value arrives via a register the callers set from a
table/variable rather than an immediate. grm-hb6.4 (per-game site hints as dataflow
seeds) is a plausible lever for the genuinely unrecoverable remainder.

DO NOT "fix" this by relaxing the mid-scan abort without an argument -- the abort is
sound and the grm-3x1 javadoc records why.

title: Backward value scan lacks single-predecessor check; over-confident value at CFG join
description: StoredValueScanner.java:114. resolveStoredValue only validates the prev->cur fall-through edge, never that cur has a single predecessor, so at a control-flow join it attributes the fall-through path value to the store with full confidence. Failure: LDA #$05 / BEQ t / LDA #$0A / t: STA $8000 returns fullyKnown 0x0A, ignoring A=$05 on the BEQ path. The immediate-fold and AND/ORA-fold paths bypass the engine merge (resolveLoad path is safe as it uses merged inStateAtStore). Fix: require block-leader / single-predecessor before folding a local immediate. Verdict CONFIRMED. Found by /code-review high.
notes: Fixed (commit pending): resolveStoredValue now aborts to unknown() at a control-flow join, detected via isControlFlowJoin (incoming flow Reference to cur from an addr other than prev). RESIDUAL: unresolved computed/indirect jumps leave no reference, so a join reached only by a jump table is not detected -- conservative in the safe direction (worst case a fold we'd otherwise make), not a wrong-value risk.
close_reason: Fixed in board-banking value-recovery hardening commit; verified compiles + buildExtension against Ghidra 12.1.2

title: recoverCallArgument guesses bank register (A-first), recording wrong bank
description: BoardBankAnalyzer.java:558. recoverCallArgument tries A then X then Y and returns the first that resolves to any immediate, not the register the helper actually reads. Failure: LDX #3 / LDA #$80 / JSR SelectBank (helper takes bank in X, its store not locally resolvable) -> A-first scan returns $80, engine records bank 0x80 instead of 3; downstream refs retargeted to wrong overlay, EOL comment lies. Fix pattern: propagate unknown() when the convention is ambiguous rather than a confident guess. Verdict CONFIRMED. Found by /code-review high.
notes: Fixed (commit pending): recoverCallArgument now scans the register the helper actually stores into its mechanism (HelperModel.argReg from StoredValueScanner.storeRegister on the switch site) instead of the A-first guess. Strictly dominates old behavior: the STX-helper failure now records the correct bank; transform helpers degrade to prior behavior, never worse. RESIDUAL follow-up: a helper that stores a DIFFERENT register than the caller loads (e.g. TXA / STA mechanism) still mis-attributes, needing recursive convention inference inside the helper body. Not filing separately unless it bites.
close_reason: Fixed in board-banking value-recovery hardening commit; verified compiles + buildExtension against Ghidra 12.1.2

title: Build pipeline: YAML -> .gdt data-type archive generator (Gradle task)
description: Per gib.1.2 review decision (struct source of truth, option 3 from the start): a Gradle build task with Ghidra jars on the classpath walks the descriptor/types YAML and emits a .gdt data-type archive via FileDataTypeManager.createFileArchive(). The loader consumes ONLY the .gdt (standard archive API, no YAML parser in runtime). Rules: .gdt is a build artifact — never committed, never hand-edited, CI always regenerates. Deliverables: (a) YAML->DataType builder (structs, flags/enums, field comments); (b) Gradle task wiring; (c) generated c64ref-derived struct YAML for VIC-II/SID/CIA feeding it (or stub until the c64ref generator lands). Bonus: the .gdt doubles as a standalone publishable artifact usable in stock Ghidra.
close_reason: YAML->.gdt build pipeline complete and independently verified: gradle buildGdt emits build/c64.gdt (5 named types, reopen-verified via openFileArchive); buildExtension confirms snakeyaml stays build-only (absent from shipped zip). Commit b636540.

title: Design: memory map schema and system descriptor format
description: Design the data model that describes a game system architecture: ROM regions (cart, BIOS), RAM regions, IO port ranges, mirroring rules, initial data type definitions (structs, enums). Goal: one descriptor file per system (YAML or JSON) drives the loader with zero hard-coded system knowledge in Java/Python. Output: draft schema + one worked example (e.g. SNES).
notes:
DESCRIPTOR DATA SOURCES (2026-07-03 survey):
- mist64/c64ref — canonical structured C64 reference (src/kernal/, src/c64io/, src/c64mem/); structured text + Python generator that can be adapted to emit JSON/YAML. THE upstream to consume.
- sajattack/c64-asm-labels — ready-made whole-memory-map label files in ACME/KickAssembler/radare2/VICE-.sym formats. CHECK LICENSE — derived from 'Mapping the Commodore 64' (Leemon), possible encumbrance like c64_ghidra.
- VICE .sym format ('al <hexaddr> .<label>') = de-facto C64 symbol interchange; Ghidra ImportSymbolsScript parses similar.
- KickAssembler built-in MOS6526_CIA/MOS6581_SID/MOS6569_VICII structs = cross-check for IO register offsets.
- c64-wiki Memory_Map banking table — the $0001 LORAM/HIRAM/CHAREN combinations to encode as named bank configurations in the descriptor (the part no existing loader handles).
Schema implication: descriptor needs (a) regions, (b) named bank configurations selecting overlay sets, (c) symbol/label imports with provenance, (d) IO register struct definitions.
BANK-SWITCHING DESCRIPTOR DESIGN (user, 2026-07-03): decompose per-game banking info as MECHANISM + INITIAL STATE.
- C64: mechanism = write to $01; initial state = #$37 (BASIC+KERNAL+IO active, CHARROM inactive). Later add cartridge GAME/EXROM lines — note .crt header bytes 0x18/0x19 literally store EXROM/GAME line state, so for cartridges initial state can come from the container, like iNES headers do for NES.
- NES: mechanism = the Mapper (defines memory segmentation + what constitutes register reads/writes); initial state = PCB-specific -> descriptor-friendly.
- Implication for schema: MECHANISM is code-shaped (pluggable strategies — NES mappers will need several categories of register-access handling, e.g. MMC1's serial 5-write loading), INITIAL STATE is pure data. Descriptor names a mechanism + parameters + initial state; the earlier 'named bank configurations' idea becomes the STATE SPACE the mechanism transitions through.
- C64 = deliberately simple POC of the mechanism plumbing (single-register write) before NES stresses programmability.
DRAFT 1 DELIVERED (2026-07-03): ghidra/SCHEMA.md (design notes) + ghidra/descriptors/c64.yaml (worked example; YAML-validated, 8 bank states / 3 windows / 7 fixed regions).
Key schema decisions in draft:
- windows/occupants model: banked ranges declare candidate occupants; states assign occupant per window. Enumerated states table (C64: 8 PLA rows) OR mechanism-computed (NES) — schema allows both.
- context_register field links descriptor to the bundled 6510 language's bank context field (TMode-style); agreement needs a build-time check (open question 3).
- symbol sets are user-toggleable with game-RE defaults (kernal-api ON, kernal-zeropage/basic OFF since games reuse those).
- 'kind: entry' symbols create functions on EMPTY ROM slots so KERNAL calls resolve to named stubs without ROM bytes.
- descriptor states hardware facts (repeat_to mirrors); loader chooses representation.
OPEN QUESTIONS for user review (in SCHEMA.md): (1) struct source of truth: inline YAML vs c64ref-generated vs .gdt archives; (2) symbol interchange: YAML canonical + VICE .sym importer, or .sym canonical; (3) descriptor<->language agreement check for context register.
TODO before close: verify ROM SHA1s against real ROM set (placeholders emptied); adapt c64ref generator for the generated/*.yaml sources; VICE cross-check of the 8-state table.
SCHEMA REVISION 1.1 (user input, 2026-07-03): READ/WRITE ASYMMETRY. Bank mapping must differentiate read vs write targets — C64 writes under BASIC/KERNAL ROM always reach the RAM beneath; $D000 varies by state (IO: r/w both chips; CHARGEN: read ROM, write RAM). Modeled as occupant property 'on_write' (not per-state): omitted=self, <occupant>=write-through, 'mechanism'=writes are bank-mechanism events (NES mapper writes — doubles as analyzer watch-list), 'none'=open bus (Ultimax later). Per-state variance falls out of occupant selection automatically.
GIB.2 IMPLICATION recorded in SCHEMA.md: Ghidra resolves references to ONE address space — LDA $A000 and STA $A000 in the same bank state cannot target different blocks. Context-aware resolution hook must be ACCESS-TYPE-AWARE: (context, address, access) -> block. Loader-policy mitigation meanwhile: analyzer annotates stores into ROM-mapped ranges with reference to on_write target.
REVIEW DECISIONS (user, 2026-07-03) — SCHEMA.md open questions resolved:
(1) Structs: YAML canonical, .gdt generated at BUILD time FROM THE START (not staged via load-time builder). Loader only consumes .gdt. New bead grm-1.5 (blocks gib.1.3) for the generator + Gradle task. .gdt = build artifact, never committed; CI regenerates.
(2) Symbols: YAML canonical + VICE .sym importer (community files, cc65/KickAss output).
(3) Descriptor<->language: LOAD-TIME check — loader verifies language declares banking.context_register, clear error on mismatch.
IMPLICATION flagged to user: building the Gradle/.gdt pipeline is the first real EXTENSION CODE, which per the incubation rule ('extension gets its own repo from creation time') approaches repo-birth.
close_reason: Schema/system-descriptor format validated end-to-end by the grm-1.3 POC: the compiled c64.map + c64.gdt (from machines/c64.yaml) drove a real Ghidra 12.1.2 C64 PRG import — regions, banked windows (home-in-base), IO chip structs, and KERNAL symbols all applied correctly (headless-verified, CHROUT Function@base:ffd2). Schema documented in docs/SCHEMA.md + docs/MAP_FORMAT.md. Residual schema growth (cartridge EXROM/GAME bits, .crt, flow-tracked banking) is tracked under the gib.2 line, not this design bead.

title: Survey Ghidra loader/extension API and existing console loaders
description: Audit: what API surface does Ghidra expose for loaders? What existing open-source console loaders exist (NES, SNES, PS1)? Determine if extension vs. script vs. core loader plugin is the right artifact type. Survey: GhidraNES, ghidra-snes-loader, ghidra-psx-ldr, etc. Output: a short design note on the extension/loader API contract and gaps vs. our needs.
notes:
PRIOR ART SEEDS (from user, 2026-07-03):
- https://github.com/hippietrail/RetroGhidra — multi-retro-system Ghidra extension; POSSIBLE CONTRIBUTION TARGET instead of reinvention; survey must include contribute-vs-build verdict
- https://github.com/c64cryptoboy/c64_ghidra — possible useful C64-specific material
- https://cesarmiquel.github.io/tech/art/science/design/2020/03/13/week-13.html — general Ghidra console-RE article, many good links
- HN 46882389 (Ghidra MCP tools) — spun off to bead game-music-extraction-gib.3
IN-TREE FINDINGS (D:/git/ghidra): 6502 + 65C02 languages exist, NO 6510 variant (identical ISA; $00/$01 port is a memory-map annotation concern, not decode). No console loaders in-tree; nearest templates: BinaryLoader, MotorolaHexLoader (opinion package).
RETROGHIDRA SURVEY VERDICT (2026-07-03): BUILD NEW, upstream shallow pieces later as goodwill.
- ~29 loaders, all uniformly SHALLOW: parse header -> createInitializedBlock -> entry point. No loader anywhere models IO registers, full hw memory maps, or banking; zero use of overlay address spaces (even Atari 2600 mirrors are just separately-named blocks).
- C64 support = thin CommodorePrgLoader.java (single CODE block, no C64 labels), C64CrtLoader.java (3 labels), D80 filesystem. No KERNAL labels, no VIC/SID/CIA, no banking.
- Architecture = one Java class per format, knowledge as Java constants; NO data-driven layer (an unused GSON GhidraLabel.java hints it was considered). Our descriptor-driven design would FIGHT their architecture, not extend it.
- Apache 2.0; alive but small (35 stars, ~4-5 contributors, bursty maintenance; Ghidra 12.x compat PR #23 open with engagement but unmerged).
- Use as REFERENCE for Ghidra API boilerplate only. After our C64 loader works, consider upstreaming format-detection pieces as standalone PR.

C64_GHIDRA SURVEY (2026-07-03): c64cryptoboy/c64_ghidra has working C64BinLoader.java (PRG load-addr detection, override option, zp/stack blocks, overlay mode) and c64LabelAddrs.py (74KB comprehensive KERNAL/BASIC ROM+RAM symbol tables). NO LICENSE SPECIFIED -> cannot reuse code/data verbatim; either ask author or regenerate labels from primary sources. No banking model, no VIC/SID/CIA annotations.

GHIDRA-MCP (2026-07-03): bethington/ghidra-mcp very active, Apache 2.0, 256 tools; assumes binary already loaded, modern-platform-oriented. Useful AFTER loader works (agent-driven verification of blocks/labels). Recorded on gib.3. HN criticisms: tool-count bloat degrades LLM tool use; fork quality concerns vs LaurieWired original.
BROAD SURVEY (2026-07-03): Three memory-map patterns exist in the wild, all painful:
(1) Overlay blocks at same vaddr (fortenbt/Ghidra-SMB3INES-Loader, Dan Sanderson C64 Crossroads walkthrough) — hardware-truthful but cross-block flow analysis breaks;
(2) Separate non-overlapping blocks per bank (kylewlacy/GhidraNes, 40+ mappers) — no addr conflicts but loses runtime-address correspondence;
(3) Manual annotation after flat load (Sanderson: ~38 hand edits for a small program).
NOBODY does descriptor-driven automation — that is the confirmed gap.
Key references: SMB3 loader = best overlay+symbol-injection example (11,500 symbols); achan1989/ghidra-snes-loader = best LoROM/HiROM mirror modeling (study for SNES phase); zeroKilo/C64LoaderWV (.d64); Dan Sanderson https://dansanderson.com/mega65/crossroads-part-2/ = clearest description of the manual workflow our loader automates; retroreversing.com/ghidra = curated plugin list.
GHIDRA-C64HELPERS CONTENTS (user inspection, 2026-07-03): (a) 6510-specific processor definition — easily incorporated into our extension (extensions can bundle languages; resolves the no-6510-in-tree gap properly instead of aliasing 6502); (b) PETSCII visualizer — feeds the generalized string-detection feature (bead grm-1.4).
close_reason: Survey complete. Deliverable: ghidra/SURVEY.md in GME (migrates with epic). Verdict: build new extension; RetroGhidra as API reference only. Key findings: descriptor-driven automation is a confirmed empty niche; upstream banked-memory space is open with 6 motivating issues and a clear proposal shape (TMode-style context + context-aware address resolution hook); c64ref is the clean descriptor data source; 6510 language bundle-able from ghidra-c64helpers precedent.

title: writesInRange misses refless indexed stores and overlay-space write references
description:
Two independent detection gaps in MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.writesInRange (MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.java:193-203), both found while investigating grm-2yx (2026-07-31). Candidate root cause for Contra's zero-annotation result; scope the fix by what the grm-2yx probe reports.

GAP 1 -- REFERENCE-ONLY PREDICATE. writesInRange inspects ONLY instr.getReferencesFrom(). But a 6502 indexed operand's base arrives as a Scalar, not an Address, so CodeManager lays down NO default operand reference at disassembly time; references appear only once constant propagation covers the code, and const-prop only covers function bodies. The canonical UxROM bus-conflict switch idiom IS 'LDA #n / TAX / STA banktable,X'. So a latch store in code outside any function is invisible even if it is disassembled. Note the class javadoc (:64-67) already ANTICIPATES indexed stores, so this is an unnoticed gap rather than a deliberate limit.

GAP 2 -- DEFAULT-SPACE ONLY. Line :196 requires to.getAddressSpace().equals(space) where space is the default space captured at configure (:130). A latch store EXECUTING FROM INSIDE a PRG_LO_B<n> overlay gets its write reference in the overlay space and is silently skipped. bankInvariantRomByte (:229) already has to undo exactly this normalization, which shows the shape was known elsewhere in the same file.

FIX SHAPE: two-tier predicate -- keep today's reference tier, add an operand-decode tier gated on StoredValueScanner.storeRegister != null (so RMW like INC $8000 keeps reference-only behavior and does not newly poison state), decoding via StoredValueScanner.plainAbsoluteTarget (:341) and LoopIdioms.indexedBase (LoopIdioms.java:82). Normalize the reference tier's space test by OFFSET in a separate commit, since it can move real-ROM goldens.

SOUNDNESS RULING (record in the javadoc): with addr_mask present AND an indexed operand, DECLINE -- base & 0xF says nothing about (base+X) & 0xF, and claiming a match would latch prg_bank off an IRQ-register write, exactly what addr_mask exists to prevent. Declining under-reports, which is the pre-existing failure mode; poisoning with unknown() instead would flood four Bandai goldens with WARNINGs as a side effect of a reachability fix. Do NOT require base+0xFF <= end -- that rejects the canonical $FFE0 bank table.

REGRESSION SURFACE: cacheable() stays true (operand decode is a pure function of (program, instr)). memory-latch is the only cacheable strategy in the tree, so MMC1/MMC3/C64/C128/PET are untouched by construction. Real-ROM goldens that may move: contra, db3, wizwarr (AxROM), dragonpower/shenlong (GxROM), and megaman -- megaman is measurement-only per grm-g73, do NOT bless it.
close_reason: Both gaps fixed (f1251fd, f6adf70) and goldens blessed (638b5c3). Full gate green. Reachability closed and the decline rule confirmed by byte-identical Bandai goldens; the annotation predictions did not hold -- value recovery tracked as grm-hum.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
MEASURED AND CONFIRMED as the root cause of grm-2yx (BankReachProbe.java, 2026-07-31). Raising confidence and scope -- this affects FOUR real titles, not one.

Per-title (sites / abs / indexed / withWriteRef / wouldMatchToday / invisible-but-reachable):
  contra        1 /  0 / 1 /  0 /  0 /  1   -- 'STA $FFD0,X' at $C142 in FUN_c13f, reachable, no write ref
  dragonpower   1 /  0 / 1 /  0 /  0 /  1   -- identical shape on GxROM
  megaman      25 / 18 / 7 / 18 / 18 /  7   -- the WORKING control still loses all 7 of its indexed sites
  wizwarr      10 / 10 / 0 /  6 /  6 /  4   -- 4 ABS sites with no reference at all

GAP 1 (refless stores) is confirmed and is broader than 'indexed': wizwarr shows refless ABS sites too, i.e. absolute stores in code constant propagation never covered. The operand-decode fallback covers both.

GAP 2 (overlay-space refs) was NOT exercised by any of these titles -- every observed site had ovl=false, so no evidence for or against it here. Keep the fix but expect no golden movement from it on this sample.

EXPECTED GOLDEN MOVEMENT after the fix: contra and dragonpower should go from 0 refs to resolving; megaman +7 sites (coordinate with grm-g73, which is measurement-only per the user); wizwarr +4. dbz2/dbz_datach/dbz_saiyan/db3 should NOT move -- their invisible sites are correct addr_mask decode rejections, and the ruling that an indexed operand with addr_mask present must DECLINE keeps them that way. If a Bandai golden moves, the decline rule is wrong and the change must not land.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED AND MEASURED (2026-07-31). Both gaps fixed as specified; the fix works, the
PREDICTIONS DID NOT HOLD. Recording the correction so the next reader is not misled.

WHAT HELD:
- The decline rule is right. All four Bandai titles re-blessed BYTE-IDENTICAL, i.e. the
  stated go/no-go condition passed. zelda/smb3 identical too (MMC1/MMC3 untouched).
- Reachability IS fixed. Contras board-level "no bank-switch write observed" warning is
  gone; the analyzer now sees STA $FFD0,X at c142 and identifies helper FUN_c13f.
- GAP 2 moves nothing, exactly as the probe predicted. Verified experimentally rather
  than by commit boundary: the five moved dumps are byte-identical with and without the
  gap-2 commit. The prescribed split was still honored (f1251fd, f6adf70).

WHAT DID NOT HOLD -- all three annotation predictions were wrong:
- "contra and dragonpower should go from 0 refs to resolving": they did NOT. Both stay at
  0 refs / 0 bank comments; they trade one board-level warning for 6 site warnings.
- "megaman +7 sites": megaman went BACKWARDS -- 1781 -> 1703 overlay refs, 153 -> 151
  bank comments, 3 -> 37 warnings.
- shenlong moved too (1 -> 6 warnings); the issue listed it only as "may move".

ROOT CAUSE OF THE MISS: seeing a mechanism write and recovering its value are different
problems. Every newly-visible site is inside a bank-switch helper taking the bank in a
register from its caller, which the block-local backward scan cannot resolve. And
StoredValueScanners mid-scan mechanism-write abort means MORE visible writes = MORE
aborted scans, which is precisely how megaman lost coverage. Filed as grm-hum (P1),
including the open question of whether megamans lost 78 refs were correct or were
artifacts of the blind spot.

DISPOSITION: landed. Goldens blessed for contra/wizwarr/dragonpower/shenlong (638b5c3);
megaman deliberately held back per grm-g73, so the real-ROM tier steady state is
unchanged at 10 PASS / 1 FAIL / 1 SKIP.

title: Per-game descriptor tier: title-keyed hints, harvested annotation, and export/reapply
description:
Third descriptor tier alongside per-machine (c64.yaml) and per-board (nes-mmc3.yaml): a descriptor keyed by ROM CONTENT that carries program facts rather than machine facts. Design: docs/per-game-descriptors-design.md; vision: docs/vision-board-banking.md section 5.5 + principle 7 + M4b.

MOTIVATION (measured, not speculative): grm-2yx found Contra (UxROM) and Dragon Ball 3 (Bandai FCG) build a provably correct overlay layout yet resolve ZERO bank annotations, while Mega Man on the SAME board resolves 1781 refs. Static analysis has a real ceiling -- a switch routine entered only via a computed jump, or copied to RAM and executed there, is unreachable by any amount of dataflow. Above that ceiling the honest answer is to RECORD the answer once, not to interrogate the next user for it.

SETTLED DECISIONS (user, 2026-07-31):
(1) DISTRIBUTION: curated in-repo set (machines/games/*.yaml -> data/games/*.map, bundled) PLUS a user-directory overlay scanned at runtime.
(2) IDENTITY: PRG-content hash primary + whole-file SHA-256 alias. Descriptor-declared matching criteria deferred (separate bead).
(3) FORMAT: YAML everywhere -- ship MapCompiler + snakeyaml in the extension so runtime and build read ONE format through ONE validator, and an exported file is directly usable as a PR.
(4) PRECEDENCE: site hints are SEEDS (no precedence question -- they cannot contradict analysis, only give it a starting point); value hints rank below recovered dataflow values and above descriptor defaults, the slot placement overrides already occupy.

THREE USES, ONE ARTIFACT: hints where analysis provably stalls; annotation harvested from mature public disassemblies (Zelda/Metroid/Mega Man/SMB) so a first import beats FUN_c34a soup; portability -- exporting your own annotation layer and replaying it on a fresh import is the same file pointed the other way.

SUCCESS MEASURE: each generation of hint files should be SMALLER than the last. A hint recording something the analyzer should have derived is a defect, not a win.

title: Tier-2 JUnit cannot see bundled sleigh languages (6510:LE:16:default et al)
description:
PROBLEM
`new ProgramBuilder("Test", "6510:LE:16:default")` from `gradle test` throws
LanguageNotFoundException. Every ProgramBuilder-based test in the repo
(BankStrategyProgramTest.java:62, DescriptorCopyHintAnalyzerTest.java:82) is forced onto
the stock `6502:LE:16:default`, so our OWN bundled language has zero Tier-2 coverage --
its only coverage is the Tier-3 headless golden suite, which is slow and coarse
(no per-opcode mnemonic/p-code assertions).

This blocks writing real per-opcode tests for the language variants in grm-azg.

WHY IT FAILS (Ghidra 12.1.2 source)
- Ghidra discovers languages through *module data directories*, not the java classpath, so
  putting data/ on testImplementation would not help.
- `AbstractGenericTest.createApplicationLayout()` (Ghidra/Framework/Generic/.../
  AbstractGenericTest.java:208-209) returns a plain `GhidraTestApplicationLayout`.
- `GhidraTestApplicationLayout.findGhidraModules()` discovers modules under
  `applicationRootDirs` (the Ghidra INSTALL only) filtered by `ClasspathFilter` +
  `getDependentModulePatterns()` -- which is why stock languages work: the pattern set
  includes File.separator + "Processors" + File.separator.
- `GhidraTestApplicationLayout.findExtensionInstallationDirectories()` returns
  `<userTempDir>/ExtensionInstallDir`, NOT the settings dir -- so the
  `-Dapplication.settingsdir` trick that tools/banktest/run-banktest.sh:121-132 uses for
  headless does NOT carry over to JUnit.
- build.gradle:437-441's `test {}` sets no system properties and does not dependsOn
  sleighCompile, and data/languages/*.sla is gitignored, so on a fresh checkout the .sla
  does not exist when tests run.

APPROACH
`createApplicationLayout()` is protected and overridable, and Ghidra's own tests already
use exactly this pattern (Ghidra/Test/IntegrationTest/.../DWARFRegisterMappingsTest.java:52,
TutorialDebuggerScreenShots.java:154 -- both return an anonymous GhidraTestApplicationLayout
subclass).

Add a repo-local abstract base test class that overrides `createApplicationLayout()` to
return a GhidraTestApplicationLayout whose `findGhidraModules()` merges in THIS repo as a
module. The repo root already has Module.manifest + extension.properties, so
ModuleUtilities recognizes it as a module root; data/languages/*.sla is then found the
same way a stock processor module's is.

Then in build.gradle `test {}`:
  - dependsOn 'sleighCompile'   (so the .sla exists)
  - systemProperty for the module dir (projectDir), read by the base class

Hermetic: no extension install, no %APPDATA%, no settings dir -- reads data/languages
straight out of the working tree, so it is safe under parallel git worktrees.

ACCEPTANCE
- A JUnit test doing `new ProgramBuilder("Test", "6510:LE:16:default")` +
  `setBytes(addr, "a9 05", true)` disassembles and asserts mnemonic "LDA".

title: c64.yaml declares context_register c64bank no language provides; warns on every analysis
description: BoardBankAnalyzer logs 'context_register c64bank is not a register declared by this language; context stamping skipped' on every C64 disassembly. Cause: machines/c64.yaml:145 still carries the aspirational context_register: c64bank. grm-bk6 decided the bundled 6510 language is system-neutral and declares NO bank-state register; grm-5zg made the field optional and stripped the equivalent fake nesbank from the NES descriptors but missed c64bank; grm-tpg then upgraded the silent skip to a warning as a typo diagnostic, so the leftover placeholder now fires that diagnostic on every run. docs/SCHEMA.md:153-160 already documents the convention: descriptors whose language has no such register omit the property. Fix: drop the field from c64.yaml, keep the design rationale as a comment. Preserves the typo warning for real typos.
close_reason: Removed context_register: c64bank from machines/c64.yaml (design rationale kept as a comment). The name never resolved: grm-bk6 made the bundled 6510 language system-neutral with no bank-state register, grm-5zg made the field optional and stripped the equivalent fake nesbank from the NES descriptors but missed c64bank, and grm-tpg turned the analyzer's silent skip into a warning as a typo diagnostic -- so the leftover placeholder fired that diagnostic on every C64 analysis. SCHEMA.md's documented convention (omit when the language has no such register) is now followed. Verified: freshly built/installed c64.map has its banking block and zero context_register, so stampContextRegister returns at the !banking.has guard before logging. Full build-and-test.sh check green, no golden churn. The typo warning still works for real typos; grm-wkk remains the issue that would introduce a real register.

title: Descriptor build tasks declare no inputs/outputs: every build re-runs all 26 .gdt/.map compilations
description:
The per-machine buildXxxGdt/buildXxxMap tasks (and buildPetsciiMap/buildScreencodeMap) are plain JavaExec with no inputs/outputs declared, so Gradle can never mark them UP-TO-DATE. Every `gradle buildExtension` -- including every tools/install-gui.ps1 run -- forks ~26 JVMs to recompile identical .gdt/.map artifacts from unchanged YAML.

Dependency shape (verified in tools/gdtbuilder):
- MapCompiler/GdtBuilder use YamlSupport.loadComposed, which follows `include:` directives resolved RELATIVE TO THE DESCRIPTOR'S OWN DIR (all current uses point at machines/fragments/nes-common.yaml).
- Both also resolve `source:` keys (register sets / type defs) the same relative way -- all current uses point at machines/generated/*.yaml.
- PetsciiCompiler: single plain load of machines/generated/petscii.yaml.
- ScreencodeCompiler: plain load of both petscii.yaml and screencode.yaml.
- The compiler classes themselves are an input: a gdtbuilder source change must invalidate outputs.

So a per-task input of just its own yaml would be WRONG (stale on fragment/generated/compiler edits).

sleighCompile already declares inputs/outputs correctly; this is the same treatment for the descriptor pipeline.

REPORTED BY: user, observing tools/install-gui.ps1 rebuild everything unconditionally.
close_reason: Declared inputs/outputs on all 26 per-machine buildXxxGdt/buildXxxMap tasks plus buildPetsciiMap/buildScreencodeMap. Shared input is fileTree('machines', excludes:['*.yaml']) -- Ant '*' does not cross '/', so it drops sibling top-level descriptors but keeps fragments/ and generated/, covering both the include: and source: reach; gdtBuilder classes are an input too. No-op rebuild now 38/38 up-to-date in 1s (was 25s). Full gate green.

title: Extension zip ships repo metadata: .beads Dolt DB is 30 MB of a 31 MB extension
description:
The built extension packages the entire repo working directory, not just the extension. Top-level entries in dist/ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC_20260725_ghidra-retro-machines.zip include .agents, .beads, .claude, .codex, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, docs, gsrc, machines, tools -- alongside the legitimate lib, data, ghidra_scripts, extension.properties, Module.manifest.

SIZE (uncompressed, by top-level entry):
  30.75 MB  .beads      <-- the Dolt issue-tracker database
   0.47 MB  tools
   0.41 MB  lib         <-- the actual extension
   0.21 MB  docs
   0.20 MB  data
   0.16 MB  machines
So the shipped artifact is roughly 75x the size of the code it exists to deliver (15.6 MB compressed, essentially all of it the beads DB), and installing it drops a full copy of the project issue tracker -- including every issue description and note -- into the user's Ghidra Extensions dir. Confirmed on disk: the pre-2026-07-25 GUI install at %APPDATA%/ghidra/ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC/Extensions/ghidra-retro-machines/ contained .beads/issues.jsonl, export-state.json and last-touched.

FIX POINT ALREADY EXISTS AND IS UNUSED. build.gradle carries the stock comment 'Exclude additional files from the built extension / Ex: buildExtension.exclude .idea/**' with no actual excludes below it. Adding excludes there is the documented mechanism.

CARE REQUIRED -- do not blanket-exclude. data/ IS read at runtime (the loaders read data/machines/<id>.map and the .gdt archives), so it must stay. machines/ holds the authored YAML that the gdtBuilder compiles INTO data/ at build time and is probably not needed at runtime, but that needs proving rather than assuming. Verify with the full acceptance gate after any exclusion, since a wrongly-excluded resource would surface as a loader failure, and note that tools/banktest's dump cache key includes the extension identity so a contents change is expected to invalidate it.

RELATED: grm-9ut (release-build strategy on GitHub Actions) should not ship artifacts in this shape; fixing this is effectively a prerequisite for publishing a release.

DISCOVERED: while writing tools/install-gui.ps1 (the GUI install helper), which installs exactly this zip.
notes:
2026-07-25 (Chris): PREFER AN ALLOWLIST over adding excludes. Being deliberate about what ships is the right shape here -- a denylist silently ships whatever new top-level file or dir lands next (this bug exists precisely because Ghidra's stock denylist predates .beads/.claude/.agents/.codex), whereas an allowlist fails loudly and safely: forget an entry and a resource is MISSING, which the acceptance gate catches, rather than silently leaked.

MECHANISM (read from D:/ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC/support/buildExtension.gradle:94-142). buildExtension is a Zip task assembled from three child specs: from(extension.properties) with token filtering, from(project.jar) into lib/, and -- the culprit -- from(project.projectDir) carrying a FIXED exclude list: build/**, *.gradle, certification.manifest, dist/**, bin/**, src/**, .gradle/**, .vscode/**, .classpath, .project, .pydevproject, .settings/**, developer_scripts, .antProperties.xml, gradlew, gradlew.bat, gradle/wrapper/*. That list is Eclipse-era and knows nothing about our layout. It lives in the install's support/ file, and our build.gradle marks that region DO NOT MODIFY, so we cannot edit the spec directly -- we can only add via buildExtension.exclude/.include from the designated hook in our own build.gradle.

SUGGESTED SHAPE -- allowlist as the source of truth, fed through the supported hook, so it is fail-safe without forking the stock task or fighting Gradle's root-vs-child CopySpec pattern semantics (a bare root-level include risks filtering the jar and extension.properties children too, and should not be attempted without testing):

  def SHIPPED = ['lib', 'data', 'ghidra_scripts', 'extension.properties', 'Module.manifest', 'README.md', 'LICENSE'] as Set
  projectDir.listFiles().each { f ->
      if (!(f.name in SHIPPED)) { buildExtension.exclude f.name; buildExtension.exclude f.name + '/**' }
  }

Anything new at the top level is then excluded by default and must be added deliberately.

STILL TO PROVE before landing, do not assume: which entries are genuinely runtime-required. data/ IS (loaders read data/machines/<id>.map and the .gdt archives). ghidra_scripts/ and Module.manifest are Ghidra-required. gsrc/ and machines/ (authored YAML compiled into data/ at build time) are probably not, but verify. Run the full acceptance gate after: a wrongly-excluded resource surfaces as a loader failure, and tools/banktest's dump cache key includes the extension identity, so expect cache invalidation on the first run.
close_reason: Allowlist added at build.gradle's buildExtension.exclude hook; zip 16.9 MB -> 510 KB, top level now exactly lib/data/ghidra_scripts/extension.properties/Module.manifest/README.md/LICENSE. machines/ proven droppable (findFilesByExtensionInMyModule -> accumulateDataFilesByExtension walks data/ only). gradle.properties was also leaking (stock denylist covers *.gradle, not *.properties). Full acceptance gate green.

title: Real-ROM reachability gap: Contra (UxROM) / DB3 (Bandai FCG) bank-switch routine never disassembled, so no mechanism write is ever seen
description: Root cause behind grm-9oz's silent-zero (now diagnosed by a WARNING bookmark). On Contra (U) (UxROM/m2) and Dragon Ball 3 (Bandai FCG/m16) the correct overlay layout is built but the forward dataflow classifies ZERO stores as mechanism writes -- no bank comments/refs. Contrast Mega Man (same UxROM board) which resolves 1781 refs. Hypothesis (issue grm-9oz (a)): the switch routine is reached only via an indirect/table jump that auto-analysis never disassembled, so MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.writesInRange() (src/main/java/retromachines/MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.java:193) never runs on the real store. Distinct from grm-m95 (Bandai FCG/GxROM sites that ARE detected but whose VALUE is unrecoverable). Candidate directions: (a) seed disassembly of the switch routine (follow indirect/table-jump targets), or (b) a ROM-wide scan for in-range writes independent of dataflow reachability, feeding those sites into runDataflow. Repro: bash tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh check <romdir> (contra, db3); the new 'no bank-switch write observed' WARNING bookmark now flags exactly these titles.
close_reason: Diagnosed and superseded. The premise in the title is disproven: Contra's bank-switch routine is disassembled, in a function, and reachable -- BankReachProbe measurement recorded in the comments. The real cause is a detection bug in writesInRange (grm-3x1, now measured across four titles), and DB3's separate RAM-resident-stub cause is split to its own bead. Nothing left under this title that is not tracked more accurately elsewhere. The probe that produced the diagnosis is committed as tools/banktest/BankReachProbe.java (d3d1da0).

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
PROBE RESULTS (BankReachProbe.java, 2026-07-31) -- THE PREMISE OF THIS BEAD IS WRONG.

Contra's bank-switch routine IS disassembled, IS inside a function, and IS reachable from the seed set. This is NOT a reachability gap.

  BANKREACH site c142 mech=0 reg=A mode=IDX base=ffd0 ovl=false decode=MATCH func=FUN_c13f reach=YES refs=1 write=NO today=NO space=RAM
  verdict.i   orphan-sites 0            <- NOT case (i)
  verdict.ii  no-site-in-disassembled-code false   <- NOT case (ii)
  verdict.iii invisible-reachable-sites 1          <- CASE (iii), decisively

Root cause: 'STA $FFD0,X' at $C142 in FUN_c13f -- the canonical UxROM bus-conflict bank table at $FFD0. It carries NO write reference in range (write=NO), so MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.writesInRange, which inspects only instr.getReferencesFrom(), never sees it. Exactly grm-3x1 gap 1.

NOT ISOLATED -- cross-title measurement (sites / abs / idx / withWriteRef / wouldMatchToday / invisible):
  contra        1 /  0 / 1 /  0 /  0 /  1     all lost
  dragonpower   1 /  0 / 1 /  0 /  0 /  1     IDENTICAL shape (GxROM)
  megaman      25 / 18 / 7 / 18 / 18 /  7     works only because 18 ABS sites carry it; loses all 7 indexed
  wizwarr      10 / 10 / 0 /  6 /  6 /  4     4 refless ABS sites lost
  db3           1 /  1 / 0 /  1 /  0 /  1     see below
  smb3, zelda   no memory-latch mechanism (MMC3/MMC1) -- probe correctly finds nothing

So the indexed/refless gap is systematic across memory-latch boards, not a Contra quirk. Fixing grm-3x1 should resolve Contra and dragonpower outright and add sites on megaman/wizwarr.

DB3 IS A DIFFERENT STORY: its single disassembled site is mode=ABS with a write reference but decode=MISS -- i.e. correctly rejected as a sibling CHR/IRQ register write, not the PRG bank register. There is NO PRG-register write anywhere in DB3's disassembled code, which confirms the RAM-resident-stub hypothesis in substance. Splitting per plan.

PROBE CAVEAT worth knowing: verdict.iii conflates 'wrongly missed' with 'correctly rejected by the addr_mask decode'. On dbz2/dbz_saiyan it reports ~50 because those boards have ~50 sibling register writes that SHOULD be rejected. The per-site decode= column disambiguates; read it, not the verdict, on addr_mask boards.

ACTION: retitle/repoint this bead at grm-3x1 as the fix, or close it in favour of grm-3x1 + the DB3 split.

title: Silent zero-detection: some banked real ROMs get correct layout but no bank annotations OR warnings (Contra m2, Dragon Ball 3 m16)
description: Found in grm-hdn real-ROM acceptance (tools/banktest/realrom, goldens contra.dump/db3.dump). On Contra (U) (UxROM/mapper 2) and Dragon Ball 3 - Gokuu Den (Bandai FCG/mapper 16) the loader builds the correct block/overlay layout (7 and 7 overlay banks resp.) but the analyzer emits ZERO bank-> comments, ZERO cross-bank overlay refs, ZERO banked instructions, AND ZERO warnings. Contrast Mega Man (U) -- same UxROM board -- which resolves 1781 overlay refs / 153 comments. The zero-WARNINGS part is the concern: the forward dataflow never classified any store as a mechanism write, so the user gets no signal that banking analysis found nothing (vs. the 'undeterminable value' warnings other titles do get). Likely the bank-switch routine is reached only via an indirect/table jump that auto-analysis never disassembled, so the mechanism write is never seen. Investigate: (a) is the switch code unreached (banked-code reachability), or (b) is a real store being silently skipped by the memory-latch scanner? At minimum, surface a diagnostic when a board declares a switch mechanism but the analyzer observed no mechanism writes at all. Repro: bash tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh check <romdir> (contra, db3).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text: Fixed the 'silent' concern (the at-minimum ask): BoardBankAnalyzer now emits a WARNING bookmark 'no bank-switch write observed' on the settled/fixpoint-stable run when a board declares bank-switch mechanism(s) but zero mechanism writes (switchResults + callSwitches) were observed; it retracts the bookmark if a later settled run does find a write, so it reflects only the settled state. RealRomDump counts it, so contra.dump/db3.dump go warnings 0->1 (re-blessed). All chunks + full acceptance gate pass; only contra/db3 goldens changed. Root-cause reachability (why the switch is unreached) split out to grm-2yx.

title: grm-z15 #5: PRG placement coverage validation (prg_placeable flag + MapCompiler check)
description: Regression #5: planPrgSlices throws mid-import on matching.size()!=1 (a map gap/overlap in RAM placement coverage), and nothing validates coverage at build time. The C64 P6510 placement target is kind:io, invisible to a generic kind-based check. Fix (user decision): introduce a prg_placeable:true region flag (schema + MapCompiler.buildRegions passthrough), set on P6510 in c64.yaml; C64PrgLoader.isAdditionalPrgTarget reads the flag instead of the hardcoded name 'P6510'. Add a machine-neutral MapCompiler coverage check: union(kind:ram regions, prg_placeable regions, per-window-collapsed ram-occupant ranges) must be internally contiguous with no gaps/overlaps, else IllegalArgumentException naming the gap/overlap. Keep the loader's matching.size()!=1 throw as defense-in-depth. MapCompilerVerify: add verifyRamCoverage negative tests (ram gap + ram overlap fail; gapless map with a prg_placeable io region compiles).
acceptance_criteria: A gapped/overlapping RAM map fails to COMPILE with a clear error naming the gap/overlap; shipped c64.yaml still compiles (gate re-compiles it); loader reads prg_placeable instead of the P6510 name hardcode; verifyMapCompiler passes with new negatives; full gate green.
close_reason: Added prg_placeable declarative flag (base isAdditionalPrgTarget reads it; C64PrgLoader name-hardcode override deleted; c64.yaml P6510 flagged, behavior-identical). MapCompiler.validateRamCoverage rejects a gapped/overlapping RAM placement union at COMPILE time, gated on formats.prg.placement:load_address (fires for c64/pet4032/c128, correctly skipped for NES whose non-contiguous RAM is loaded by NesRomLoader). MapCompilerVerify negatives (gap+overlap) + positive (prg_placeable io region) added. All three CBM maps still compile; full gate green. Commit b0ac942.

title: grm-z15 #4: degrade path aborts (windows NPE guard + honest up-front skip validation)
description: Regression #4: (a) planPrgSlices (~550) iterates map.getAsJsonArray('windows') unguarded though load() guards map.has('windows') (369) — NPE on a windows-less map. (b) When window setup is skipped (banking incomplete, ~374-378), window-occupant slices never get a placement space and persistPrgPlacement throws 'No address space was created for PRG target ...' (720-723), aborting the import the skip message promised to survive. Fix: guard the planPrgSlices windows loop on map.has('windows'); when window setup will be skipped, decide up front — if any planned PRG slice targets a window occupant, throw a clear IOException naming the incomplete banking + the needed window placement, instead of the deep persist throw; otherwise (no window-targeted slices, PET-like) proceed. Verification is inspection-level + the existing PET windows:[] path; the incomplete-banking C64 path can't be fixtured without map-injection plumbing (loader hardwires machines/c64.map) — file a P4 follow-up for a malformed-map harness.
acceptance_criteria: Windows-less map plans region slices with no NPE; a skipped-window map with window-targeted slices fails with a clear message (not the deep persist throw); PET no-window path still imports; full gate green. Regression-4 runtime coverage documented as inspection-level with a filed follow-up bead.
close_reason: planPrgSlices now guards map.has('windows') (no NPE on a windows-less map). When banking is incomplete, load() fails up front with a clear message if any PRG slice targets a banked-window occupant (windowOccupantSliceTargets), instead of the confusing deep persistPrgPlacement 'No address space' abort; otherwise the skip proceeds (PET-like). Both need a hand-edited map to reach; verified by inspection + existing PET windows:[] path. Fixture deferred to grm-abg. Full gate green. Commit 6f1894a.

title: grm-z15 #3: struct typing across a carved init/uninit boundary (per-field fallback)
description: Regression #3: AbstractCbmPrgLoader.createCarvedTarget (~632-633) applies a region struct at region.start even when PRG slices split the region into initialized+uninitialized blocks; DataUtilities.createData cannot span a memory-block boundary in Ghidra 12.1.2, so it fails (only logged) and the 6510 port registers are left untyped. Repro: load $FF00, 0x101 payload (wrap places 1 byte at $0000, so R6510 at $0000-$0001 straddles). Fix: add a per-field fallback in DescriptorSupport.applyStructType — keep whole-struct createData as the fast path; on failure, if the resolved type is a Structure, createData each getDefinedComponents() component at start+component.getOffset(), catching/logging per field. R6510 is DDR@0 + PORT@1 (two 1-byte fields), so DDR@$0000 types even when PORT@$0001 is in a separate block. Single-block callers never hit the fallback (unchanged). Fixture: prgstraddletest.
acceptance_criteria: Wrapped $FF00 import leaves the R6510 DDR field typed at $0000 (port registers no longer fully untyped); single-block struct typing unchanged; prgstraddletest golden passes; full gate green.
close_reason: Regression #3 does NOT reproduce in Ghidra 12.1.2: built the reviewer's exact repro (load $FF00, 0x101 payload -> R6510 straddling init $0000 / uninit $0001) as headless fixture prgstraddletest; Listing.createData spans the carved block boundary fine (whole R6510 struct typed, len=2, neither field dropped). The reviewer's 'createData can't span a block boundary' premise is empirically false. No code change needed; kept prgstraddletest as a permanent guard. Full gate green. Commit be78857.

title: grm-z15 #1+#2: restore unconditional entry point + 2-byte zero-payload PRG acceptance
description: Regression #1: AbstractCbmPrgLoader.java entry block (~454-485) gates addExternalEntryPoint on entryBlock.isExecute(); a load address in a non-executable block (e.g. $0000 P6510 io) silently gets no entry point/function/log. Fix: call addExternalEntryPoint unconditionally (old behavior — records entry only, no code assumption); keep markAsFunction gated on executableEntry; add a log line when the function mark is skipped for a non-exec entry block. Regression #2 (user decision: RESTORE acceptance): lower findSupportedLoadSpecs threshold 3->2; in load(), when prgLength==0 build the full map/symbols but skip placement, label the load address with a clear log, do not resolve an entry against absent slices; remove the now-reachable dead prgLength==0 throw. Fixtures: prgentrytest (load $0000, non-exec P6510) and prgemptytest (2-byte zero payload) in the c64-loader chunk.
acceptance_criteria: PRG at $0000 gets an external entry point + no function + a log explaining the skipped function mark; 2-byte PRG imports under C64PrgLoader with full map/symbols; new prgentrytest/prgemptytest goldens pass; full gate green with existing goldens byte-identical.
close_reason: addExternalEntryPoint now unconditional (entry point recorded even for a non-exec load block, e.g. $0000 P6510); markAsFunction still gated on executability with an explanatory log. 2-byte zero-payload PRG accepted again (threshold 3->2, dead throw removed, dedicated zero-payload entry path). Fixtures prgentrytest/prgemptytest added. Full gate green, existing goldens byte-identical. Commit c2cbecb.

title: Single source of truth for targeted Ghidra version (currently 12.1.2)
description: User decision 2026-07-19: one canonical declaration of the targeted Ghidra version, everything else by reference; user commits to keeping the D:\ install and the D:\git\ghidra checkout in step with it. close_reason: Landed: gradle.properties ghidraTargetVersion=12.1.2 canonical; build.gradle version guard (verified failing correctly against a 12.0.4 path and passing against 12.1.2); banktest scripts derive defaults; CLAUDE.md de-literaled; bd memory build-ghidra-install-dir updated. title: PETSCII string search analyzer, system.text descriptor key, headless fixture
description: Phases E+F-fixture of the grm-1.4 plan. MapCompiler.buildSystem passes system.text through verbatim (~6 lines; buildSystem currently whitelists keys) + MapCompilerVerify assertion. Add system.text blocks to machines/c64.yaml, pet4032.yaml, c128.yaml: { encoding: petscii, variant: <match machine petscii_variant>, string_search: { min_length: 4 } }. New PetsciiStringAnalyzer: descriptor-gated via DescriptorSupport.MAP_PATH_PROPERTY (mirrors C64BasicAnalyzer conventions, AnalyzerRunLog), gated on PRESENCE of system.text.string_search, late priority; StringSearcher(Program, CharSetRecognizer, minLen, 1, false, false) with recognizer accepting 0x20-0x5F (+0xC1-0xDA shifted); callback skips non-1-byte-datatype finds (UTF-16 side-scan guard), acts only on fully-undefined ranges, applies TerminatedPetsciiStringDataType when trailing 0x00 else fixed PetsciiStringDataType via DataUtilities.createData CLEAR_ALL_UNDEFINED_CONFLICT_DATA. title: PETSCII charset SPI, TableCharset, six string datatypes, verifyCharsets
description: Phases C+D+F-gradle of the grm-1.4 plan. (C) retromachines.charset.RetroCharsetProvider (CharsetProvider SPI; lazy, exception-swallowing init — a throwing provider poisons Charset.availableCharsets() JVM-wide; loads compiled maps via getResourceAsStream, NO Ghidra imports) + TableCharset (int[256]->codepoint decoder, surrogate-aware maxCharsPerByte=2; codepoint->canonical-byte encoder maxBytesPerChar=1) + META-INF/services/java.nio.charset.spi.CharsetProvider. Charset names: x-petscii-unshifted (aliases petscii, x-petscii), x-petscii-shifted (alias petscii-shifted), x-c64-screencode-unshifted (alias c64-screencode), x-c64-screencode-shifted (screencode charsets may initially be absent until grm-1.4.5's map exists — provider must tolerate a missing resource per-charset). Gradle: stageCharsetResources Copy task data/*.map -> build/generated-resources/retromachines/charset/, wired into sourceSets.main.resources + processResources (buildExtension packs project.jar per buildExtension.gradle:117 — verified, resources will ship). (D) Six fixed-charset AbstractStringDataType subclasses in retromachines/data/ following StringDataType pattern (no-arg ctor, (DataTypeManager) ctor, clone, static dataType singleton; non-null charsetName hardwires charset): PetsciiStringDataType, TerminatedPetsciiStringDataType, PetsciiShiftedStringDataType, TerminatedPetsciiShiftedStringDataType, ScreencodeStringDataType, ScreencodeShiftedStringDataType (screencode fixed-length only). (F) tools/charset/CharsetProviderVerify.java + verifyCharsets JavaExec task (own source set; classpath = main output + staged resources + gson): proves real ServiceLoader SPI in plain JVM; asserts charsets resolve by name+alias, decode == PetsciiMapper.toDisplayUnicode for all bytes x variants, canonical round-trip.
acceptance_criteria: verifyCharsets passes in plain JVM; extension zip contains the services file and staged .map resources; datatypes auto-discovered (headless check in grm-1.4.4).
close_reason: Charset SPI + datatypes landed: RetroCharsetProvider/TableCharset (lazy, failure-swallowing), 6 fixed-charset string datatypes, stageCharsetResources jar wiring (dist-zip verified), verifyCharsets 1037 cases green in plain JVM. Full gate SUITE OK.

title: PETSCII unicode layer: petscii.yaml schema 2, compiler expansion, PetsciiMapper.toDisplayUnicode
description: Phase A of the grm-1.4 plan. Add a unicode: section to machines/generated/petscii.yaml (schema 2): C0/C1 pass-through for controls (codepoint = byte value, user-confirmed), true glyphs for ASCII divergences (0x5C GBP U+00A3, 0x5E U+2191, 0x5F U+2190), full per-variant graphics table (box drawing U+2500s, block elements U+2580s, Symbols for Legacy Computing U+1FB00-FF), mirror rules (0xC0-DF=0x60-7F, 0xE0-FE=0xA0-BE, 0xFF=0x7E) decoding to canonical glyphs, provenance block for the Unicode mapping source. PetsciiCompiler accepts schema 2, emits unicode_variants (2x256 codepoints) + encode (codepoint->canonical byte) into data/petscii.map beside the existing variants: key; escaped-layer output must stay byte-identical (frozen petcat convention; basic-petscii/basic-dialects goldens guard). PetsciiMapper parses the layer, adds toDisplayUnicode(int|byte[], Variant) and loadFromStream(InputStream) (loadFromMapFile refactored onto it). PetsciiMapperVerify extended: unicode completeness 256x2, mirror equivalence, control policy, encoder canonicalization round-trip encode(decode(b))==canonical(b).
acceptance_criteria: verifyPetsciiMapper passes with new unicode checks; full build-and-test.sh check green with byte-identical existing goldens; toDisplayUnicode defined for all 512 byte-variant combos.
close_reason: Unicode layer landed: petscii.yaml schema 2, compiler expansion (escaped layer byte-identical), PetsciiMapper.toDisplayUnicode/encodeUnicode/loadFromStream, verify extended to 4480 cases. Full gate SUITE OK.

title: C64PrgLoader entry/degrade-path regressions from arbitrary load-address rework
description:
From /code-review of codex commit fd17727 (grm-dvx arbitrary PRG load addresses). Five related regressions vs the old fixed-0x0801 loader, all in src/main/java/retromachines/C64PrgLoader.java:

1. ENTRY POINT SILENTLY DROPPED (CONFIRMED, ~line 409): entry creation is gated on entryBlock.isExecute(); a load address landing in a non-executable block (P6510 io-kind at $0000, canExecute=false) gets a label but no external entry point, no function, and no log message. Old loader added them unconditionally. Repro: full-memory-snapshot PRG with load address $0000.

2. 2-BYTE HEADER-ONLY PRG REJECTED (CONFIRMED, ~line 210): findSupportedLoadSpecs minimum went 2 -> 3, so a zero-payload .prg falls through to the raw Binary loader instead of importing with the full C64 map/symbols as before; also makes the prgLength==0 IOException (~272) dead code.

3. STRUCT ACROSS CARVED BOUNDARY (PLAUSIBLE, ~line 556): createCarvedTarget applies the region struct (2-byte R6510) at the region start even when slices split the region into initialized+uninitialized blocks; createData fails (only logged), 6510 port registers left untyped. Repro with shipped map: load $FF00, 0x101 payload (wrap covers only $0000).

4. DEGRADE PATH ABORTS (PLAUSIBLE, ~line 644): when banked-window setup is skipped ('skipping banked-window setup'), window-occupant slices never get a placement space and persistPrgPlacement throws 'No address space was created for PRG target RAM_A000', aborting the import the skip message promised to survive. Sibling: planPrgSlices (~494) NPEs on a map with no windows array — a shape load() explicitly supports. Both need hand-edited/variant maps today (MapCompiler always emits the keys) but the loader's own code claims to support the shapes.

5. PLACEMENT GAPS ABORT IMPORT, NO VALIDATOR (PLAUSIBLE, ~line 532): != 1 placement targets per PRG byte now throws instead of the old log-and-single-block degrade. Shipped c64.yaml is gapless today, but nothing (MapCompiler or CI) validates coverage, so the first map edit that opens a gap breaks every spanning PRG import.

Suggested split if needed: 1+2 are quick behavioral fixes; 3 needs applyStructType to skip/split when the region is carved; 4 wants either upfront validation with a clear error or a real degrade; 5 wants a MapCompiler coverage check.
acceptance_criteria: PRG at $0000 gets an entry point (or an explicit log explaining the drop); 2-byte PRG imports with C64 map again or the rejection is deliberate+documented; wrapped $FF00 import leaves R6510 typed; skipped-window and gap cases either import degraded or fail with a clear validation error, covered by banktest fixtures.
notes: Item #3 (struct across carved boundary) was PLAUSIBLE and does NOT reproduce in Ghidra 12.1.2 -- verified empirically in grm-z15.2 (fixture prgstraddletest): createData spans an init/uninit block boundary fine, so R6510 types correctly at $0000-$0001. Resolved as a guarded non-bug, no code change.
close_reason: All five reviewed regressions resolved across sub-beads z15.1-z15.4: #1 entry point restored (unconditional external entry + gated function mark + log), #2 2-byte PRG accepted again, #3 verified NOT reproducible in 12.1.2 (createData spans a carved block boundary; kept a guard fixture), #4 degrade path made honest (windows NPE guard + up-front clear error), #5 compile-time placement coverage check + declarative prg_placeable flag. Follow-ups: grm-abg (malformed-map harness for #4 runtime coverage), C128 P8502 prg_placeable. Full gate green throughout.

title: AnalyzerRunLog lifecycle: markCompleted fires on failure paths and before the phase-2 follow-on round
description:
From /code-review of codex commits 065577e..fd17727 (commit 837148d, grm-olp quieting). Two confirmed defects in when AnalyzerRunLog.markCompleted is called:

1. FAILURE PATHS CONSUME THE ONE-SHOT VERBOSITY: BoardBankAnalyzer.added() calls markCompleted on the map-load IOException path (~line 228), BoardModel.parse null (~234), and empty-mechanisms (~244); C64BasicAnalyzer does the same on gdt/petscii open failures (~175/185). A transient first-run failure permanently silences the first *successful* run (no 'running', no helper list, no summary) — and AnalyzerRunLog has no reset API.

2. MARKED BEFORE THE FOLLOW-ON FULL ROUND: markCompleted fires at the end of round 1 (~line 337), but the adjacent LAST_COMPLETED comment documents that phase-2 disassembly side effects deliberately trigger a framework re-run 'in full'. That completing round of the same initial analysis runs verbose=false, so the only summary ever logged carries stale round-1 counts.

Fix direction: mark completed only after a successful, fixpoint-reached run (e.g. move the body into doAdded() and mark at the single wrapper exit only when the run did real work and the LAST_COMPLETED fingerprint matches), and consider an AnalyzerRunLog reset when analysis config changes. Also note markCompleted call sites are copy-pasted on ~9 exit paths across the two analyzers — a structural wrapper removes the whole class of miss.
acceptance_criteria: First successful analysis after a failed run logs verbosely; the summary logged reflects the final (fixpoint) round's counts; regression covered by a banktest fixture or unit check.
notes: Implementation staged 2026-07-18: AnalyzerRunLog uses a v2 persisted key so saved Programs polluted by the old failure policy get one clean retry; C64BasicAnalyzer centralizes completion so false/exception/cancellation paths remain initial while successful work/no-ops complete; BoardBankAnalyzer defers summary, cache stamp, and completion until entry/exit function+instruction fingerprints are stable, and no longer completes descriptor/resource/strategy failure paths. Regression additions cover legacy-key migration, failure followed by verbose successful BASIC retry, real banking v2 completion, and the fixpoint predicate. Validation completed: production compileJava PASS; VerifyBankTest.java standalone compilation against Ghidra 12.1.2 jars PASS; diff check PASS; independent final review found lifecycle logic sound. Remaining before closure: run focused c64-banking + basic-petscii and full headless suite. Attempts were blocked before execution by the external-execution account usage limit (resets 2026-07-25), not by a test failure.
close_reason: Completed by follow-on session after in-flight agent hit its session limit. Implementation (staged by that agent, reviewed here): AnalyzerRunLog v2 persisted key (one clean verbose retry for Programs polluted by the old failure policy); C64BasicAnalyzer added()->analyze() wrapper so completion is recorded at a single exit (failures/cancellation/exceptions stay retry-eligible, successful work and no-ops complete); BoardBankAnalyzer defers summary + LAST_COMPLETED stamp + completion until the entry/exit structural fingerprint is stable (reachedFixpoint), so phase-2 changing rounds stay verbose and the one summary carries final counts. Validation: orchestrator + independent subagent review clean; focused c64-banking + basic-petscii chunks PASS (new B5 lifecycle criterion demonstrates failure-stays-incomplete + verbose retry); FULL build-and-test.sh check PASS. Known gap noted: C7/C8 cover banking completion + fixpoint predicate but not a BoardBankAnalyzer-specific failure-retry/legacy-key scenario (B5 covers those only for C64BasicAnalyzer).

title: C64 loader: checkbox options to toggle KERNAL-vars and BASIC-vars symbol sets at import
description: Sub-scope of grm-hnm (user request 2026-07-13). Once c64ref generates the zeropage / page-2 / page-3 KERNAL and BASIC VARIABLE symbol sets, add loader Option CHECKBOXES (boolean options in the C64 import dialog, like the KERNAL/BASIC ROM path options from grm-mbm) to enable/disable applying them, with appropriate defaults. Probably ONE checkbox for the KERNAL variable symbols (zeropage/page2/page3 kernal vars) and ONE for the BASIC variable symbols -- not per-set. DEFAULTS per grm-1.2 rationale: these variable sets default OFF (games reuse those zeropage/low-RAM ranges, so the labels would mislabel game data), while the KERNAL-API set stays ON. Wiring: today the loader only applies symbol sets whose descriptor default==on and silently skips default==off (per DescriptorSupport.applySymbolSet / C64PrgLoader.load ~line 280-289) -- so a checkbox Option must let the user OVERRIDE the descriptor default at import (checked = apply even if default off; unchecked = skip even if default on). Model the boolean Option on NesRomLoader's option pattern; consider CLI args too (like grm-mbm's -loader-<name>). May also want a KERNAL-API-symbols checkbox (default on) for symmetry. Depends on grm-hnm generating the variable sets.
notes:
2026-07-13 SYMBOL SETS SPLIT (prep for the checkboxes): generator now emits THREE low-RAM sets from c64ref src/c64mem PRG guide, bucketed by start addr -- basic-zeropage ($02-$8F, 58), kernal-zeropage ($00-$01 + $90-$FF, 63), page23 ($0100-$03FF pages 1-3 combined, 61). Replaced the old single kernal-zeropage/c64ref-c64mem-zp.yaml. All default off. c64.yaml has 5 sets now: kernal-api (on), kernal-zeropage, basic-zeropage, page23, basic-api (all off). REMAINING for grm-zlj: the actual loader checkbox Options to enable these off-by-default sets at import (change C64PrgLoader.load's default-only gate to default-OR-user-checkbox; add boolean Options like RomFileOption pattern; likely checkboxes for kernal-zeropage, basic-zeropage, page23, basic-api -- and kernal-api on by default).
2026-07-13 IMPLEMENTED + headless-tested (commit pending). Per-set checkbox Options in C64PrgLoader.getDefaultOptions (Boolean, grouped 'Symbol sets', default = descriptor default, -loader-symbols-<set> CLI arg). load() gate uses the checkbox VALUE, NOT OR-ed with the default (per user: option value is authoritative and reflects the default; isDefault only the absent-checkbox fallback). Data-driven from the map's symbols[] -- no hardcoded set names. banktest symtoggle: -loader-symbols-basic-zeropage true applies exactly basic-zeropage (TXTTAB@2B present, no sym@90, CHROUT@FFD2 on); full suite green. REMAINING: GUI verification that the checkboxes render + toggle correctly in the import dialog (manual, like grm-mbm).
close_reason: Implemented, headless-tested, and GUI-verified by the user. C64PrgLoader offers a per-set symbol checkbox (grouped 'Symbol sets') data-driven from the descriptor's symbols[]; the load gate uses the checkbox VALUE (default seeded to the descriptor default; NOT OR-ed), so an unattended import applies descriptor defaults while the user can enable off-by-default sets (kernal-zeropage/basic-zeropage/page23/basic-api) or disable on-by-default kernal-api. -loader-symbols-<set> CLI args for headless. banktest symtoggle green (-loader-symbols-basic-zeropage true applies exactly that set). Symbol data from grm-hnm's c64ref generation (three-way zeropage/page23 split). Commit f2ea0f0.

title: Analyzers: quiet routine logging on re-analysis runs, verbose only on first pass
description: The retromachines analyzers emit routine log output on EVERY added() call -- i.e. every time instructions are (re)disassembled, including manual/incremental disassembly after the initial autoanalysis, not just the first full autoanalyze run. BoardBankAnalyzer is the worst (23 log.appendMsg); C64BasicAnalyzer (8) and others also log per-run summaries. Desired: the first full autoanalyze run may be verbose, but SUBSEQUENT runs should be quiet -- only log messages of Great Importance (genuine warnings/errors), suppressing routine INFO/summary chatter. Approach options: (a) set a marker after the first analysis (a program property / Options flag) and gate routine logging on its absence; (b) detect incremental vs full (added-set size, or whether prior analysis state exists); keep WARNING/error bookmarks always on. Applies to BoardBankAnalyzer + C64BasicAnalyzer + any analyzer with per-run summary logging. Observed by user after the grm-mbm GUI test.
close_reason: Implemented persistent per-analyzer initial-run logging policy. BoardBankAnalyzer now gates six routine progress/summary messages and C64BasicAnalyzer gates its run banner after the initial attempt; all warnings, failures, malformed-input messages, and warning bookmarks remain unconditional. Markers live in Program.ANALYSIS_PROPERTIES and are isolated by concrete analyzer class. compileJava and buildExtension pass against Ghidra 12.1.2.

title: Partition test suite into chunks with subset selection; full suite gates acceptance
description: Split testing into related chunks runnable independently (candidates: c64-banking, nes-banking, basic+petscii, bit-algebra, plus future per-milestone chunks) so active development runs only the relevant subset fast/often. Mechanism: chunk argument or tag filter on run-banktest.sh (and gradle test tags if the JUnit spike lands), with a documented convention mapping source areas -> chunks. HARD RULE: final acceptance and commits still gate on the FULL suite passing — subset runs are a development-loop optimization only. Consider a 'quick' alias (skip slow analyzeHeadless imports where a cached project suffices) and rough timing measurements to prove the speedup.
notes: Implemented chunk selection in run-banktest.sh and build-and-test.sh: c64-banking, c64-loader, c64-recovery, basic-petscii, nes-banking, bit-algebra, and all. Default full gate now includes every headless golden plus verifyPetsciiMapper and verifyBitAlgebra; subsets are documented as development-only. Fixtures generate lazily; bit-algebra alone skips extension build/install; unsupported bless bit-algebra is rejected. No quick/cache alias: fresh-project invalidation is not yet trustworthy. Validation 2026-07-18: bash syntax/CLI checks pass; bit-algebra PASS in 19.5s; c64-banking all 4 goldens PASS in 72.7s; full canonical gate PASS in 140.6s. Relative to full: about 86% and 48% faster respectively on this machine.
close_reason: Implemented and verified chunked development-loop selection with the full suite preserved as the acceptance gate.

title: Self-modifying code strategies: run-from-elsewhere, decrypt-on-the-fly, cross-processor code upload
description: Umbrella for making the extension useful on the self-modifying-code patterns retro software actually uses — an axis Ghidra has traditionally handled poorly (static listing assumes bytes at an address are THE code). Three concrete use-case families (children), plus a cross-cutting question: the Ghidra Debugger's emulator/trace machinery may be leverageable for all of them (execute the copier/decryptor in the p-code emulator, capture the resulting memory image, feed it back into static analysis) — traditionally SMC was hopeless statically, but Debugger-assisted 'run it, then analyze what it produced' changes the economics. Design tension to resolve early: which patterns deserve STATIC modeling (descriptor-driven, like banking) vs EMULATION-ASSISTED recovery vs manual workflow documentation. Relationship to banking engine (grm-5tl): banking changes which pre-existing bytes are visible; SMC creates NEW bytes at analysis time — different problem, but the overlay/alternate-view plumbing and the analyzer-pass architecture are shared infrastructure.
notes: 2026-07-12 grm-1.7.4 survey COMPLETE — design tension RESOLVED, full findings in docs/smc-survey.md. Machinery: EmulatorHelper is @Deprecated(since 12.1, forRemoval=true); all emulation work targets ghidra.pcode.emu.PcodeEmulator + PcodeEmulationCallbacks (readUninitialized = IO fault policy hook, dataWritten = exact dirty-set capture) + EmulatorUtilities.loadProgram (plain-emulator harness, no Trace needed). Interpreted emulator is SMC-safe by construction (SleighInstructionDecoder re-decodes each instruction from live state; avoid JIT emulator for SMC). In-tree precedent: EmuX86DeobfuscateExampleScript. DEBUGGER (per user direction, evaluated first-class): pure-emulation mode + GUI Copy Into Program = the manual/interactive tier (document in grm-fy0); headless Trace round-trip buys nothing over direct Memory.setBytes; TraceRmi retro connector (VICE/Mesen) does not exist and stays NO-GO until demonstrated need — VICE .vsf snapshot import is the cheap 80% (real-hardware-fidelity memory image, zero protocol work). Approach split: 1.7.1 STATIC now; 1.7.2 emulation pilot; 1.7.3 static-first with SPC700 language sourcing as new prerequisite (stock Ghidra has NO SPC700 sleigh — SPCdra is the community candidate). Shared EmulationRecovery harness bead created; reuses the same PcodeEmulationCallbacks layer the banking vision picked for L4 (§7.1) — one callback stack serves both features.

title: State-field packing has no cumulative-width validation (>32 bits silently corrupts)
description: MapCompiler.java:604. parseStateFields accepts each field with bits<=31 but never checks the SUM. packState does packed |= fieldValue << shift; shift += bits. Once cumulative shift >= 32, Java shifts are mod-32 so the field wraps into low bits and packed int corrupts. Failure: two 20-bit fields (sum 40) -> second field overwrites first, wrong initial_state/states.value, no error. Fix: reject total width > 32. Verdict PLAUSIBLE.
notes: Fixed. Added a cumulative-width check in parseStateFields: sum of all banking.state field widths must be <= 31. Refined the bead's '>32' threshold to '>31' via primary-source evidence: BoardBankAnalyzer.java:193 derives the whole-state mask as (1 << stateBitNames.size()) - 1 where stateBitNames has one entry PER BIT, so total==32 gives (1<<32)-1 == 0 (empty mask) in addition to packState's mod-32 shift wrap. Cap at 31 keeps both the packing and the runtime mask correct. Verified: all descriptors+sketches still compile; a sketch with two 20-bit fields (total 40) now fails at build with 'banking.state total width 40 bits exceeds 31'.
close_reason: P2 code-review fixes: truncated-ROM up-front guard + cumulative state-width validation. compileJava + buildExtension + buildMap/validateSketches all green; width gate empirically confirmed.

title: Truncated ROM: vector read past EOF throws uncaught IOException out of load()
description: NesRomLoader.java:345. checkRange validates window offsets against the DECLARED prgSize, never actual file length. A .nes declaring 32KB PRG with a 16KB body passes all gates; the high window block creation fails-and-is-swallowed but is still added to placed; labelVectorTargets then readBytes(fileOffset,2) past EOF -> IOException propagates out of load() (try/finally does not catch it), aborting import with an exception dialog instead of a logged skip. Fix: validate declared PRG against provider length up front, or guard the vector read. Verdict PLAUSIBLE.
notes: Fixed by option (a): validate declared PRG against actual provider length up front, right after InesHeader.parse. If header.prgFileOffset()+header.prgSize() > provider.length(), log 'Truncated iNES image...' and return gracefully. Placed BEFORE any resource allocation (board resolution, gdt open, block creation) so the early return leaks nothing. This is the right-altitude fix: guards the single trusted invariant (declared==actual PRG bytes) once, covering both the swallowed block-creation failures and the previously-unguarded vector read at labelVectorTargets (provider.readBytes past EOF -> IOException out of load() -> exception dialog). No NES headless test harness exists (banktest is C64-only); verified by compile + reasoning.
close_reason: P2 code-review fixes: truncated-ROM up-front guard + cumulative state-width validation. compileJava + buildExtension + buildMap/validateSketches all green; width gate empirically confirmed.

title: MapCompiler accepts maps: keyword offset that the runtime cannot resolve
description: MapCompiler.java:66 (EXPR_KEYWORDS includes offset) vs DescriptorSupport ExprParser.parseFactor (no offset case) and referencedFields (excludes only last/second_last). A descriptor using offset compiles clean but at load time referencedFields returns {offset}, which != the banked field name, so NesRomLoader logs needs exactly one banking.state field and never places the window (or env.get(offset) throws). Valid-looking descriptor -> silently incomplete memory map. Fix: either drop offset from the compiler keyword set or implement it in the runtime. Verdict CONFIRMED.
notes: Fixed by DROPPING offset from the grammar (not implementing it). Rationale: the loader places every computed window as a CONTIGUOUS Ghidra block, so the window-relative CPU offset is added IMPLICITLY by the affine mapping; evalExpr returns one base offset per window/bank with no per-byte term. 'offset' in an expression would double-count (PRG[bank*0x4000+offset]) or be misread as a state field (PRG[offset] -> referencedFields {offset} -> 'unknown state field'). It was also unused by every descriptor. Removed offset from MapCompiler.EXPR_KEYWORDS + its javadoc; synced docs/SCHEMA.md, docs/MAP_FORMAT.md, docs/vision-board-banking.md to state the offset is implicit. Verified: all machines/*.yaml + sketches recompile clean; a sketch using 'offset' now fails at BUILD time ('identifier offset is neither a banking.state field nor one of [second_last, last]') instead of compile-clean/fail-at-load. Runtime (DescriptorSupport.ExprParser) needed no change -- it never claimed offset.
close_reason: Dropped the unimplementable/unused 'offset' keyword; compiler grammar + docs now match the runtime. Build-time rejection verified.

title: Descriptor include/shared-fragment mechanism (NES boards duplicate regions/symbols/types 6x)
description: The six NES board descriptors (nes-nrom + 5 discrete mappers, grm-4iq) copy memory.regions, symbols, types, formats, and validation verbatim because the schema has no include/composition mechanism. Every PPU/APU struct fix must now be applied six times. Add a shared-fragment mechanism to MapCompiler/GdtBuilder (e.g. 'include: nes-common.yaml' resolved at compile time) and de-duplicate. Also revisit: MapCompiler unconditionally requires banking.context_register whenever banking: is present, forcing the NES boards to declare a provisional 'nesbank' register no language declares yet — make it optional or tie the requirement to the bundled-language milestone (grm-bk6).
notes: Implemented compile-time descriptor composition via YamlSupport.loadComposed for machine roots only: relative string/list includes, recursive canonical cycle detection, missing/absolute/type validation, deterministic left-to-right deep map merge, list append, local override, numeric nested-key preservation, deep-copy isolation, and controlled cyclic-alias rejection.
