MapCompiler and GdtBuilder share composition; raw PETSCII/external sources remain unchanged. GdtBuilder validates schema and unique type names before touching the last good GDT. Added verifyDescriptorComposition to buildExtension. Migrated all 10 shipping NES descriptors to machines/fragments/nes-common.yaml (core regions, MMIO symbols, NES_PPU/NES_APU_IO types, iNES format), preserving board-specific regions/windows/banking/validation. Removed fake nesbank from 9 banked descriptors and both sketches; context_register is optional and documented. Validation: composition verifier, buildMap, buildGdt, validateSketches, compileJava PASS; all 10 generated NES maps exactly match pre-change baseline after removing only context_register; all GDTs retain NES_PPU/NES_APU_IO; nes-banking chunk PASS; post-review canonical full suite PASS. Final review found and verified fixes for cyclic YAML aliases and duplicate-type output preservation.
close_reason: Implemented and fully validated shared descriptor composition, NES common-fragment migration, and optional context-register support.

title: Suppress 6502-language default block conflicts (ZERO_PAGE/STACK) in descriptor loaders
description: NES (and likely C64) imports log 'Failed to add language defined memory block due to conflict: ZERO_PAGE/STACK' — the stock 6502 pspec declares default blocks at $0000/$0100 that collide with our descriptor-driven RAM blocks. Cosmetic (import succeeds), but noisy. Options: shouldSetImageBaseOnNewProgram/default-block suppression hook, or name our RAM regions to subsume the pspec blocks. Observed during grm-9ux headless verification (SMB, Pac-Man).
close_reason: Fixed: descriptor loaders (AbstractCbmPrgLoader, NesRomLoader) override createDefaultMemoryBlocks with DescriptorSupport.createDefaultMemoryBlocksQuietly — pspec default blocks that conflict with descriptor memory are skipped silently; overflow/invalid-address failures still log. Full build-and-test.sh check SUITE OK; manual headless NES + C64 PRG imports show zero conflict messages.

title: M2: NES discrete mappers — UxROM/AxROM/CNROM/GxROM/BNROM via memory-latch strategy
description: First NES banking, per docs/vision-board-banking.md M2. Add the memory-latch strategy: store anywhere in a declared range, written value (or field) is the state, optional bus-conflict rule (effective value = written AND ROM byte at target — some discrete boards). Descriptors for UxROM (16K switchable $8000, fixed-last $C000), AxROM (32K $8000), CNROM (PRG fixed; CHR-only banking — near-trivial PRG side), GxROM/BNROM. Overlay-generation L4 (interim): one overlay per bank on the switchable window only — fixed windows are single blocks; no bank-by-window duplication (contrast GhidraNes MMC1Mapper.java:27-45). ACCEPTANCE: on real UNROM titles (Mega Man, Castlevania, Contra, DuckTales), bank-switch stores are detected, cross-bank JSR/JMP auto-resolve to the correct overlay, unknown-state sites get explicit ambiguity markers. GME payoff: nes/megaman + nes/bionic music-driver RE gets bank-aware disassembly.
close_reason: M2 discrete mappers shipped. memory-latch strategy (range store, shift/mask field extraction, bus-conflict AND when target is constant bank-invariant ROM, write-only-latch load resolution) via shared StoredValueScanner extracted from register-write with zero C64 regression (banktest suite byte-identical, 13/13, re-run on final build). Five shipping descriptors: nes-uxrom(2)/cnrom(3)/axrom(7)/gxrom(66)/bnrom(34); nes.yaml renamed nes-nrom.yaml; build.gradle machine tasks now data-driven glob. Loader realizes switchable computed windows home-in-base + <window>_B<v> overlays and records the board in program info; NesBankingAnalyzer reads it. Engine: computed-window retargeting, residence clamp (execution implies mapping), helper-call propagation (const helper state or call-site immediate arg recovery), and disassembly/function kick at cross-bank flow targets. ACCEPTANCE on real ROMs: Mega Man (UNROM) 153 switch annotations, 1507 cross-bank JSR/JMP refs primary into PRG_LO_B4/B5/B6, 7435 instructions disassembled inside bank overlays (13337 total vs 353 without banking), helper FUN_dc21 unrecoverable-arg site gets explicit WARNING. Castlevania: helper JSR sites detected with honest ambiguity markers (bank arg loaded from memory variable - stage-driven, statically unresolvable). W&W (AxROM): single 32K window, home+B1-B3, vectors from switchable home, 17 switches incl 'bank -> 2 via FUN_ff69'. Contra imports clean but stalls at 717 instrs (indirect-jump dispatch, generic coverage limit). DuckTales absent from ROM collection. Deviation: descriptors carry provisional context_register nesbank (MapCompiler requires it; dormant until grm-bk6). Follow-up filed: grm-5zg (descriptor include mechanism + optional context_register). Unblocks grm-6a7/grm-hsv (M3).

title: M2: extract BoardBankAnalyzer + strategy library (register-write) from C64BankingAnalyzer
description: Split C64BankingAnalyzer into (a) a machine-independent BoardBankAnalyzer engine — CFG worklist dataflow, per-bit partial-knowledge state (migrate PortState toward RegisterValue, which it reimplements), agree-bit merges, call-clobber rules, initial-state defaults, context stamping via ProgramContext.setRegisterValue, switch-site comments/bookmarks — and (b) a strategy library discovered via ClassSearcher, starting with register-write (fixed-address store; masked-RMW backward-scan value recovery already built and verified). Strategy interface owns: candidate-write recognition, value recovery (delegating to shared dataflow), state-field update emission with per-bit confidence. Configuration comes entirely from the schema-v2 descriptor (banking.mechanisms). ACCEPTANCE: C64 banktest/banktest2 headless suites pass unchanged (zero regression) with the C64 path running through the generic engine + register-write strategy. See docs/vision-board-banking.md section 6 (L2).
close_reason: BoardBankAnalyzer engine + strategy library extracted; ZERO REGRESSION proven by the new committed banktest suite (tools/banktest: 13 criteria + golden behavior dumps blessed against the pre-refactor analyzer, byte-identical after). Engine (BoardBankAnalyzer, abstract): CFG worklist dataflow, BankState per-bit value+mask (PortState renamed/promoted; RegisterValue's model on ints — full RegisterValue binding blocked on grm-bk6's context register, documented), agree-bit merges, initial-state defaults, effective-state fallback, switch-site EOL comments w/ known/assumed provenance, WARNING bookmarks only when zero bits known, overlay reference retargeting incl on_write, and ProgramContext.setValue context stamping that engages only when the language declares banking.context_register (dormant until grm-bk6 — stock 6502 has none). Strategies: BankSwitchStrategy ExtensionPoint (data/ExtensionPoint.manifest suffix; ClassSearcher discovery, fresh instance per mechanisms[] entry, configured from params) + RegisterWriteBankSwitchStrategy owning the verified masked-RMW backward scan. C64BankingAnalyzer is now ~60 lines: loader gate + map path + name (bookmark category preserved via getSimpleName). Documented deviation: WARNING bookmark message TEXT generalized (was register-write-specific prose); location/presence unchanged, dumps unaffected. Suite: tools/banktest/run-banktest.sh check|bless. Unblocks grm-4iq (memory-latch tier).

title: M1: iNES loader + board registry + NROM baseline (nes.yaml)
description: NES entry point per docs/vision-board-banking.md M1: iNES header parsing (mapper number, PRG/CHR sizes, trainer), board-descriptor registry keyed by mapper number with user override as a loader Option (pattern: Loader.getDefaultOptions, Loader.java:176 — board choice rides alongside the language pair, no LoadSpec changes), nes.yaml descriptor in schema v2. NROM end-to-end first: fixed PRG mapping (16K mirrored or 32K), CPU-space MMIO regions with PPU/APU/controller register types+symbols, vectors labeled and disassembled. CHR stays out of CPU space (GhidraNes parks it at $0000 in CPU space — known-wrong precedent, see NesMapper.java:161-203). No banking yet; this proves the loader stack is system-neutral. GME payoff: nes/smb (NROM) becomes the first Ghidra-navigable GME music target.
close_reason: iNES loader + board registry + NROM baseline shipped, verified end-to-end headless vs ghidra 12.1.2. machines/nes.yaml (schema v2): PPU/APU register structs (NESdev-checked), nes-mmio symbol set, vector slots, physical PRG + computed windows PRG[0]/PRG[last] — the last expression handles NROM-128 mirroring AND NROM-256 with zero special-casing. NesRomLoader: iNES header parse (magic/PRG/CHR/mapper/trainer), constant maps:-expression evaluator (ints, last, second_last, arith; state-field exprs deferred to bank engine), NES Board import option; NesBoardRegistry scans bundled machines/*.map for system.board.ines_mappers (data-driven: new boards = new descriptors, no Java). Loader stack proven system-neutral: descriptor interpretation extracted from C64PrgLoader into DescriptorSupport (regions/perms/volatile/subregions/types/symbols), C64 loader delegates, compiles green. VERIFIED: SMB (NROM-256) — correct blocks/perms, MMIO labels, typed vectors, NMI/RESET/IRQ functions, 1066 instructions from canonical reset; Pac-Man (NROM-128) — mirror windows placed, vectors resolve, $FF00 reset disassembled. CHR deliberately not loaded (PPU space deferred per vision §5.4). Follow-up filed for cosmetic ZERO_PAGE/STACK pspec-block conflict messages. Unblocks grm-4iq. GME payoff: nes/smb is now Ghidra-navigable.

title: M1: descriptor schema v2 — state tuples, mechanisms list, physical spaces, computed occupants, mode layouts
description: Generalize the board descriptor schema (SCHEMA.md / machines/c64.yaml) per docs/vision-board-banking.md section 5: (a) banking.state becomes a named tuple of fields mapping onto context-register sub-fields (RegisterValue per-bit partial knowledge); (b) banking.mechanism becomes mechanisms[] list, each a strategy instance with params and the state fields it feeds; (c) physical: spaces backing ROM images laid out once, with windows mapping into them via a deliberately tiny expression language (state fields, integer arithmetic, last/second_last, window-relative offset); (d) mode-dependent layouts[] selected by state fields (MMC1/MMC3 PRG modes). Enumerated occupants + truth-table states (C64 style) remain first-class. ACCEPTANCE: c64.yaml expressed in v2 regenerates the current .map/.gdt byte-identically (or with documented, reviewed diffs); MapCompiler + SCHEMA.md/MAP_FORMAT.md updated; UxROM and MMC3 sketches from the vision doc validate against the schema.
close_reason: Schema v2 shipped. (a) banking.state = named field tuple ({name,bits}, first field = bit 0); (b) banking.mechanisms[] = strategy instances with opaque params + sets validation; (c) top-level physical[] spaces + window maps: 'SPACE[expr]' with compile-time-validated mini-expression language (ints, state fields, last/second_last/offset, + - *, parens); (d) memory.layouts[] mode-dependent window sets keyed by when:{field:value}. ACCEPTANCE: c64.map regenerates byte-identical except one reviewed 36-line banking hunk (state_bits->state, mechanism->mechanisms) documented in MAP_FORMAT.md; .gdt unaffected (GdtBuilder reads only types:); C64BankingAnalyzer updated to v2 keys, full buildExtension green vs ghidra 12.1.2; UxROM+MMC3 sketches (machines/sketches/) compile via new validateSketches gradle task. Note: maps: values must be quoted inside YAML flow mappings ([ is a flow indicator) — documented in SCHEMA.md; vision doc examples show the unquoted aspirational form.

title: Board-level banking engine: machine-independent four-layer roadmap
description: Umbrella for the design vision recorded in docs/vision-board-banking.md (v1, 2026-07-07): first-class, data-driven board-level banking — four layers (L1 optional CPU-assist register; L2 strategy-driven write detection + value recovery; L3 pure-data interpretation; L4 application via context register + resolution hook, overlays as interim ceiling). Stepping stones: C64 (M0, shipped) -> schema v2 + NES NROM (M1) -> strategy library + discrete mappers (M2) -> MMC1/MMC3 protocol strategies + bank-placement inference (M3) -> MMC5 + GB MBC machine-independence proof (M4) -> core hook integration gated on RFC #9349 signal (M5). Guiding principles in the doc, notably: analysis over interrogation (infer bank placement from flows, never ask upfront — retire the GhidraNes per-bank combo-box pattern) and physical-space backing with windowed views (no bank-by-window block explosion). Related: grm-bk6/grm-wkk (C64 L1/L2 upgrades, parallel track); GME bead gib.2 (upstream engagement).

title: Bundle 6510 sleigh language (PORT register + c64bank context fields)
description:
Bundle a 6510 language variant with the extension (precedent: grue74/ghidra-c64helpers), replacing the fallback_language 6502:LE:16:default used today (c64.yaml cpu.language already names 6510:LE:16:default).

Contents beyond stock 6502:
- PORT register modeling the on-die $00/$01 port; specialized zp constructors (operand==$01, and ==$00 for DDR) route LDA/STA/etc through the register instead of memory — makes bank-switch idioms ordinary register dataflow (see grm-wkk for why).
- c64bank context register with three 1-bit fields LORAM/HIRAM/CHAREN (TMode-style; RegisterValue gives per-bit partial knowledge for free).
- Consider undocumented/illegal opcodes while in there (games use them).

Keep decode otherwise identical to stock 6502. Loader stops passing fallback_language once bundled.
notes: 2026-07-07 DESIGN CORRECTION (user): on-die-ness places only the mechanism REGISTER, never banking semantics — the PLA wiring of port bits to LOROM/HIROM/CHAREN is external, C64-board-specific. Counterexample: 6510T in the 1551 drive has the identical port wired to drive-control signals. Therefore the 6510 language must be SYSTEM-NEUTRAL: define PORT as an anonymous 8-bit on-die register routed from $00/$01 accesses; NO LORAM/HIRAM/CHAREN naming, no c64bank truth-table knowledge in the slaspec. Per-system bit naming, if wanted, goes in a per-system pspec variant via register alias (ARM precedent: ARMt.pspec 'TB alias ISAModeSwitch') or stays entirely analyzer/descriptor-side.
close_reason: Bundled 6510 sleigh language shipped. data/languages/6510.{slaspec,ldefs,pspec,cspec} + sleighArgs.txt; build.gradle sleighCompile task (ghidra.pcodeCPort.slgh_compile.SleighCompile, SoftwareModeling/Generic/Utility lib classpath, -a) wired into buildExtension; compiled .sla gitignored (build artifact) + packaged. LANGUAGE: 6502 decode/semantics byte-identical PLUS on-die PORTDDR($00)/PORT($01) registers; specialized zero-page constructors (OP1/OP2, inherited by OP2LD/OP2ST) route DIRECT $00/$01 accesses through the registers so STA $01 -> PORT = A is register dataflow (verified via pcode probe: results=[PORT] inputs=[A]); indexed ($01,X) stays memory. SYSTEM-NEUTRAL per the 2026-07-07 design correction: port named anonymously, NO LORAM/HIRAM/CHAREN, NO c64bank context register in the slaspec (bank meaning is board wiring, not CPU arch). Two sleigh gotchas solved+documented: (1) unquoted register-name display token is parsed as an operand ref and breaks export-size inference -> quote it ("PORT"); (2) dynamic *[register] export compiles to a STORE-via-pointer (results empty) not a clean register write -> static export PORT is required and works (coexists with the tables' memory exports like stock OP2:A). LOADER: DescriptorSupport.resolveLanguageId reads system.language, verifies availability, falls back to 6502 only if unavailable; C64PrgLoader uses it; fallback_language removed from c64.yaml (loader stops passing it, per acceptance). ANALYZER kept green without the grm-wkk propagator refactor: register-write mechanism gained optional 'register' param (c64.yaml: register: PORT); StoredValueScanner.writesRegister/readsRegister detect the on-die register via getResultObjects/getInputObjects; strategy ORs address|register so 6510 (register) and the 6502 fallback (address) both work. ZERO REGRESSION: C64 banktest suite 13/13 PASS and both dumps BYTE-IDENTICAL to goldens under the 6510 language; NES Mega Man byte-identical (153 switches/1507 cross-bank refs/13337 instrs) confirming the shared StoredValueScanner change is safe. Clean-from-scratch gradle build green; zip packages the language. Illegal/undocumented opcodes DEFERRED to grm-azg (not a pure win -- defining them makes data bytes decode as instructions, hurting code/data separation; needs an opt-in-variant design decision). context_register kept as c64bank in c64.yaml (MapCompiler still requires the field; making it optional is grm-5zg) but documented as the not-yet-realized application-layer channel; stampContextRegister stays dormant. Unblocks grm-wkk (TMode-style propagator refactor now has its PORT register).

title: Phase 0 bank-aware analyzer: flow-track bank state, retarget refs into overlay banks
description: The gib.2 Phase 0 interim (RFC docs/rfc-banked-memory.md): a Ghidra analyzer that (a) tracks C64 bank state along control flow from banking.initial_state, updating at determinable writes to the banking mechanism address ($0001, from banking.mechanism in the descriptor — which MapCompiler must now emit into c64.map, currently dropped); (b) for instruction operands targeting a banked window, when the effective occupant for the access differs from the base-space home block, adds an explicit primary reference into that occupant's overlay space (legal today: ReferenceDBManager.addMemoryReference has no same-space constraint). Includes write-under-ROM: WRITE accesses route via the occupant's on_write (STA $A000 with BASIC banked in -> RAM_A000::a000 even in the default state). Data-driven from c64.map; no hardcoded C64 facts beyond schema. Unknown/conflicting state -> leave defaults + bookmark. Demonstrates demand for the upstream RFC and gives correct cross-bank xrefs today.
design: Bank-state tracking: simple forward dataflow over the CFG (worklist; per-block in/out state; merge conflict -> unknown), NOT SymbolicPropogator — transparent and sufficient for the LDA #imm/STA $01 idiom; stored value from immediate-load lookback within the block (A/X/Y). state = value & mechanism.mask; occupants from banking.states. Refs: addMemoryReference(instr, overlayAddr, refType, SourceType.ANALYSIS, opIndex) + setPrimary; skip when effective occupant == home AND access is not a rom write-under. EOL comment or bookmark at bank-switch instructions showing the new state. Gate canAnalyze on executable format == C64 PRG loader name. Extend synthetic test PRG with a state-5 section + state-7 write-under-ROM to verify.
close_reason: Implemented + independently re-verified headless (Ghidra 12.1.2). C64BankingAnalyzer (AbstractAnalyzer, INSTRUCTION_ANALYZER, priority REFERENCE_ANALYSIS.after(), gated on executableFormat == loader name): forward dataflow to fixpoint (known->conflict->UNKNOWN lattice) from entry/function seeds at banking.initial_state; bank switches recognized via WRITE ref to banking.mechanism.address with backward immediate-load scan (LDA/LDX/LDY #imm, block-bounded, clobber-aware); refs into banked windows retargeted to the state occupant's overlay (reads/exec) or its on_write occupant (writes — incl. write-under-ROM in the HOME state), SourceType.ANALYSIS, set primary, default demoted; EOL 'bank -> N (...)' comments; WARNING bookmark on undeterminable switch; idempotent. MapCompiler now emits banking.mechanism (was dropped); MAP_FORMAT.md updated. Verified: LDA $A000@state5 -> RAM_A000::a000 READ primary; STA $E000@state5 -> RAM_E000::e000 WRITE; STA $A000@state7 -> RAM_A000::a000 WRITE (write-under-ROM); JSR $FFD2 untouched. Subagent-found API gotcha: CodeUnit.getScalar(0) returns null for bare immediates — pull Scalar from getOpObjects instead.

title: C64 PRG loader (6502): overlays, IO struct annotation, KERNAL symbols; consume .gdt+.map
description: The grm-1.3 POC loader. Ghidra 12.x AbstractProgramWrapperLoader (class name MUST end 'Loader'): override load(Program, ImporterSettings); findSupportedLoadSpecs returns one LoadSpec w/ LanguageCompilerSpecPair(6502:LE:16:default,default), gated on .prg extension / valid 2-byte load-addr header. In load(): read 2-byte LE load address, place PRG bytes; read bundled c64.map (gson) + c64.gdt (FileDataTypeManager.openFileArchive); create region MemoryBlocks; create per-bank OVERLAY blocks (MemoryBlockUtils.createInitializedBlock/createUninitializedBlock isOverlay=true, distinct block name per occupant -> distinct overlay space); apply IO structs from .gdt at subregion addresses (program.getDataTypeManager().resolve + DataUtilities.createData CLEAR_ALL_UNDEFINED_CONFLICT_DATA); apply inline symbols (SymbolTable.createLabel IMPORTED + addExternalEntryPoint; KERNAL entry stubs via AbstractProgramLoader.markAsFunction); set entry point at load address. Defer 6510 language + c64bank context register + flow-tracked banking (separate bead). Locate bundled resources via Application.findDataFileInAnyModule.
design: MEMORY LAYOUT (corrected per user 2026-07-04 — references must resolve in the BASE space): Do NOT make all window occupants overlays; that reproduces the #6651 dangling-reference bug (JSR $FFD2 resolves in base space, so labels in overlay spaces are never consulted). Instead: the occupant selected by banking.initial_state (C64 state 7 = BASIC/IO/KERNAL) is the HOME block in the BASE (default) space; only the ALTERNATE occupants become overlay spaces. Base space = 7 always-visible regions ($0000-$9FFF, $C000-$CFFF) + PRG (initialized, split RAM_MAIN around it) + window HOME blocks: BASIC@$A000 (empty ROM slot R+X), IO@$D000 (apply VIC/SID/CIA .gdt structs + color RAM + IO1/IO2), KERNAL@$E000 (empty ROM slot R+X). Overlays (own spaces, same nominal addr): RAM_A000, RAM_D000, CHARGEN, RAM_E000. CONSEQUENCE: KERNAL symbols (CHROUT@$FFD2 etc.) and IO structs are applied in the BASE space home block, so refs from PRG code resolve NOW without gib.2. Residual (refs INTO alternate/overlay banks) is the gib.2 problem — POC creates overlay blocks + labels but does NOT wire cross-refs into them; a future overlay-aware labelling/analyzer pass (or gib.2) attaches those. Program entry point = PRG load address (base space).
notes: REOPENED for code-review fixes (2026-07-04): (1) RAM regions were read-only (write flag passed as isIo) — centralize r/w/x into canWrite(kind)/canExecute(kind): RAM=r+w+x, ROM=r+x, IO=r+w, applied at all block-creation sites (fixes the ad-hoc drift across createRegionBlock/createRamMainSplit/createWindowOccupant/createIoSubregions). (2) RAM_MAIN split produced two blocks both named RAM_MAIN — give the carved halves distinct address-suffixed names (aligned w/ stock BinaryLoader: separate blocks are normal; join() can't merge FileBytes-initialized PRG with uninitialized RAM). (3) drop unused regionsByName param from createRegionBlock/createPrgBlock.
close_reason: Review fixes applied + re-verified headless (Ghidra 12.1.2). #1 RAM now writable (centralized canWrite/canExecute: RAM=r+w+x, ROM=r+x, IO=r+w — consistent across all 4 block-creation sites, base & overlay); #2 split halves distinctly named RAM_MAIN_0800/RAM_MAIN_0807 (aligned w/ stock BinaryLoader; join() can't merge init+uninit); #3 dead regionsByName param removed. Re-smoke confirms all RAM blocks w=true, IO w=true/x=false, ROM w=false/x=true, distinct names, CHROUT Function@ffd2, entry@0801, IO structs applied, Import succeeded.

title: Build-time map compiler: c64.yaml -> c64.map JSON; bundle .gdt+.map into extension data/
description: Runtime loader (grm-1.3.2) needs the C64 memory map without a YAML parser. Add a build-time compiler (MapCompiler, in the existing build-only gdtBuilder source set) that reads machines/c64.yaml and emits a c64.map JSON resource (regions, windows/occupants/subregions, banking states, inline symbols). JSON chosen because Ghidra bundles gson (Framework/Generic/lib/gson-2.13.2.jar) so the runtime loader parses it with ZERO shipped dependency. Also redirect the grm-1.5 .gdt output and the new .map into a bundled data dir (data/machines/) and make buildExtension package them, so both artifacts ship in the extension zip. Both are generated build artifacts: gitignore them, never commit.
design: c64.map JSON schema (contract with grm-1.3.2): { system:{id,name,language}, regions:[{name,start,end,kind,type?,comment?}], windows:[{name,start,end,occupants:[{name,kind,image?,on_write?,subregions?:[{name,start,end?,size?,repeat_to?,kind?,type?,comment?}]}]}], banking:{initial_state,context_register,state_bits,states:[{value,:,...}]}, rom_images:{:{size,occupant}}, symbols:[{set,default(bool),region?,entries:[{addr,name,kind,comment?}]}] }. Addresses as decimal JSON numbers. Compiler emits INLINE symbol entries only (source: sets not yet generated). Passes repeat_to through (loader decides mirror policy). Output data/machines/c64.gdt + c64.map; buildExtension.dependsOn buildGdt+buildMap (attach lazily). Document the schema in docs/MAP_FORMAT.md.
close_reason: Build-time map compiler complete + verified: gradle buildExtension alone bundles data/machines/c64.gdt + c64.map; c64.map matches frozen schema (7 regions, 3 windows w/ IO subregion types+repeat_to, 8 banking states, kernal-api inline symbols); snakeyaml stays build-only. Commit 872c669.

title: Generalized string detection: PETSCII + per-game tile-table text mappings
description:
Future feature: extend string detection beyond ASCII for retro systems.
- C64: PETSCII (KERNAL/CHROUT strings) AND screen codes (direct screen-RAM writes) — two DIFFERENT mappings, each with shifted/unshifted charset variants. Prior art: PETSCII visualizer in grue74/ghidra-c64helpers fork (inspect for reuse ideas).
- NES/SNES: per-game tile->character mappings, published as .tbl 'table files' by the ROM-hacking/translation community (romhacking.net, Data Crystal) — a de-facto standard format we could ingest directly, giving per-game string detection from community-documented data.
Integration points to investigate: Ghidra string data types support pluggable Java Charsets (extension could register PETSCII charsets); string-search analyzer charset hooks; descriptor schema could reference charset/table per system or per game.
Fits the descriptor-driven vision: text encoding is system knowledge (or game knowledge, for tile tables) that belongs in data, not code.
notes: DESIGN INPUT (user, 2026-07-11): the CBM BASIC detokenizing analyzer (grm-odt.1, epic grm-1.6) now DEPENDS ON this bead and is its first concrete consumer — its needs must inform this design, not be retrofitted. Requirements from that consumer: (1) a Java-callable byte->display-string mapping API for PETSCII usable OUTSIDE Ghidra's charset/string-search machinery — the detokenizer builds EOL comment text programmatically (string literals inside quotes, raw REM text) and cannot go through StringDataInstance; (2) both PETSCII variants (shifted/unshifted) selectable per call site; screen codes are a SEPARATE mapping (direct screen-RAM writes) the detokenizer does NOT need — do not conflate; (3) control/graphics bytes ($00-$1F, $80-$FF inside quotes) need a printable escaped rendering convention (e.g. {CLR}, {RVS ON}, {c-A}) — pick one, document it, and keep it stable since it lands in golden test dumps; (4) the mapping data should be data-driven (descriptor/shared data file) per project convention, and shared with any future Ghidra charset registration rather than duplicated. Suggested shape: a small PetsciiMapper (or CharsetTable) class + data file, with Ghidra Charset registration layered on top later for string search. The NES/SNES .tbl half of this bead is unaffected by the BASIC consumer but should share the table-data plumbing where natural.
close_reason: All 5 children complete: PetsciiMapper escaped layer (.1), unicode layer schema 2 (.2), charset SPI + 4 JVM charsets + 6 fixed-charset string datatypes + verifyCharsets (.3), descriptor-gated PetsciiStringAnalyzer + system.text key + petscii-strings fixture (.4), screen-code permutation family (.5). PETSCII and screen-code strings are now first-class in Ghidra: charset dropdown, datatypes, and auto-analysis string search, all descriptor-driven and gate-verified. The NES/SNES .tbl half was split out to grm-pqk by user decision (dynamic per-game tables cannot be JVM charsets); grm-td4 (typing BASIC text runs) is unblocked by the new datatypes.

title: POC: C64 loader that maps banked RAM/ROM, IO ports, and PRG load address
description: Implement a minimal proof-of-concept Ghidra loader for the Commodore 64 that (a) reads a PRG file's 2-byte load-address header and places code correctly, (b) maps the banked memory layout — RAM under KERNAL/BASIC/CHARGEN, plus the IO region — using Ghidra overlay address spaces to represent the overlapping banks selectable via the $00/$01 processor port, (c) annotates IO chip registers (VIC-II, SID, CIA1, CIA2, color RAM), (d) applies initial struct/label definitions for known hardware registers. Validates that the system descriptor design (gib.1.2) is sufficient to drive real C64 analysis. Open question to resolve in design: how faithfully to model banking given Ghidra's static memory model.
notes: DESIGN (2026-07-03, decided w/ user): (1) Descriptor delivery = COMPILE MAP AT BUILD TIME. Build tooling emits c64.gdt (types, existing) PLUS c64.map (regions/windows/banking/symbols) as bundled extension data resources; the runtime loader reads BOTH via non-YAML means (no snakeyaml in shipped extension). (2) POC language = stock 6502:LE:16:default; defer bundling 6510 + c64bank context register + flow-tracked bank state to a later bead (gib.2 track). Banking already decided = overlay address spaces. LOADER API (Ghidra 12.x, source-verified): override load(Program, ImporterSettings) on AbstractProgramWrapperLoader (NOT the classic 6-arg load); findSupportedLoadSpecs returns one LoadSpec w/ LanguageCompilerSpecPair(6502:LE:16:default,default); class name MUST end in 'Loader'. Overlays: MemoryBlockUtils.createInitializedBlock(...,isOverlay=true) once per bank, distinct block name per bank -> distinct overlay space (BASIC_ROM:a000). Bundled .gdt: Application.findDataFileInAnyModule('c64.gdt') -> FileDataTypeManager.openFileArchive(f,false); apply via program.getDataTypeManager().resolve(dt,DEFAULT_HANDLER) + DataUtilities.createData(...,CLEAR_ALL_UNDEFINED_CONFLICT_DATA). Symbols: SymbolTable.createLabel(addr,name,IMPORTED)+addExternalEntryPoint; KERNAL stubs via AbstractProgramLoader.markAsFunction(prog,name,addr). Decomposition: grm-1.3.1 build-time map compiler+bundling; grm-1.3.2 the 6502 PRG loader.
close_reason: POC complete + headless-verified (Ghidra 12.1.2). Both children done: grm-0xt (build-time c64.map compiler + .gdt/.map bundling) and grm-974 (6502 PRG loader). Acceptance (a) PRG 2-byte load-addr header read + code placed, (b) banked layout mapped, (c) IO chip registers annotated (VIC/SID/CIA/color RAM via .gdt structs), (d) struct+label defs applied — ALL verified. DESIGN REFINEMENT vs original description: original said 'use overlay spaces to represent overlapping banks'; we improved to HOME-IN-BASE (occupant selected by initial bank state = home block in BASE space; only ALTERNATES become overlays) because pure-overlay banks reproduce the #6651 dangling-reference bug — base-space code (JSR $FFD2) never consults overlay labels. Result: default bank config fully cross-referenced today (CHROUT Function@base:ffd2), pre-gib.2. Descriptor design (gib.1.2) validated as sufficient to drive real C64 analysis. Residual = refs INTO alternate/overlay banks (gib.2 context-aware resolution).

title: Game System Architecture Loader
description:
Root epic for ghidra-retro-machines: a descriptor-driven Ghidra loader extension that sets up complete retro system architectures — memory maps, banked windows (mechanism + initial state), IO chip register structs, copyright-safe ROM slots, symbol sets — from per-machine YAML descriptors (machines/*.yaml). Initial target: Commodore 64. Design docs: docs/SURVEY.md (founding survey), docs/SCHEMA.md (descriptor schema).

LINEAGE: incubated in CBongo/game-music-extraction as beads epic gib.1 (children gib.1.1-gib.1.5 = grm-1.1-grm-1.5); migrated here at repo-birth 2026-07-03. Related work still tracked in GME: gib.2 (Ghidra core banked-memory upstream proposal), gib.3 (Ghidra MCP tooling).
notes:
ARCHITECTURE DECISIONS (user, 2026-07-03):
1. MVP input format: PRG (2-byte load address header).
2. Banking: overlay address spaces for MVP — best Ghidra can do today. IO region always needed by music code; BASIC/KERNAL/CHARGEN rarely needed by music code itself but frequently involved in the LOADER code paths (esp. KERNAL). Long-term: improving Ghidra core banked-memory support is a stated motivation of this whole effort — see bead game-music-extraction-gib.2.
3. ROMs (copyright): symbol-only labels by default (e.g. KERNAL entry points); reserve labeled memory-map slots so users can pull their own ROM dumps in via File > Add To Program; optional loader ROM-path options possible later.
4. Schema: evolving descriptor schema from day one, NOT hardcode-C64-first. Solo development until project is more baked; collaborators later.
5. Build-vs-contribute still open pending RetroGhidra survey (gib.1.1).
REPO NAME DECIDED (user, 2026-07-03): ghidra-retro-machines. Verified collision-free on GitHub (no exact match; no confusable neighbor in the Ghidra/RE space). Pitch: 'give Ghidra the whole machine, not just the file' — descriptor-driven system architecture loaders for retro computers and consoles. Layout affordance: machines/c64.yaml, machines/nes.yaml. Repo-birth trigger reached: gib.1.5 (.gdt build pipeline) is the first extension code; at repo creation, migrate this epic's subtree per the MIGRATION NOTE above and move GME's ghidra/ design docs (SURVEY.md, SCHEMA.md, descriptors/) into the new repo.

title: NES 2.0 exponent PRG-size form is unmodeled: window placement is wrong, and identity declines to key
description:
InesHeader.parse (NesRomLoader.java:127-134) does not model NES 2.0's exponent PRG-size form -- when h[9]'s low nibble is 0xF, the PRG-ROM size is 2^exponent * (multiplier*2+1) rather than a linear 16K unit count, and parse falls back to the low byte h[4] alone.

CONSEQUENCE 1 (the larger bug, pre-existing): prgSize() is then a guess, so window placement, the truncation guard and the $FFFA-$FFFF vector read all operate on wrong bounds for such an image.

CONSEQUENCE 2 (surfaced by grm-hb6.1): NesRomLoader.gameIdentity() declines to emit a per-game identity for these files, because the PRG slice bounds are unreliable and a wrong 64-hex key is invisible where an absent one is diagnosable. The header now carries a boolean exponentPrgSize component recording the fallback, and that is currently its only consumer.

Fixing this changes prgSize(), hence window placement, hence the nes-banking goldens -- which is exactly why it was held out of grm-hb6.1. Real-world incidence is low (the form exists for oversized homebrew/multicarts), so this is worth doing when a real image demands it rather than speculatively.

Acceptance: decode the exponent form in parse; drop the exponentPrgSize decline in gameIdentity() (or keep it only for genuinely unparseable headers); add a Tier-1 case to NesGameIdentityTest asserting an exponent-form image now yields an identity over the correct slice.

title: Copy loops that look in-place but cross occupants: LDA $A000,Y / STA $A000,Y is a real copy
description:
Fenced out of grm-9a0 (2026-07-31) deliberately, so the source-resolution change stayed reviewable.

CopyLoopAnalyzer.tryRecognize rejects a loop whose load and store share a base:

    if (src.equals(dst) || !idx.equals(staIdx)) return null;

That test runs on BASE-SPACE addresses, before either side is re-homed, and the comment above the resolution block says why: re-homing first would make 'src != dst' trivially true.

But on a banked machine the shared-base case is NOT always in-place. The canonical C64 idiom

    LDA $A000,Y ; reads the BASIC ROM (LOROM home occupant)
    STA $A000,Y ; writes RAM_A000  (on_write, since you cannot write to ROM)

is a genuine ROM->RAM-under-ROM copy that the recognizer currently discards as an in-place decrypt. Same shape at $E000 for the KERNAL. These are among the most common boot routines on the platform.

grm-9a0 built exactly the machinery needed to tell the two apart: LoopIdioms.overlayAccessTarget(lda, src, len, RefType::isRead) and (sta, dst, len, RefType::isWrite) resolve to DIFFERENT occupants for a cross-occupant copy and to the SAME one for a true in-place transform. So the test could become 'reject only when the RESOLVED addresses are equal'.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE HERE. Loosening that early return changes which loops the recognizer claims at all, and CopyLoopAnalyzer shares LoopIdioms with C64DecryptLoopAnalyzer -- an in-place decrypt is the shape being admitted. Wanted its own bead, its own fixture, and its own look at the decrypt path rather than riding along on a source-resolution change.

NEEDS: a fixture (mkcopytest.py copybankedinplace.prg) pinning LORAM=0 or reading BASIC with the dump supplied, plus a check that no existing decrypt fixture starts being claimed as a copy.

REFS: CopyLoopAnalyzer.java:167 (the early return), :205-225 (the resolution block and its ordering comment), docs/smc-runfromelsewhere-design.md section 8.

title: DB3 (Bandai FCG): no PRG-register write exists in disassembled code; stub is RAM-resident
description:
Split from grm-2yx after BankReachProbe measurement (2026-07-31). Distinct root cause from Contra's, which turned out to be grm-3x1 (a writesInRange detection bug).

MEASUREMENT: db3 has exactly ONE store in disassembled code whose operand targets the latch range, and it is a correct rejection --
  sites.total 1, sites.abs 1, sites.indexed 0, sites.withWriteRef 1, sites.wouldMatchToday 0, decode=MISS
decode=MISS against addr_mask 0xF / addr_match 0x8 means it is a sibling CHR/IRQ register write, NOT the PRG bank register. So there is NO PRG-register write anywhere in DB3's disassembled code. Nothing for detection to find, and nothing grm-3x1 will fix.

CORROBORATION: db3's three CopyLoopAnalyzer warnings 'copy-shaped loop RAM:e7d4|e826|e7fd -> RAM:0200 could not be bounded; not applied' at e69e/e707/e712 (grm-7pp) say the FCG bank-switch stub is copied to RAM $0200 and executed there. Its ROM image is never disassembled.

TWO ROUTES, both valid:
(a) AUTOMATED -- bound the copy loop, materialize the transfer, disassemble the RAM stub. This is RunFromElsewhere/TransferMaterializer territory; blocked behind epic grm-1.7 and grm-7pp.
(b) HINTED -- a per-game descriptor (grm-hb6) names the switch site directly. Consumed as a dataflow seed with disassemble-first (grm-hb6.4), which is exactly the case (ii) the seeding rule was designed for. Resolvable WITHOUT waiting on grm-1.7.

DB3 is therefore the per-game tier's first real customer and a good acceptance target for grm-hb6.

HINT-AUTHORING RAW MATERIAL from the probe's byte scan: cand.total 580, cand.decodeMatch 124 (unverified -- a byte scan over data cannot distinguish code from a coincidental byte pair). verdict.hint listed 8d00 first. Confirm by hand before curating.

title: Compiled game descriptors must not use the .map extension; add data/games to .gitignore
description:
Two concrete couplings found while writing docs/per-game-descriptors-design.md (2026-07-31).

(1) EXTENSION COLLISION. NesBoardRegistry.scan enumerates Application.findFilesByExtensionInMyModule('.map') (NesBoardRegistry.java:83) and filters on system.board.ines_mappers. A compiled data/games/*.map would land in that board scan. Harmless TODAY thanks to the system == null skip at :88-90, but it is a live coupling that will bite the first time either side changes. RULING (design doc section 4.1): compiled game descriptors use .gmap.

(2) GITIGNORE GAP. .gitignore lists data/machines/*.map only. data/games/* needs adding, or the first buildExtension after the tier lands commits build output.

title: MosConstantReferenceAnalyzer base retargeting can defeat addr_mask decode on Bandai FCG
description:
VERIFIED IN CODE, not merely suspected. Found while investigating grm-2yx (2026-07-31).

MECHANISM: MosConstantReferenceAnalyzer.addBaseReferenceOnce (MosConstantReferenceAnalyzer.java:253-260) ADDS a reference to the operand base and its caller returns false, which suppresses the stock computed reference for that path. So an indexed store with a KNOWN index that used to reference the computed address now references the base instead.

CONSEQUENCE ON addr_mask BOARDS: MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.matchesDecode (:211-213) requires (offset & addrMask) == addrMatch. Bandai FCG (data/machines/nes-bandai-fcg.map) configures addr_mask 0xF / addr_match 0x8. A computed reference at $8008 DECODES AS MATCH; the base reference at $8000 that replaces it DECODES AS MISS. An indexed FCG register write with a known index that used to be detected therefore is no longer detected.

NOT CURRENTLY OBSERVED: the Bandai goldens (db3/dbz2/dbz_datach/dbz_saiyan) did not move in commit 08af5e8, so no shipped title exercises it today. But it is a real soundness hole introduced by grm-phv, and the shape of code that triggers it (STA reg,X into a mapper register file) is ordinary.

RELATED: grm-phv (introduced it), grm-2yx (found it). Note the interaction with the writesInRange operand-decode fallback bead: that fallback must DECLINE on (addr_mask present AND indexed operand), because base & 0xF says nothing about (base+X) & 0xF.

title: Re-analysis must pick up newly shipped descriptor data after an extension upgrade
description:
USER REQUIREMENT: with a working disassembly in Ghidra, installing a new extension version should let re-analysis pick up any new hints that shipped with it, plus other analysis improvements.

CONCRETE DEFECT: BoardBankAnalyzer's redundant-rerun cache LAST_COMPLETED (BoardBankAnalyzer.java:150-160, checked :216-226) is keyed on fingerprint(program) (functionCount << 40 ^ numInstructions) and mapPath -- NOT on descriptor CONTENT. An upgraded extension shipping a revised descriptor at the same path can therefore be judged already-complete and skip. Whatever key identifies a descriptor version must enter that cache.

MOSTLY ALREADY SUPPORTED: setSupportsOneTimeAnalysis() (DescriptorCopyHintAnalyzer.java:93) plus idempotent materialization and the existing-comment guards mean re-running is safe in principle.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERION -- USER EDITS MUST SURVIVE: descriptor- and analyzer-applied annotations go in as SourceType IMPORTED/ANALYSIS and must never overwrite USER_DEFINED. That is what makes re-analysis safe to run in a program someone has been working in for months. Test it explicitly.

Note the related but distinct path: exporting your annotation layer and reapplying to a fresh import is the ExportGameDescriptor bead, not this one. This bead is about in-place re-analysis.

title: Harvest community disassemblies into per-game symbol sets
description:
Popular titles (Zelda, Metroid, Mega Man, SMB) already have mature public disassemblies. Ingesting them is what turns a fresh import from FUN_c34a soup into a readable disassembly -- the highest-value payload of the per-game tier, far larger than site hints.

NO NEW SCHEMA NEEDED. docs/SCHEMA.md:484-495 already defines named symbol sets, user-toggleable at import, each carrying provenance (upstream project, license, generation date), with kind: entry symbols becoming functions. The generated shape is a flat entries: [{addr, name, kind, comment}] list -- see machines/generated/c64ref-kernal.yaml. A per-game symbol set is that same file with a different provenance block.

GENERATOR PRECEDENT ALREADY EXISTS: tools/gensymbols/gen_c64ref_symbols.py (from closed grm-hnm) converts mist64/c64ref into machines/generated/*.yaml with a 'generated by ... -- do not hand-edit' header. Per-game harvesters are new instances of that pattern, one per upstream disassembly format.

CONVERGE WITH grm-54p (the C64 instance of this exact idea: import a fully pre-analyzed/labeled/commented ROM; its recorded comment already proposes a user-runnable script building the import file from user-supplied inputs). They should share mechanism, not grow separate ones. Sourcing question (submodule + build-time generation vs committed artifacts) is grm-p5w -- decide ONCE for both.

LICENSING is the gating constraint and a per-source judgment, not a policy set once: public NES disassemblies range from public-domain to entirely unlicensed. provenance is the designed answer, with build-time exclusion of sets that may not be redistributed. See vision doc section 10 risk 8.

FIRST TARGET: Zelda -- already pinned in the real-ROM tier (tools/banktest/realrom/manifest.tsv) and has mature public disassemblies.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
CORRECTION (docs/per-game-descriptors-design.md section 3b.3): the claim 'no new schema concept needed for symbols' is very nearly right but NOT literally true.

The existing symbol schema's region: qualifier (docs/SCHEMA.md:484-495) assumes one always-visible location. A game label at $8000 on a banked board is AMBIGUOUS across (e.g.) 16 UxROM banks. Per-game symbol sets therefore need exactly ONE new concept: a block: bank qualifier naming the residence.

Reuse the existing space-qualified vocabulary rather than inventing a grammar -- ghidra_scripts/RunFromElsewhereTransfer.java:166-171 already spells addresses as BLOCK:offset. Everything else about the symbol schema carries over unchanged, including provenance and the gen_c64ref_symbols.py generator pattern.

title: ExportGameDescriptor script: annotation layer out as YAML, valid as both overlay file and PR
description:
ghidra_scripts/ExportGameDescriptor.java. Writes YAML (snakeyaml emits, so shipping it per the compiler bead serves both directions) containing the computed identity plus the facts discovered in this program: bank-switch sites, labels, comments, later types.

HARD REQUIREMENT (user, 2026-07-31): output must be valid as BOTH a drop-in overlay file AND a machines/games/*.yaml pull request. That is what closes the loop: reverse -> export -> share -> curate.

Ghidra already ships whole-program carriers (Program XML, .gzf); the gap this fills is a SELECTIVE export of just the annotation layer.

ROUND-TRIP TEST: export, compile, re-consume on a fresh import, assert the same annotations. Prior art for the interaction model: ghidra_scripts/RunFromElsewhereTransfer.java (the shipped manual front-end) and the zelda row of tools/banktest/realrom/manifest.tsv, which is already a hand-authored per-game hint keyed by SHA-256.

title: Consume per-game site hints as dataflow seeds in BoardBankAnalyzer
description:
Analyzer-side, not loader-side -- DescriptorCopyHintAnalyzer.java:57-61 explains why: consuming a directive only at import 'would make the common path unreachable' for a user who supplies data AFTER importing. setSupportsOneTimeAnalysis() (:93) is load-bearing and materialization must be idempotent. A game descriptor arriving after import is the NORMAL case here, so inherit that shape exactly.

MECHANISM: feed hinted addresses into runDataflow's seed set (BoardBankAnalyzer.java:568-576) with BankState.fullyKnown(board.initialState()), disassembling first if no instruction is present -- reuse the DisassembleCommand idiom addOverlayRef already uses (:1588-1596).

SEED, DO NOT INJECT (load-bearing ruling): do NOT fabricate a SwitchResult. Seeding means the site's own computeSwitch still runs, so a WRONG hint produces no annotation instead of a confident falsehood -- and findHelpers, the second dataflow pass, and reference retargeting all cascade for free.

Reuse the applyAll(program, map, monitor, log) seam (DescriptorCopyHintAnalyzer.java:155), split out precisely so a descriptor object can be handed in without an installed extension (:150-153) -- cheapest testable entry point for the whole tier. Label provenance the way ORIGIN = 'descriptor copied_from hint' (:85) does.

title: Ship MapCompiler + snakeyaml in the extension; add an error-collecting compile mode
description:
Reverses an explicit decision: build.gradle:220 states the snakeyaml dependency is 'never copied into the extension lib/', wired at :250 as gdtBuilderImplementation, with MapCompiler's YAML front-end (YamlSupport) noted at :268. Ghidra 12.1.2 bundles NO yaml parser (verified: only gson-2.9.0.jar).

WHY REVERSE IT: one authoring format for both the curated and overlay paths, and crucially ONE VALIDATOR -- so runtime and build cannot drift apart on schema semantics while docs/SCHEMA.md:12-14 says the schema is still evolving. Also makes an exported descriptor directly usable as a PR. MapCompiler itself imports only gson + JDK; only its YAML front-end needs snakeyaml.

UPDATE the build.gradle:220 comment with the new rationale rather than silently contradicting it.

ERROR-COLLECTING MODE: MapCompiler currently FAILS THE BUILD on a bad descriptor. At runtime a malformed user file must collect errors and skip, matching DescriptorCopyHintAnalyzer.java:186-188 ('an NPE out of added() aborts the entire analysis pass for the program, where a malformed directive should cost only that directive'). Concrete work item, not a detail.

COMPILE ON READ, DO NOT CACHE: descriptors are tiny, and this repo already rejected a cache-backed mode because a correct cache needs explicit invalidation rules.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
DESIGN REFINEMENTS (docs/per-game-descriptors-design.md section 4.3):

(1) MapCompiler must PHYSICALLY MOVE to src/main/java to ship at all -- buildExtension packages the 'main' source set only, and MapCompiler's residence in the gdtBuilder source set (build.gradle:231-237) is precisely what excludes it. Bonus: build.gradle:264-272's test wiring gets simpler afterward.

(2) The snakeyaml reversal is NARROWER than first scoped: the curated set still compiles at BUILD time as it does now, so snakeyaml ships ONLY to serve the overlay path. State that in the updated build.gradle comment -- it makes the reversal much easier to justify.

(3) Error-collecting mode should WRAP rather than rewrite the existing throw sites, so build-time strictness is preserved unchanged and only the runtime caller opts into collection.

title: Runtime descriptor lookup outside the installed module (user-directory overlay)
description:
Largest net-new piece of grm-hb6. Today descriptors resolve ONLY inside installed modules: DescriptorSupport.loadMap (DescriptorSupport.java:142-151) uses Application.findDataFileInAnyModule; NesBoardRegistry.scan (NesBoardRegistry.java:81-110) uses Application.findFilesByExtensionInMyModule. There is NO user-settings-dir usage anywhere in src/main/java -- zero precedent.

BUILD ON Application.getUserSettingsDirectory(). Conveniently tools/banktest/run-banktest.sh:123 already relocates that dir for test isolation, so the overlay is testable per-worktree for free.

REQUIREMENTS: search order overlay-before-curated (local work-in-progress must win for the same title) with shadowing LOGGED, never silent. Do NOT inherit NesBoardRegistry's static memoization (:49, :54-59) -- a mid-session drop-in is never re-scanned there; the game registry needs non-memoized lookup or an explicit refresh. Rule on whether include: composition is permitted in overlay files (disallow, or resolve against overlay dir + bundled fragments).

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
DESIGN REFINEMENT (docs/per-game-descriptors-design.md sections 4.2/5.3):

USE Application.getUserSettingsFiles(dir, ext) (Application.java:635-646), NOT raw getUserSettingsDirectory(). Its copyFilesFromPreviousVersion branch (:640-643) migrates a user's overlay files across a GHIDRA version upgrade for free -- hand-rolling the scan silently loses that, which matters a lot for files representing months of reverse-engineering work.

Upstream precedent: BSimServerManager.java:56-64 uses exactly this primitive. It is SIMULTANEOUSLY AN ANTI-PRECEDENT: it scans inside a memoized singleton's constructor (:46-51), the same trap as NesBoardRegistry's static memoized boards field. Do not copy that half.

title: Per-game identity: PRG-content hash + whole-file SHA-256 in the extension
description:
The shipped extension computes NO hash of any kind -- grep for SHA256/getExecutableSHA/crc over src/main/java finds nothing. NesRomLoader's parsed identity is mapper-number-only (InesHeader record, NesRomLoader.java:104; board resolution :322-323). Per-title identity is net-new.

DESIGN: PRG-content SHA-256 primary (hash the PRG-ROM slice only, so headerless dumps, corrected bad headers and re-dumps of identical content all match ONE descriptor -- InesHeader already knows prgBanks/trainer so the slice bounds are in hand); whole-file SHA-256 as an alias for exactness, which also lets tools/banktest/realrom/manifest.tsv and the extension agree on a key.

Store the resolved game-descriptor path as a Program Info property beside MAP_PATH_PROPERTY (DescriptorSupport.java:79) so analyzers read it back the same way.
close_reason: Shipped: NesRomLoader stamps Retro Machines.Game Identity (prg:<64 hex> file:<64 hex>) on every NES import, computed from the ByteProvider at import. GAME_DESCRIPTOR_PROPERTY declared but unwritten pending grm-hb6.2/.3, per the settled identity-only scope. Verified at all three tiers: 23 new Tier-1 tests (suite 98->121), criteria GID1/GID2/GID3 PASS on all 10 NES fixtures with GID3 an independent slice-bounds oracle, and REALROM prgsha256 in the real-ROM dump. Full gate SUITE OK. Commit f945703. NES 2.0 exponent PRG-size form declines to key -- filed as grm-dfj. Realrom goldens (12) still need user re-bless with the pinned ROMs.

title: Upstream Ghidra PR: ConstantPropagationContextEvaluator.setMinStoreLoadOffset assigns the wrong field
description:
Verified at Ghidra_12.1.2_build (D:/git/ghidra, tag-exact).

ConstantPropagationContextEvaluator.java:127-130 --

    public ConstantPropagationContextEvaluator setMinStoreLoadOffset(long minStoreLoadRefAddress) {
        maxSpeculativeOffset = minStoreLoadRefAddress;   // should be minStoreLoadOffset
        return this;
    }

It is chained LAST in ConstantPropagationAnalyzer.flowConstants (:507-512):

    new ConstantPropagationContextEvaluator(monitor)
        .setTrustWritableMemory(...)
        .setMinSpeculativeOffset(minSpeculativeRefAddress)
        .setMaxSpeculativeOffset(maxSpeculativeRefAddress)
        .setMinStoreLoadOffset(minStoreLoadRefAddress)     <-- clobbers maxSpeculativeOffset
        .setCreateComplexDataFromPointers(...)

Two consequences:
 1. maxSpeculativeOffset is overwritten with minStoreLoadRefAddress (option default 4), discarding
    the value setMaxSpeculativeOffset just installed -- on a 16-bit space canAnalyze computes 128
    (ConstantPropagationAnalyzer.java:155-157), so the end-of-memory rejection window shrinks 128 -> 4.
 2. minStoreLoadOffset never receives the option value; it stays at its constructor default of 4
    (ConstantPropagationContextEvaluator.java:56). The user-visible analysis option
    "Min absolute reference" / MINSTORELOADREFADDRESS is therefore INERT.

Affects the base analyzer and all 13 per-processor subclasses (MIPS, ARM, PowerPC, x86, SH4, PIC16,
68K, Hexagon, RISCV, Sparc, NDS32, Loongarch, Toy), every one of which repeats the same fluent chain.

Fix is one line: assign minStoreLoadOffset.

Why we care: "Min absolute reference" is exactly the knob a 6502 user must lower to get zero-page
references, and it is the field tom-seddon's Ghidra6502 prior art tried to set. Discovered while
researching grm-phv; deliberately kept SEPARATE from it -- grm-phv ships an in-extension analyzer and
does not depend on this landing upstream.

ALSO FOUND, record only, do NOT PR (behavior argument, not a bug):
 - OperandReferenceAnalyzer.canAnalyze:142-163 hard-disables itself for default address spaces of
   <= 16 bits ("only analyze programs with address spaces > 16 bits"), excluding every 8/16-bit
   retro target from data-reference analysis. Ditto ElfScalarOperandAnalyzer.
 - ScalarOperandAnalyzer:161-167 discards every operand scalar < 4096, which on a 16-bit machine
   throws away most of the address space.
 - SymbolicPropogator.java:2253-2264 carries the author's own TODO: "this could be a calculated
   OFFSET reference with a base address".

Upstream context for grm-phv (do not reopen): ghidra#201 is the base-vs-computed indexed reference
issue, closed 2019, with emteere confirming 2024-07-16 that it is expected behavior and that the
generic fix needs full-function dataflow. Scope approved for this bead is the setter fix ONLY -- no
comment on #201, no upstream analyzer proposal.

title: Run-from-elsewhere: banked SOURCES -- read the occupant off the LDA the way grm-bqs reads it off the STA
description:
docs/smc-runfromelsewhere-design.md section 8 open question 3, reframed by grm-bqs (2026-07-27). A copy source may live in a banked window; today CopyLoopAnalyzer takes LoopIdioms.indexedBase(lda) at face value, which names the base-space HOME occupant of the containing window -- the same class of mistake grm-bqs fixed on the destination side.

WHY THIS IS SMALLER THAN THE DOC ORIGINALLY IMPLIED. grm-bqs closed the destination half not by adding a schema key but by consuming what BoardBankAnalyzer already computes: it resolves every access against the bank state live at that instruction and re-homes the reference into the occupant reached. grm-5tl.9 already made it emit READ references as well as WRITE ones (the RMW split, BoardBankAnalyzer:1451-1470), so the source should be readable off the LDA exactly as the destination is off the STA -- LoopIdioms.overlayWriteTarget with the reference-type polarity flipped, probably generalized to overlayAccessTarget(store, base, len, RefType predicate).

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING is a fixture, not a mechanism. Needs a PRG whose copy loop READS from a banked window -- the natural one is a copy out of the KERNAL or BASIC ROM with the dump supplied, which is also the shape docs/smc-survey.md risk 4 flags. Note the asymmetry that makes this harder to assert than the destination: a read goes to whichever occupant is LIVE (there is no on_read key, and no equivalent of on_write to make the answer bank-state-independent), so the fixture has to pin the bank state deliberately rather than relying on the default.

ALSO CHECK while here: DescriptorCopyHintAnalyzer.resolveSource:261-269 already prefers the NAMED block and takes its address space, which is a second, independent path to the same answer for the declarative front-end. Decide whether the two should converge.
close_reason:
Banked copy SOURCES resolved off the LDA, mirroring grm-bqs on the STA.

MECHANISM. LoopIdioms.overlayWriteTarget generalized to overlayAccessTarget(access, base, len, Predicate<RefType> polarity); CopyLoopAnalyzer passes RefType::isWrite for the destination and RefType::isRead for the source, both in the same late position after the src/dst and jump-into-range tests. TransferTarget stays keyed on the destination only -- a re-homed source changes where bytes are READ FROM, not where they are placed. RunFromElsewhere.validate and TransferMaterializer.readSource needed no change: neither couples src and dst spaces.

CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY, the issue's core claim: BoardBankAnalyzer was ALREADY emitting the correct re-homed READ reference (grm-5tl.9's RMW split). The new copybankedsrc-srcref-resolved criterion PASSES against the unpatched analyzer in both runs. There was no missing mechanism, only a missing consumer -- exactly as docs/smc-runfromelsewhere-design.md section 8 predicted.

FIXTURE (the actual work, per the issue). copybankedsrc.prg: the C64 CHARACTER ROM as source -- a NON-HOME occupant of the CHARIO window, since initial_state has CHAREN=1 and the home occupant is IO -- with an ordinary base-space $C000 RAM destination, so the read is the only banked thing in the fixture. Pins the bank state itself with LDA #$33 / STA $01, which the issue called for: with the default state every C64 window's live occupant IS its home occupant, so there is nothing to resolve.

Run BOTH ways, and unlike the copybanked pair these two MUST DIFFER -- that is the demonstration:
  copybankedsrc    (no dump)  -> gate 0 refuses, nothing placed, note names CHARGEN:d000
  copybankedsrcrom (chargen)  -> COPY_c000 carved in place, bytes aa ab a8 a9 ae af ac ad
Those are chargen.bin's (i & 0xFF) ^ 0xAA pattern, which exists nowhere in the PRG image.

PRE-FIX, measured with the mechanism stashed: both runs identical, both refusing with 'copy RAM:d000 -> ...' (the IO home occupant, uninitialized either way), so supplying the character ROM changed nothing and its bytes were never reached.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE PLAN. The no-dump golden as first written was bit-identical pre- and post-fix (both refuse, for different reasons), so it guarded nothing on its own. Added a SOURCE line parsed out of the refusal note -- the only place that run records which occupant was resolved -- plus a copybankedsrc-norom-source-resolved criterion pinning CHARGEN:d000. Both halves of the pair are now real guards.

CONVERGENCE QUESTION (the issue's 'ALSO CHECK'): DECIDED NO. DescriptorCopyHintAnalyzer.resolveSource and LoopIdioms.overlayAccessTarget answer the same question from different KINDS of evidence -- a human-authored block name with no instruction, vs. an instruction whose reference the banking analyzer resolved against live bank state. Converging would mean inventing a fake instruction on the descriptor path or degrading the instruction path to a descriptor-only derivation, and the second is impossible in principle: there is no on_read key because a read goes to whichever occupant is LIVE. Cross-referencing javadoc added to both sites; no code moved.

THE ASYMMETRY, recorded in LoopIdioms javadoc because it is the instructive part: on_write exists because a write's destination is bank-state-INDEPENDENT (you cannot write to ROM, so a store to $E000 reaches RAM_E000 either way, statically stateable). A read's is not. Only per-instruction resolution can supply it.

FENCED OUT -> grm-cpj: the src.equals(dst) early return still rejects LDA $A000,Y / STA $A000,Y, a real ROM->RAM-under-ROM copy, as an in-place decrypt. grm-9a0 built the machinery to tell them apart but admitting them touches the shared decrypt path and wants its own fixture.

Docs: section 8 open question 3 marked DONE with the rationale; section 9 checkbox added. Full gate green; no pre-existing golden moved.

title: ADC (and RRA) compute the V and C flags incorrectly -- inherited from Ghidra's stock 6502 spec
description:
data/languages/6502core.sinc:140-151 (a byte-faithful copy of Ghidra's own
Ghidra/Processors/6502/data/languages/6502.slaspec:127-138) has two flag defects in ADC:

    local op1 = OP1;
    local tmpC = C;
    C = carry(A, op1);      # (1) carry-in not included
    A = A + op1 + tmpC;
    resultFlags(A);
    V = C;                  # (2) signed overflow set to the unsigned carry

(1) WRONG CARRY-OUT. carry(A, op1) is evaluated before tmpC is added, so a carry that
    arises only from the carry-in is lost.
    Repro: A=$FF, operand=$00, C=1 -> result $00 and the real 6502 sets C=1;
    this spec computes carry($FF,$00)=0 and clears C.
    Impact: breaks carry propagation in multi-byte arithmetic -- the CLC / LDA lo1 /
    ADC lo2 / LDA hi1 / ADC hi2 idiom that 16-bit adds in music drivers are built from.

(2) WRONG OVERFLOW. V is signed overflow, not unsigned carry; they are different flags.
    Repro: A=$50, operand=$50, C=0 -> result $A0. No unsigned carry, so this spec yields
    V=0, but +80 + +80 overflowed into negative and the real 6502 sets V=1.
    Correct form: V = ((A ^ result) & (op1 ^ result) & 0x80) != 0

SCOPE
- Affects ADC in all three bundled languages (6510:LE:16:default, 6510:LE:16:undoc,
  6502:LE:16:undoc), and RRA in the two :undoc variants -- RRA is ROR-then-ADC and the
  vendored 6510_illegal.sinc deliberately mirrors the base spec's ADC idiom, so it
  inherits both bugs.
- SBC is NOT affected: it uses the subtraction_flags1 macro, which implements the full
  correct bit formula. The vendored ISC likewise routes through subtraction_flags1.
- Consequence: any decompiled 6502/6510 code branching on BVC/BVS after ADC, or relying
  on ADC's carry-out, is mis-modeled. Decompiler output and SymbolicPropogator results
  are affected, not just the listing.

PRE-EXISTING AND INHERITED, not introduced by grm-bk6 or grm-azg -- verified identical in
the official spec at tag Ghidra_12.1.2_build. Fixing it in 6502core.sinc means our 6510
languages diverge (correctly) from stock 6502 behavior; note that in the file header.
Plausibly upstreamable to Ghidra afterwards, like grm-phv.

WATCH: the golden fixtures may shift if any fixture's analysis depends on ADC flags.
Review the diff rather than blessing it blind. Add Tier-2 tests asserting the p-code for
both repro cases above (AbstractBundledLanguageTest makes this reachable, bead grm-2pi).

Found during the grm-azg audit of the vendored undocumented-opcode semantics, which
cross-checked p-code against MAME's om6502.lst/m6502.cpp and the oxyron.de opcode matrix.

title: Resolve the Ghidra install dir from a machine-local ghidraInstallRoot (stock precedence preserved)
description:
Separate the two concerns that the stock skeleton conflates in one absolute path: WHERE Ghidra
installs live (machine-local) vs WHICH version this project targets (repo-local). Motivating
failure: a GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR env var is snapshotted when a shell or long-running agent session
starts and cannot be corrected in place, so a session that outlives a Ghidra retarget fails
grm-9r7's version guard on every build until it restarts. Secondary goal: keep developer drive
letters out of committed files.

CHANGES
- New ghidraInstallRoot property, set once in the machine-local ~/.gradle/gradle.properties,
  composed with gradle.properties' ghidraTargetVersion to form <root>/ghidra_<ver>_PUBLIC.
  Retargeting becomes one line in gradle.properties with nothing outside the repo to update.
- build.gradle resolution order: GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR env var -> -PGHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR ->
  ghidraInstallRoot -> "<REPLACE>". Upstream PRECEDENCE IS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED (principle of
  least astonishment); ghidraInstallRoot is appended as a pure fallback and the two stock
  branches are untouched. An earlier draft inverted the order so -P would outrank the env var
  -- REJECTED, see the design note below.
- Version-guard failure messages explain both knobs and the stale-env-var escape hatch, and no
  longer hardcode D:/ghidra_<ver>_PUBLIC.
- Docs: README "Building" + new "Overriding the install dir"; CLAUDE.md tells agents NOT to
  prefix gradle with GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR=<path>; docs/testing.md drops the prefix;
  gradle.properties comment updated. bd memory build-ghidra-install-dir rewritten.

DESIGN NOTE -- why precedence was NOT inverted
Inverting it would violate the principle of least astonishment for anyone who knows the Ghidra
skeleton, and it turned out to be unnecessary: because the stock branch is a Groovy truthiness
test, an EMPTY value is falsy, so a stale env var can be blanked per invocation and resolution
falls through to ghidraInstallRoot:

    GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR= gradle <task>

Verified stable across repeated runs with no Gradle-daemon contamination (the ambient value is
still honored on the next unprefixed run). `env -u GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR gradle ...` is the
equivalent that truly unsets. CAVEAT: do not "tighten" the stock condition to `!= null` -- that
would silently break this escape hatch. Noted in a build.gradle comment.

WINDOWS GOTCHA worth keeping documented: ghidraInstallRoot must be absolute with a trailing
FORWARD slash. A bare drive letter is drive-relative ("D:" means the current directory on D:,
composing to "D:ghidra_<ver>_PUBLIC"), and .properties treats "\" as an escape character, so a
trailing backslash reads as a line continuation and silently leaves the value as the bare drive
letter. Both were observed empirically, not theorized.

VERIFIED
- no env, no -P -> ghidraInstallRoot governs (exit 0)
- -P beats ghidraInstallRoot when env unset (exit 0)
- env var beats -P: env 12.0.4 vs -P 12.1.2 resolved 12.0.4 -> guard fired (upstream order intact)
- stale env blanked by 'GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR=' prefix -> falls through, exit 0, 3/3 runs
- full gate: bash tools/banktest/build-and-test.sh check -> SUITE OK

FOLLOW-UP FOR THE USER (not done here): the Windows User-scope GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR is still set
to D:\ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC, so ghidraInstallRoot is skipped in normal use on this machine until
that variable is removed or blanked per invocation.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text: Landed in 578fe7e. Stock precedence preserved; 'GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR= gradle <task>' is the documented escape hatch for a stale env var. REMAINING USER ACTION (not code): the Windows User-scope GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR is still set to D:\ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC, so it wins and ghidraInstallRoot is skipped in normal use on this machine. Remove it ([Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR', $null, 'User')) to let ghidraInstallRoot govern, or keep it and blank per invocation. ~/.gradle/gradle.properties already holds ghidraInstallRoot=D:/.

title: NesRomLoader hard-codes its language ID instead of resolving from the descriptor
description: NesRomLoader.java:92 has 'private static final String LANGUAGE_ID = "6502:LE:16:default";' and NesRomLoader.java:169-170 builds its LanguageCompilerSpecPair straight from it, bypassing DescriptorSupport.resolveLanguageId(). Every other loader (AbstractCbmPrgLoader.java:266-274) reads system.cpu.language from the machine descriptor and falls back only if that language is unavailable. Consequence: nes-*.yaml descriptors declare 'language: 6502:LE:16:default' but that value is ignored -- a board wanting a different CPU language (e.g. the :undoc variant from grm-azg, or a future 2A03-specific language) cannot express it in the descriptor. Route NesRomLoader through resolveLanguageId with the current constant as the safety fallback.

title: 6502/6510 Constant Reference Analyzer: indexed refs should target the base address
description:
Ghidra's stock Constant Reference Analyzer resolves indexed 6502/6510 operands to the
*computed* address: `LDA $2000,X` gets a reference to `$2000+X` for whatever X the
SymbolicPropogator happened to know. On 6502 that is almost always wrong -- the programmer
means the table at the base address `$2000`, and scattering references across `$2000+n`
buries the table instead of revealing it. Frequently encountered and a persistent irritation
in real analysis sessions.

Wanted: our own analyzer (or an option) that references the BASE address for indexed modes.

The one genuine exception is `(zp,X)` -- indexed *indirect*, where the pointer really does
live at `zp+X`, so `zp+X` is the correct reference there.

Modes to cover: zp,X / zp,Y / abs,X / abs,Y / (zp),Y -> base; (zp,X) -> zp+X (unchanged).

PRIOR ART: https://github.com/tom-seddon/Ghidra6502 ships a replacement "6502 Constant
Reference Analyzer" doing exactly this; see its README and analyzer source for the approach.

Gate on processor in {6502, 6510} the way CopyLoopAnalyzer already does
(src/main/java/retromachines/CopyLoopAnalyzer.java:101), so it also covers the new
:undoc language variants from grm-azg.

Plausibly upstreamable to Ghidra afterwards, since it is not C64-specific.

Independent of grm-azg -- no ordering dependency either way.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
Confirmed in the wild by grm-bqs (2026-07-27), with a concrete measurement. For 'STA $E000,X' driving an 8-byte down-counting copy loop, the references actually attached to the store are $E006 and $E007 -- never $E000, the base. So a consumer that wants 'which occupant does this indexed access reach' cannot match on the base address at all.

LoopIdioms.overlayWriteTarget works around it by matching a re-homed reference anywhere in [base, base+len) and then re-homing the BASE into the space it found, rather than returning whichever index the constant analyzer happened to pin down. That workaround is correct independently of grm-phv (any offset in the range identifies the occupant, since one store writes the whole range through one window), so fixing grm-phv will not break it -- but the range match becomes redundant for that caller, and the comment in overlayWriteTarget's javadoc pointing here should be revisited then.

title: Suppress KERNAL IOINIT ($FDA3) from user-visible bank-switch-helper analyzer log
description:
The banking analyzer detects $FDA3 in the C64 KERNAL ROM as a bank-switch helper. That is a true positive in mechanism terms -- $FDA3 is the meat of the IOINIT KERNAL routine, which resets the 6510 port ($00/$01) to its power-on state -- but it is noise to the user: it is a stock KERNAL housekeeping routine, not a game's banking helper, and it will fire on every program that has a KERNAL ROM loaded.

Wanted: keep treating it as a helper UNDER THE HOOD (the mechanism modelling is correct and the value recovery may depend on it), but suppress it from the analyzer output the user actually reads. So this is a reporting/log filter, not a recognition change -- do not stop recognizing it.

Open questions for whoever picks this up: whether to suppress by address (a known-KERNAL-routine denylist, which needs the ROM to be identified), by provenance (helper sits inside a region whose kind is rom and whose image is the stock kernal), or by a general 'helper found in ROM rather than in the loaded PRG' rule. The general rule is probably right and probably covers more stock-ROM false-positive noise than just IOINIT.

Reported by Chris 2026-07-25 while working the grm-1.7 front-ends.

title: Run-from-elsewhere copies are materialized in place (carve + snapshot), not as overlays
description:
DECISION (grm-chu, 2026-07-25). Full record with file:line citations: docs/smc-inplace-vs-overlay.md.

CHOSEN: carve the destination out of its containing uninitialized block (Memory.split x2 -> convertToInitialized(0) -> setBytes) so the copied bytes live at the address the CPU runs them from. A base-space JSR/JMP into the destination then resolves natively, with no per-call-site reference bridging.

VERDICT ON THE CORE QUESTION the bead was opened on: NO Ghidra core change is needed, there is no upstream ask, and this is NOT an RFC #9349 item. Memory.split has no initialized-ness check (MemoryMapDB.java:989-1035); the pattern has an in-tree analyzer precedent (GolangSymbolAnalyzer.java:712-728 isolating runtime.writeBarrier) and a precedent in our own loader (AbstractCbmPrgLoader.createCarvedTarget:706-744). convertToInitialized is whole-block only -- there is no sub-range variant, public or package-private -- so split-then-convert is the only supported route.

REJECTED, and it was close: a non-overlay byte-mapped block at base:dst (legal -- createByteMappedBlock(..., overlay=false) gates only on checkRange, MemoryMapDB.java:1952) would have kept dual-home byte identity AND self-healing when a ROM is supplied later. It loses on two verifiable properties: freeing the range needs removeBlock, which calls deleteAddressRange (MemoryMapDB.java:1887) and destroys symbols/comments/refs in the range, and the result reports isInitialized()==false.

TWO INVARIANTS, both enforced in code, not just documented: (a) carving requires Transform.IDENTITY -- convertToInitialized writes a synthetic fill byte, which is only acceptable where the destination held nothing meaningful; a decrypt-in-place has real encrypted bytes, so unifying grm-1.7.2 onto this materializer must never enable carving. Checked in canCarve as well as at the top of materialize, deliberately redundantly. (b) carve range == write range, so no fill byte survives.

UNREADABLE SOURCE: produce nothing -- no overlay fallback, no invented bytes. Per Chris: for an explicit descriptor copied_from directive, no KERNAL ROM means no CHRGET copy is produced. Recoverable later because materialization is idempotent and the analyzer declares supportsOneTimeAnalysis. This REVERSES docs/smc-runfromelsewhere-design.md section 8 question 2, which had recommended best-effort materialization against an uninitialized source.

OVERLAY RETAINED as the fallback for destinations that cannot be carved (already initialized, straddling blocks, or already in an overlay space).
close_reason: Decision recorded and now reflected in both docs. smc-inplace-vs-overlay.md gained Gate 0.5 + precondition 5 + the IN_PLACE_BANKED placement in §5, a dated amendment line in §8, and the TransferTransform type-name fix. smc-runfromelsewhere-design.md's four stale spots (§3 best-effort option, §4 loader-applies-the-hint, §5 dual-home assumption, §7 sequencing) now match what shipped, and §8 q3 is reframed.

title: NES run-from-elsewhere: copy-to-$6000 (PRG-RAM) real-ROM case + machine-neutral recognizer
description:
Chris observed an NES title copying code into $6000 (PRG-RAM/SRAM) and executing it there -- probably Mega Man or Bionic Commando, not yet confirmed which. This is a real-hardware instance of the run-from-elsewhere pattern (grm-1.7.1) on a non-C64 machine, and is worth BOTH a real-ROM regression case and a synthetic NES fixture mirroring the idiom. Not a blocker for anything.

THREE THINGS STAND BETWEEN HERE AND THAT TEST (all found while implementing grm-chu):

1. The recognizer is C64-only. C64CopyLoopAnalyzer.canAnalyze gates on program.getExecutableFormat().equals(C64PrgLoader.NAME), so it cannot fire on ANY NES ROM today. The port looks cheap: the NES CPU is a 6502, the LDA abs,X / STA abs,X / DEX / BPL idiom is identical, LoopIdioms is pure 6502 with nothing C64-specific, and TransferMaterializer (post-grm-chu) is already machine-neutral. So the work is mostly canAnalyze/registration -- either widen the gate or add an NES sibling analyzer.

2. Which mapper the title uses decides whether the destination is even mapped. MMC1 (machines/nes-mmc1.yaml:82) and MMC3 (machines/nes-mmc3.yaml:60) declare 'PRG_RAM $6000-$7FFF kind: ram' -- an uninitialized base-space block, so grm-chu's in-place carve applies cleanly and refs to $6000 would resolve natively. UxROM (machines/nes-uxrom.yaml) declares NO $6000 region at all, only PRG_LO/PRG_HI at $8000-$FFFF. Mega Man and Contra are both UxROM in the real-ROM manifest, so if Mega Man is the title, either the descriptor needs a PRG-RAM region added or the observation belongs to a different game.

3. An UNMAPPED destination has no good placement branch yet -- a gap grm-chu did not cover. TransferMaterializer.canCarve requires getBlock(dst) != null, so when nothing covers the destination at all (the UxROM $6000 case) it falls through to the byte-mapped overlay. That is the worst of the three options there: with the range entirely unmapped there is no conflict to avoid, so the RIGHT answer is a plain non-overlay createInitializedBlock at base:dst -- no carve, no split, no overlay, and references resolve for free. Adding that third branch is small and self-contained.

HARNESS NOTES: the real-ROM tier is tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh with titles hash-pinned in tools/banktest/realrom/manifest.tsv (megaman is already pinned: mapper 2, nes_uxrom, sha e5bbc798...); ROM binaries are never committed, absent/mismatched dumps SKIP rather than fail.
