A synthetic fixture would follow tools/banktest/mkcopytest.py, which after grm-chu already covers all three C64 placements (in-place carve at a block start, in-place carve interior, overlay fallback).

FIRST STEP: identify the actual title and the address it copies from, then decide whether it is a descriptor gap (item 2) or a placement gap (item 3) or both.
notes:
2026-07-25 (Chris): The Legend of Zelda has a public disassembly that can be consulted to find the copy routine instead of reversing it from scratch. Canonical repo: https://github.com/aldonunez/zelda1-disassembly ("A complete disassembly of The Legend of Zelda", ~259 stars, Assembly, actively updated, default branch 'master').

Zelda is the strongest candidate of the pinned titles: it is MMC1, so machines/nes-mmc1.yaml:82 already declares PRG_RAM $6000-$7FFF kind:ram (battery-backed save RAM), which means the destination is a real uninitialized base-space block and grm-chu's in-place carve would apply directly -- no descriptor gap and no unmapped-destination gap (items 2 and 3 above). It is also already hash-pinned in tools/banktest/realrom/manifest.tsv as 'zelda' (sha 8f72dc2e...), so the real-ROM harness can use it with no manifest work. Contrast Mega Man, which is UxROM and has no $6000 region declared at all.

DEAD END TO NOT REPEAT: the GitHub code-search API does not index that repo -- 'repo:aldonunez/zelda1-disassembly "6000"' returns total_count 0, and so does a generic term, which means the .asm sources are not indexed rather than the string being absent. Consulting it requires a local clone plus grep, not the GitHub MCP search tools.

Also still unconfirmed which title Chris actually observed; Zelda is a hypothesis to check against the disassembly, not an identification.
close_reason:
Title identified from ROM bytes as The Legend of Zelda (not Mega Man); routine at bank 1 $8D00 copying $A500 -> $6C90, 0x1270 bytes, entered by JMP $6C90 at $A13B. Recognizer ported off its C64 gate to descriptor + 6502/6510 language (CopyLoopAnalyzer). Unmapped-destination placement branch added as TransferPlacement.NEW_BLOCK. Synthetic nescopytest fixture covers the widened gate with a loop executing from a bank overlay into base-space PRG_RAM. Zelda wired into the real-ROM tier via -preScript and the manual script, since its indirect-indexed pointer walk is invisible to the recognizer; zelda.dump blessed showing COPY_6c90 carved out of PRG_RAM.

The bead's items 2 and 3 turned out moot for Zelda (MMC1 already declares PRG_RAM as a base-space region), and the real find was the opposite of what was expected: widening the gate produced FALSE POSITIVES on 3 of 4 real ROMs by materializing ordinary RAM data copies, including over the stack page. Fixed by requiring a jump into the range before materializing at all -- a return to the design doc's original rule, affordable only because the deferred-call case now has the copied_from directive and the manual script. Commits b6328fa, 5b76946, 1203655.

Two things deliberately NOT done: LoopIdioms.resolve was added and then REMOVED as dead code (Ghidra's OverlayAddressSpace.getAddress already re-homes an out-of-overlay offset to the base space), and megaman's golden was left failing on the known grm-g73 drift rather than blessed.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
2026-07-25 TITLE IDENTIFIED FROM THE ROM BYTES: it is THE LEGEND OF ZELDA. Not a hypothesis any more, and not Mega Man.

EVIDENCE. Scanned both pinned dumps for control flow into $6000-$7FFF. Zelda: 389 JSR and 87 JMP into PRG-RAM, in coherent 6502 context (e.g. 'CMP #$7B / BCS +4 / CMP #$6E / BCS +15 / JSR $7314 / BEQ +10 / LDA #$00'). Mega Man: the $6xxx hits are false positives inside graphics data (bitmap-looking context, no coherent flow). Chance baseline for a 128 KiB ROM is ~64 hits, so Zelda's 389 is ~6x over noise AND reads as real code.

THE COPY ROUTINE: PRG bank 1, CPU $8D00 (file offset 0x4D00).
  $8D00 LDA #$00 / STA $00 ; LDA #$A5 / STA $01   -> src ptr = $A500
  $8D08 LDA #$90 / STA $02 ; LDA #$6C / STA $03   -> dst ptr = $6C90
  $8D10 LDY #$00
  $8D12 LDA ($00),Y / STA ($02),Y                  <- the copy
        16-bit increment of both pointers (LDA/CLC/ADC #$01/STA + LDA/ADC #$00/STA)
  $8D30 CMP #$7F / BNE $8D12 ; LDA $02 / CMP #$00 / BNE $8D12 ; RTS
So: bank-1 $A500 -> $6C90, length $7F00-$6C90 = 0x1270 (4720) bytes. There is a JMP $6C90 at bank 1 $A13B.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD -- item 1 of the description is only HALF right. Porting the recognizer off its C64 gate was necessary (done, this session: C64CopyLoopAnalyzer -> CopyLoopAnalyzer, gated on descriptor + 6502/6510 language) but is NOT SUFFICIENT for Zelda: this is an indirect-indexed pointer walk with a 16-bit terminator test, structurally invisible to the LDA abs,X / STA abs,X / DEX / BPL recognizer. Zelda must be driven by the MANUAL front-end (grm-1.7.1.1), which is exactly the long-tail case that bead exists for. Not worth widening the recognizer for a one-off idiom.

ITEMS 2 AND 3 OF THE DESCRIPTION ARE MOOT FOR ZELDA. machines/nes-mmc1.yaml:80-88 declares PRG_RAM $6000-$7FFF kind:ram under memory.regions -- a plain base-space uninitialized block -- and realrom/expected/zelda.dump already shows 'PRG_RAM 6000-7fff overlay=false'. So the in-place carve applies directly: no descriptor gap (item 2) and the unmapped-destination gap (item 3) is not on this path. Item 3 was implemented anyway as robustness: TransferPlacement.NEW_BLOCK, commit b6328fa.

ROMS ARE AVAILABLE LOCALLY: H:/emulators/nes/ROMs. 'Legend of Zelda, The (PRG 0) (U).nes' and 'MEGAMAN.NES' both hash-match the manifest pins exactly, so the real-ROM tier runs today with:
  bash tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh check /h/emulators/nes/ROMs

FOR THE REAL-ROM STEP: use -preScript, NOT a second -postScript. Pre-scripts run at HeadlessAnalyzer.java:1012-1016, BEFORE the 'Analysis' transaction opens at :1045, so the materialized $6C90 bytes are present when auto-analysis runs and Ghidra's own disassembler and reference analysis pick them up. Verified separately that NesRomLoader creates the bank overlay blocks at import time (NesRomLoader.java:698), so the overlay-qualified source address W8000_M3_B1:a500 already resolves at pre-script time.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
2026-07-25 PREMISE VALIDATED END-TO-END against the real ROM, before writing any harness wiring. Imported Zelda headlessly with NesRomLoader and drove RunFromElsewhere.apply directly from a throwaway -preScript:

  src = W8000_M3_B1::a500, dst = 6c90, len = 0x1270, disassemble+function on

  PROBE result placement=IN_PLACE block=COPY_6c90 already=false detail=
  PROBE block 6c90-7eff init=true overlay=false
  PROBE first16 a9 00 85 13 e6 11 60 20 b6 08 24 24 24 24 24 24

Three things this settles:
1. Placement is IN_PLACE in the BASE space, exactly as predicted from nes-mmc1.yaml's PRG_RAM region -- no overlay, so the 389 JSR / 87 JMP call sites into $6000-$7FFF resolve natively with no bridging. That was the entire motivation of grm-chu.
2. The overlay-qualified source address parses and reads: W8000_M3_B1::a500 resolves at PRE-SCRIPT time, confirming NesRomLoader creates the bank overlays at import (NesRomLoader.java:698), before scripts and before analysis.
3. The copied bytes are REAL CODE, not data: a9 00 85 13 e6 11 60 = LDA #$00 / STA $13 / INC $11 / RTS. A coherent little routine ending in RTS at the very start of the copied image.

So the remaining work for the real-ROM tier is only harness wiring, and it is lighter than planned: realrom-test.sh already reads an optional 7th 'opts' column from manifest.tsv and passes it UNQUOTED into the analyzeHeadless command line, and realrom_cache_key already folds opts into the cache key. So the -preScript invocation can go straight in the manifest row. The only harness changes needed are adding the repo's ghidra_scripts dir to -scriptPath (currently just tools/banktest) and whatever RealRomDump needs to surface the copy. Note RealRomDump already dumps every block, so COPY_6c90 will appear in the golden automatically.

WATCH OUT: adding ~4.7 KiB of newly disassembled code will move zelda.dump's instruction and reference counts a lot. grm-g73 already records that these counts are a fragile golden surface (megaman drifts 1781/7437 vs 1782/7435), so consider whether zelda's counts should be bucketed/dropped rather than pinned exactly.

title: Run-from-elsewhere: copy destination inside a banked window carves the wrong occupant
description: Discovered while implementing grm-chu's in-place carve. TransferMaterializer.canCarve only asks whether the destination's containing BASE-SPACE block is uninitialized, splittable and DEFAULT. On the C64 the home occupant of a banked window is a base-space block, so a copy loop targeting $E000 (a real pattern: games run code from the RAM under the KERNAL ROM) finds the KERNAL block there. With no ROM image supplied KERNAL is uninitialized, so the carve fires and splits KERNAL into KERNAL / COPY_e000 / KERNAL_xxxx -- when the semantically correct destination is the RAM_E000 overlay (the RAM under the ROM), not the ROM occupant. With a ROM image supplied KERNAL is initialized and it correctly falls back to the overlay, so the bug only shows in the no-ROM case. Mechanically harmless today (verified: nothing outside C64BasicAnalyzer's getBlock(\"PRG\") looks an occupant block up by name, and OverlayNaming parses overlay SPACE names, which a carve does not create), so this is a mislabeling/navigation problem rather than a correctness break. Fix direction: canCarve should consult the descriptor and refuse to carve a block that is a window occupant, choosing the window's RAM occupant instead -- which is the mirror image of the deferred 'banked sources' question in docs/smc-runfromelsewhere-design.md section 8 open question 3, and probably wants solving with it.
close_reason: Fixed by reading BoardBankAnalyzer's re-homed write reference off the storing instruction (LoopIdioms.overlayWriteTarget) rather than re-deriving a write target from the descriptor -- which cannot work in general, since which occupant a write reaches is bank-state-dependent (C64 CHARIO: VIC registers vs RAM_D000). CopyLoopAnalyzer now hands the materializer a destination already homed in the right space, marked TransferTarget.RESOLVED_SPACE, and moved one analysis-priority step past the banking analyzer to make that ordering a real dependency rather than a tie. Front-ends with no instruction to resolve through are covered by precondition 5: only plain RAM is carved, never an unwritable (ROM) or volatile (I/O) block. Reported as the new TransferPlacement.IN_PLACE_BANKED, which takes the entering-jump bridge. Fixtures copybanked/copybankedrom (goldens deliberately byte-identical). Full gate green.

title: Reference-precedence retargeting: redirect refs from base to a copied overlay
description: Constructive complement to the overlay-friction bead. Once a copied overlay exists at a destination, it holds the authoritative bytes and can be assumed to take precedence over base. An analyzer pass could then override the default reference creation for addresses covered by such an overlay -- retargeting incoming references (e.g. JSR $0073) from base:dst to the overlay copy program-wide, rather than bridging each call site one at a time (as grm-1.7.1's per-site bridgeJump does). Depends on the run-from-elsewhere materialization (grm-1.7.1) existing to mark which ranges are overlay-backed copies.
notes: 2026-07-25 (grm-chu): NARROWED. grm-chu changed the default materialization for a verbatim copy into uninitialized RAM to an in-place carve in the BASE space, so those copies now resolve incoming references natively -- a JSR/JMP at the destination address hits the materialized code with no retargeting at all. Program-wide reference-precedence retargeting is therefore no longer needed for the common run-from-elsewhere case. This bead still applies to (a) the overlay FALLBACK path (destination already initialized, straddling two blocks, or already in an overlay space -- see TransferMaterializer.canCarve) and (b) banking overlays generally, which remain the real motivator. Consider re-titling toward banking if the fallback path alone does not justify it.

title: Investigate in-place block initialization vs overlay for run-from-elsewhere copies (may need Ghidra core changes)
description: grm-1.7.1 materializes a copied region as a byte-mapped OVERLAY because the destination (e.g. $0073) already sits inside an existing uninitialized block, so a non-overlay block would conflict. This is friction: the overlay is a workaround, not the truth (those RAM bytes genuinely become the copied code). Concrete cost: under the overlay model a real call site like JSR $0073 resolves to base:$0073, NOT the overlay copy -- so references do not point at the materialized code, breaking navigation and making 'detect a call into the destination' (the code-evidence signal) unreliable for deferred-call cases like CHRGET. Investigate initializing a sub-range of an existing uninitialized block in place, or a first-class 'bytes sourced from elsewhere' relation. May require Ghidra core changes / upstream discussion.
close_reason:
RESOLVED: no Ghidra core change needed, no upstream ask, NOT an RFC #9349 item. Investigated and implemented in one pass.

FINDING: Memory.split has no initialized-ness check (MemoryMapDB.java:989-1035) and convertToInitialized is whole-block only with no sub-range variant (public or package-private), so split-then-convert is the only supported route -- and it is a blessed one, with an in-tree analyzer precedent (GolangSymbolAnalyzer.java:712-728) and a precedent in our own loader (AbstractCbmPrgLoader.createCarvedTarget:706-744).

SHIPPED: new TransferMaterializer carves the destination out of its containing uninitialized block (split x2 -> convertToInitialized(0) -> setBytes) in the base space, falling back to the previous byte-mapped overlay when the destination cannot be carved. C64CopyLoopAnalyzer reduced to recognition. The friction the bead was filed about is gone: golden copyloop.dump now pins CALLREF RAM:c000, i.e. the entering jump's primary reference resolves in the base space onto real materialized code with no bridging.

INVARIANTS enforced in code, not just documented: carving requires Transform.IDENTITY (checked redundantly in canCarve so a future decrypt unification cannot silently overwrite real encrypted bytes with a synthetic fill), and carve range == write range so no fill byte survives. Unreadable source produces nothing rather than inventing bytes or falling back to an overlay.

DOCS: docs/smc-inplace-vs-overlay.md (decision record, incl. the genuinely close rejected option C); docs/smc-runfromelsewhere-design.md sections 2/8/9 updated. Decision bead grm-7da.

TESTS: TransferMaterializerTest (10 JUnit cases: full decision matrix + 4 carve geometries + idempotence); new copyoverlay headless fixture pinning the overlay fallback and giving bridgeJump its first-ever coverage; VerifyBankTest reworked (the old dump could not distinguish base from overlay because fmt() drops the address space). Full acceptance gate green, 45 JUnit tests, 36 golden dumps, zero diffs.

DISCOVERED: grm-bqs (a destination inside a banked window carves the wrong occupant) and grm-1.7.6 (NES copy-to-$6000 real-ROM case, which also exposes a missing placement branch for a wholly UNMAPPED destination -- currently falls to overlay where a plain non-overlay initialized block would be strictly better).

title: Run-from-elsewhere: descriptor copied_from hint (Tier A / CHRGET)
description: Per-game YAML descriptor hint that declares a known boot-time copy so the loader/analyzer materializes it without pattern-matching. Parse in tools/gdtbuilder MapCompiler.buildOccupant (beside on_write); AbstractCbmPrgLoader records the hints as program metadata; C64CopyLoopAnalyzer consumes them through the same materialize() core. Because the author knows the payload, the hint carries explicit disassembly parameters that populate the TransferSpec directive directly: disassemble (bool), create_function (bool), and an optional entry address that may differ from the copy destination start (mid-block entry for headered payloads / non-zero routine offsets). Canonical case: C64 CHRGET copied to zero page $0073 from KERNAL $E3A2. Fixture can use the synthetic mkromtest.py kernal.bin (offset $3A2 = $A2) via -loader-kernalRom for deterministic initialized source bytes, no copyrighted ROM.
notes:
2026-07-25 (grm-chu): PLACEMENT POLICY IS NOW DECIDED for Tier A -- see docs/smc-inplace-vs-overlay.md and decision bead grm-7da. Three consequences for this bead:

1. ROM-GATED, NOT BEST-EFFORT. If the source ROM bytes are not readable, the directive is IGNORED -- no CHRGET copy is produced, no overlay of '??', log note only. This REVERSES docs/smc-runfromelsewhere-design.md section 8 question 2, which had recommended best-effort materialization; that question is now marked answered in the doc.

2. THIS BEAD NEEDS AN ANALYZER OR COMMAND FRONT-END, not loader-time-only work. Because the directive is ignored when the ROM is absent, the 'user supplies a KERNAL ROM later' path is only reachable if the directive can be re-evaluated after load. TransferMaterializer.materialize is idempotent (COPY_xxxx block-exists guard) and C64CopyLoopAnalyzer declares setSupportsOneTimeAnalysis, so a re-runnable front-end gets this for free -- a purely loader-time implementation makes it unreachable.

3. USE TransferMaterializer.materialize(program, spec, category, monitor, log). Do not reimplement placement. It already handles carve-vs-overlay selection, provenance, disassembly directive, and reference bridging. Emit TargetKind.SAME_SPACE unless you have a reason to force one.

NAMING NIT: this bead's title says 'copied_to', but docs/smc-runfromelsewhere-design.md section 4 defines the schema key as 'copied_from' (attached to the DESTINATION region, naming its source). Code and docs were normalized to copied_from on 2026-07-25; the bead title is the last holdout and should be renamed.
close_reason: copied_from descriptor directive shipped: MapCompiler.buildCopiedFrom with address normalization and build-failing validation (source must resolve, range inside the region, entry inside the range), machines/c64.yaml carries the CHRGET hint, and DescriptorCopyHintAnalyzer consumes it as a BYTE_ANALYZER at BLOCK_ANALYSIS priority with setSupportsOneTimeAnalysis. Analyzer not loader, because the ROM-gated rule makes 'supply the KERNAL later, re-run' the recovery path and only a re-runnable front-end reaches it. Both halves covered end to end in c64-loader against the synthetic kernal.bin: copyhinttest asserts COPY_0073 holds a2..b9, copyhintnorom asserts no block and ZEROPAGE not even split. Commit d1a8371.

title: Run-from-elsewhere: manual command/script front-end
description: The auto copy-loop recognizer (C64CopyLoopAnalyzer, grm-1.7.1 first increment) only catches loops matching its pattern. The user's workflow: after the analyzer catches what it can, the human works through the code and finds MORE copies the recognizer missed (especially complex loaders, e.g. SPC700). A user-invoked Ghidra script/command should take source/dest/size, a transform selector (identity now; constant-XOR / running-XOR later, the latter routing through grm-edg EmulationRecovery to also cover the grm-1.7.2 case), and a separate-Program flag (SPC700, grm-1.7.3). It emits a TransferSpec into the SAME materialize() core the analyzer uses, so provenance/disassembly/dual-home are shared. This is the long-tail workhorse; build quickly after the auto recognizer.
close_reason: Both front-ends shipped. ghidra_scripts/RunFromElsewhereTransfer.java (interactive ask* / headless key:value, split on ':' twice so overlay-qualified addresses survive) and RunFromElsewherePlugin (pure adapter, submits a BackgroundCommand since a Swing action holds no transaction). Both funnel through the new public RunFromElsewhere facade, as does the recognizer and the descriptor directive. Script covered headlessly by the rfemanual fixture; the plugin has NO automated regression path by construction (docs/testing.md rules out GUI test infra), which is why it holds zero logic. Commits b6328fa, 5b76946. Proven on a real target: it is what materializes Zelda's PRG-RAM copy, which the auto recognizer cannot see.

title: Real-ROM tier: megaman ref/instr counts drift (1781/7437 vs 1782/7435), fragile golden
description: The megaman (UxROM, mapper 2) real-ROM golden (grm-zai) pins refs.intoOverlay=1781 and instrs.inOverlay=7437. During grm-y20, two consecutive fresh imports both produced 1782/7435 -- a stable shift -- while the bank-> comment text stayed byte-identical (so this is unrelated to the grm-y20 comment-format change). Ghidra auto-analysis on a large real ROM (7400+ instrs) appears bistable in disassembly/ref counts (likely analysis thread-scheduling nondeterminism), making exact-count assertions in RealRomDump goldens fragile for large ROMs. Options: (a) tolerate small deltas on large-ROM count lines; (b) replace exact instrs.inOverlay/refs.intoOverlay with a coarser bucket for real ROMs; (c) root-cause the bistability. Not blocking -- real-ROM tier is opt-in, out of CI. The megaman golden is intentionally left at 1781/7437 (currently FAILs on check) pending this decision.
notes: Discovered while blessing zelda+smb3 for grm-y20; only megaman among the 12 pinned titles showed count drift. contra/wizwarr/db3/dbz2/datach/saiyan/dragonpower/shenlong all still PASS; smb SKIP (not in indexed dir).

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
2026-07-25 REPRODUCED EXACTLY, and confirmed unrelated to the grm-1.7.x work. Running the real-ROM tier on H:/emulators/nes/ROMs, megaman is the ONLY failing row, and its whole diff is:
  - REALROM count refs.intoOverlay 1781   -> 1782
  - REALROM count instrs.inOverlay 7437   -> 7435
i.e. verbatim the pair this bead already records. No COPY_ blocks are involved (the copy-loop recognizer produces none on megaman after the evidence gate landed), so nothing in the run-from-elsewhere work touches it. Deliberately NOT blessed: the value would just flip again on the next run.

Useful datum for whoever fixes this: the counts move in OPPOSITE directions (refs +1, instrs -2), which smells like an analysis-order race rather than a simple off-by-one -- one extra reference resolving into an overlay appears to cost two instructions somewhere else.

ALSO, a separate real-ROM harness bug found and FIXED this session (commit 375c4f5), which was masking everything else: realrom-test.sh never stripped CR when parsing manifest.tsv, so on a Windows CRLF checkout whichever column happened to be LAST on a row carried a trailing backslash-r into a path. That surfaced as 'golden not found: .../expected/contra.dump' for files plainly present, and made 4 of 5 supplied ROMs fail for a reason that had nothing to do with their content. If this bead was ever investigated on Windows before now, the observations may have been taken through that fog.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
2026-07-29, grm-phv: the refs.intoOverlay BASELINE for megaman has legitimately moved, so
whoever fixes this bead must re-baseline rather than compare against 1781/1782.

MosConstantReferenceAnalyzer (grm-phv) retargets indexed 6502 references from the computed
address to the addressing mode's base, which COLLAPSES N computed refs per indexed access
(one per index value the propagator resolved) into ONE base ref. Measured on this corpus:

  megaman  refs.intoOverlay  1781 (golden) -> 1704     [-77, ours]
  megaman  instrs.inOverlay  7437 (golden) -> 7435     [the pre-existing drift value this bead records]
  smb3     refs.intoOverlay   871 -> 846               [-25, ours; blessed]
  zelda    refs.intoOverlay   unchanged                 [only sample.ref 8094 moved ::8029 -> ::8028; blessed]

So megaman's instrs.inOverlay=7435 is still exactly the alternate value recorded here, NOT
something grm-phv caused -- the bistability is unchanged. Only the ref count moved, and for a
deliberate reason.

megaman.dump was deliberately NOT blessed, honoring this bead's standing decision ("the value
would just flip again on the next run"). It still FAILs on check, now with refs 1781 -> 1704
instead of 1781 -> 1782. zelda and smb3 WERE blessed (their diffs are one line each, both
explained above).

When this bead is resolved, the correct new pin for megaman is refs.intoOverlay=1704 with
instrs.inOverlay still bistable between 7435 and 7437.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
MEGAMAN BASELINE for the grm-3x1 fix (BankReachProbe.java, 2026-07-31), captured per the measure-don't-bless decision.

Probe today: sites.total 25, sites.abs 18, sites.indexed 7, sites.inFunction 24, sites.orphan 1, sites.reachable 25, sites.withWriteRef 18, sites.wouldMatchToday 18, verdict.iii invisible-reachable-sites 7.

So megaman currently resolves via its 18 absolute sites and loses all 7 indexed ones to grm-3x1. When that fix lands expect roughly +7 switch sites and a corresponding change in refs/comments/instruction counts. megaman.dump stays DELIBERATELY UNBLESSED; record the post-fix delta here rather than accepting it.

Real-ROM tier re-run 2026-07-31 with the probe attached: 10 PASS / 1 FAIL (megaman, expected) / 1 SKIP (smb) -- same as 08af5e8, so the probe itself perturbs nothing.

title: Real-ROM value-recovery gap: Bandai FCG / GxROM titles pass bank# via helper/table, so no bank values resolve
description: Found in grm-hdn real-ROM acceptance (goldens dbz2/dbz_datach/dbz_saiyan/dragonpower/shenlong). Block/overlay layout is correct on all, but every detected switch site is unrecoverable: warnings 'call to bank-switch helper FUN_xxxx whose bank argument could not be recovered at this call site' and 'mechanism write with a genuinely undeterminable value'. Result: 0 resolved bank-> comments and 0 cross-bank overlay refs on these titles -- the headline retargeting feature contributes nothing. These games load the bank number from a variable/table rather than an immediate, defeating immediate/mask-algebra recovery. This is a known value-recovery limitation class (helper-arg recovery, gib.2-style context resolution), not a descriptor bug (mappers 16/157/159/66 all layout correctly). Track as the real-ROM motivation for deeper value recovery (table/variable-fed bank args, helper-arg recovery through a stored parameter). Contrast titles where immediates work: Mega Man (UxROM) 1781 refs, wizwarr (AxROM) concrete bank->0/3/7.

title: Shippable optional real-ROM test tier (hash-pinned NES board goldens)
description: Build a reproducible, shippable-but-optional real-ROM regression tier for the NES board descriptors, feeding grm-hdn's acceptance pass. ROM binaries are NOT committed (copyright+size); they are supplied at run time via a ROM library dir. Each pinned title is identified by whole-file SHA-256 so the harness validates against the exact known-good dump and cleanly SKIPs (never falsely FAILs) when a ROM is absent or is a different/bad dump (the library has bad-dump variants with wrong mapper header bytes: Dr Mario [o4]/Tetris [b3]->m65). Deliverables: (1) tools/banktest/RealRomDump.java -- name-agnostic, read-only GhidraScript emitting a bounded/normalized/copyright-safe REALROM golden (block layout, overlay-space + ref counts, bounded samples of bank-> comments / cross-bank overlay refs / warning bookmarks, and the program SHA-256); no ROM bytes or disassembly. (2) tools/banktest/realrom/manifest.tsv pinning id/title/sha256/mapper/board/golden/loader_opts. (3) tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh check|bless <romdir...> -- standalone (NOT a run-banktest.sh chunk, NOT in build-and-test.sh 'all'), reuses build/ghidra-home isolation like measure-overlay-scale.sh, hash-indexes the library, imports via NesRomLoader + full analysis + RealRomDump postScript, diffs/bless goldens, second-layer asserts dumped sha256==manifest. (4) docs/testing.md update. Pinned set ~10-12: MMC1 zelda, MMC3 smb3, UxROM contra(+megaman), AxROM wizwarr, NROM smb, plus newly-shipped Bandai FCG (m16 Dragon Ball + 157 Datach + 159) and GxROM (Dragon Power, Shen Long no Nazo).
close_reason: grm-zai: shippable hash-pinned real-ROM test tier landed (33b2c50). grm-hdn: acceptance pass run across 12 real ROMs; per-board results recorded, 3 follow-up findings filed (grm-9oz/m95/y20).

title: Wire 'gradle test' into the acceptance gate as a fast chunk
description: Spike grm-32f.1 left the JUnit test target opt-in (not in buildExtension dependsOn, not run by build-and-test.sh). Once real (non-redundant) unit tests exist, add a 'gradle test' invocation to tools/banktest/build-and-test.sh as a selectable chunk so it gates acceptance alongside the E2E golden suite, while staying fast for the dev loop. Program-fixture tests cost ~1.5s/class (AbstractGenericTest Application bootstrap); pure tests are ~instant -- keep the chunk fast. E2E golden suite REMAINS the out-of-process acceptance authority; gradle test is additive for pure/program-fixture logic.
acceptance_criteria: build-and-test.sh exposes a unit/junit chunk that runs 'gradle test'; documented in the chunk map; full gate green.
notes: grm-32f.4 already did the BLUNT wiring: build-and-test.sh now runs the `test` task (in place of the retired verify* JavaExec tasks) for the all/basic-petscii/basic-dialects/petscii-strings/bit-algebra selections, and the full `all` gate runs it. Remaining scope for 32f.5 is the FAST/selective part: `test` is currently monolithic (runs the whole src/test/java suite wherever invoked), so a partial chunk like nes-banking pays for Ghidra-bootstrap program-fixture tests it doesn't need. Make test selection per-chunk (e.g. gradle test --tests <pattern> mapped from the chunk), and/or add a dedicated fast `unit`/`junit` chunk. The bit-algebra chunk name is now a misnomer (runs whole suite) -- consider renaming as part of this.
close_reason: Gave the JUnit suite its own selectable chunk: renamed the misnamed bit-algebra chunk to `unit` (it already ran the whole suite). `check unit` runs `gradle test` only (no extension build/install); the full `all` gate runs headless + unit. Decoupled headless chunks from JUnit (undoing grm-32f.4's blunt coupling) so a targeted dev loop pays zero JUnit cost. Deliberately skipped finer per-chunk --tests scoping (suite is small/fast; chunk->class map would be fragile). Chunk map/docs updated (build-and-test.sh, CLAUDE.md, testing.md). Full gate green; `check unit` verified standalone. Commit b43101f.

title: Migrate bespoke main()+JavaExec verifiers to JUnit @Test in the test source set
description: Spike grm-32f.1 proved the gradle test target works (Ghidra AbstractGenericTest+ProgramBuilder, JUnit4). Migrate the existing verifiers from main()+System.exit+JavaExec into JUnit @Test under src/test/java, retiring the per-verifier source sets/JavaExec tasks: bitAlgebraCheck (pure), gdtBuilder MapCompilerVerify/DescriptorCompositionVerify (pure+gson+snakeyaml), petsciiCheck (main.output+gson). CAVEAT: verifyCharsets deliberately relies on the JavaExec classpath BEING the forked JVM system classpath so Charset.forName exercises real ServiceLoader SPI discovery (build.gradle staged META-INF/services + .map resources); a Test-worker fork must be verified to exercise the same SPI path before charset moves -- flag, don't assume; may stay JavaExec if not. Do incrementally; each verifier can be its own commit. MapCompilerParsingTest (from the spike) is the reference pattern.
acceptance_criteria: Verifiers run as JUnit @Test with per-assertion reporting; old JavaExec verify* tasks removed or reduced; verifyCharsets ServiceLoader path resolved (migrated or documented why it stays); full acceptance gate still green.
close_reason: Migrated all 5 bespoke main()+JavaExec verifiers (verifyBitAlgebra/verifyMapCompiler/verifyDescriptorComposition/verifyPetsciiMapper/verifyCharsets) to JUnit4 @Test classes under src/test/java with full coverage preserved. Charset ServiceLoader caveat RESOLVED in favor of migration: Gradle Test-worker fork exercises real SPI discovery (RetroCharsetProviderTest 6/6 green). Retired the 3 check source sets + 5 verify* tasks in build.gradle; wired the  task into build-and-test.sh in their place; deleted the superseded spike MapCompilerParsingTest; refreshed docs. Full acceptance gate green (SUITE OK). Commit a748814.

title: NES/SNES .tbl per-game text tables: parser, loader option, TblStringAnalyzer
description: Split out of grm-1.4 by user decision (2026-07-19): per-game dynamic tables cannot be JVM charsets (SPI enumerates once at launch). Architecture (decided in grm-1.4 planning): (1) retromachines.text.TblTable — pure parser + longest-prefix decoder, zero Ghidra imports; MVP grammar per Nightcrawler Table File Format standard: # comments/blank lines, multi-byte HH...=text entries (longest hex match wins), /HH=[label] end-of-string tokens, [$XX] raw-byte fallback, tolerate legacy *XX= linebreak entries and trailing \n; DEFER $-control params and !/@ table switching. (2) Loader option on NesRomLoader styled after RomFileOption (path + Browse + headless arg + Preferences memory); at import store the RAW .tbl text verbatim + source filename in a dedicated Program options node ('Retro Text Table') so projects stay portable and re-analysis never needs the file. (3) TblStringAnalyzer gated on that property: decodes end-token-terminated runs via longest match; MVP output = PRE comments + bookmarks (C64BasicAnalyzer philosophy); custom dynamic datatype is a possible later phase. Verification: verifyTblParser pure-gradle task + NES fixture with golden.
acceptance_criteria: verifyTblParser passes; NES fixture golden shows decoded .tbl strings as PRE comments/bookmarks; full gate green.

title: C64 screen-code mapping family: screencode.yaml, compiler, data/screencode.map
description: Phase B of the grm-1.4 plan (can trail C-F without blocking). machines/generated/screencode.yaml: permutation rules referencing the PETSCII unicode layer (screen 0x00-0x1F <- petscii 0x40-0x5F, 0x20-0x3F identity, 0x40-0x5F <- 0x60-0x7F, 0x60-0x7F <- 0xA0-0xBF; 0x80-0xFF reverse-video -> glyph of b&0x7F, canonical low byte on encode, reverse-video lossy by design), both variants, provenance. ScreencodeCompiler reusing PetsciiCompiler expansion helpers -> data/screencode.map (unicode_variants 2x256 + encode; NO escaped layer — petcat convention does not apply to screen codes). build.gradle buildScreencodeMap task mirroring buildPetsciiMap, added to buildExtension deps and stageCharsetResources inputs. Extends verifyCharsets screencode assertions (grm-1.4.3 provider already serves these names once the map exists).
acceptance_criteria: verifyCharsets screencode checks pass; x-c64-screencode-* charsets resolve; full gate green.
close_reason: Screen-code family landed: permutation-based screencode.yaml (PRG Appendix B verified, no overrides), ScreencodeCompiler reusing PetsciiCompiler helpers, buildScreencodeMap wired, verifyCharsets full screencode checks 2067 cases, full gate SUITE OK. Reverse-video mechanism comment corrected per user (CHARROM copies, not hardware inversion).

title: gdtbuilder: extract shared harness for Verify* tools (write/check/expectError/temp-dir copied 3x)
description: From /code-review of commit cac2c16. DescriptorCompositionVerify.java's write() and check() are byte-for-byte identical to MapCompilerVerify.java's, and both main() methods share verbatim Files.createTempDirectory / try-finally / Files.walk-reverse-delete boilerplate; tools/petscii/PetsciiMapperVerify.java independently reinvents the same standalone-verify pattern. Extract a small shared VerifyHarness (write/check/expectError hook/temp-dir lifecycle) in the gdtbuilder package so a harness fix (e.g. Windows temp-dir file-lock cleanup, richer failure reporting) lands once; the next Verify* tool reuses it instead of a fourth copy.
acceptance_criteria: One shared harness used by DescriptorCompositionVerify and MapCompilerVerify (PetsciiMapperVerify optional if cross-source-set sharing is awkward); verifyDescriptorComposition, verifyPetsciiMapper, and the full build-and-test.sh check stay green.
close_reason: Extracted gdtbuilder.VerifyHarness holding the shared temp-dir lifecycle (run), write, check, and the throws-and-contains assertion tail (expectThrows). DescriptorCompositionVerify and MapCompilerVerify now delegate to it via VerifyHarness.run + static imports; their expectError/expectCompileError helpers delegate to expectThrows. Removed the duplicated write/check methods and now-unused File/Comparator imports from both. PetsciiMapperVerify left out (separate petsciiCheck source set, default package, no shared classpath, and doesn't use the temp-dir/write/check pattern) per the AC. Both verifiers print 'verification passed'; full build-and-test.sh check green; no golden churn; net -48 lines.

title: Composition validation gaps: duplicate-name guards for regions/symbols/physical; context_register typo is silent
description:
From /code-review of commit cac2c16 (grm-5zg shared fragment composition). Two verified gaps:

1. DUPLICATE-NAME GUARDS ONLY COVER types[]: list-append merge means a board-local list entry can share a name with a fragment entry. grm-5zg added GdtBuilder.validateUniqueTypeNames for types[], but memory.regions[], symbols[] set names, and physical[] names have no uniqueness check in MapCompiler — findRegion (~line 756) is first-match-wins, so a duplicate silently shadows for lookups (e.g. rom_images target/size validation) while BOTH entries are emitted into the compiled .map. A board author who adds a local region named like a fragment's (natural given 'local override' semantics for maps) gets silent wrong output. Fix: extend uniqueness validation to regions/symbols/physical at MapCompiler load, mirroring validateUniqueTypeNames; add DescriptorCompositionVerify cases.

2. TYPO'D context_register HAS ZERO DIAGNOSTIC: cac2c16 removed SCHEMA.md's documented load-time descriptor<->language agreement check ('fails with a clear error') when making context_register optional. Now MapCompiler passes any name through unchecked and BoardBankAnalyzer.stampContextRegister (~1494) silently returns when program.getRegister() is null — a typo like 'c64bnk' disables context stamping with no compile error, no log, no bookmark. Minimal fix: log a warning in stampContextRegister when the option is present but the register is undeclared by the language; better: validate at map compile time once languages are bundled (grm-bk6).
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate region/symbol-set/physical names fail map compile with a clear error (verifier case added); a context_register naming a register the language does not declare produces at least a logged warning at analysis time; full build-and-test.sh check green.
close_reason: Fixed both gaps. (1) MapCompiler now validates uniqueness of memory.regions[] names, physical[] names, and symbols[] set names via a validateUniqueNames helper mirroring GdtBuilder.validateUniqueTypeNames; duplicates fail compile with '<context> <name> is declared twice'. Added 3 MapCompilerVerify cases (dup-region/dup-physical/dup-symbol-set). (2) BoardBankAnalyzer.stampContextRegister now logs a warning via log.appendMsg when context_register is present but names a register the language does not declare (was a silent return); SCHEMA.md updated to document the warning. Compile-time cross-check deferred to grm-bk6. Full build-and-test.sh check green, no golden churn.

title: Declarative-map debt from PRG rework: inert formats section, zero-consumer load_target, hardcoded P6510, derivable PRG_* properties
description:
From /code-review of codex commit fd17727 — confirmed cleanup/altitude items, none user-visible today:

1. INERT formats SECTION: machines/c64.yaml declares formats.prg (extensions [.prg,.p00], 2-byte header, placement, initial_bank_state) and docs/SCHEMA.md (~359) documents formats.prg.placement as selecting the policy, but NO Java reads the formats section — C64PrgLoader hardcodes '.prg' (~207; the declared .p00 is not honored) and the 2-byte header (~267). Either wire the loader to read it or delete the section+docs.

2. ZERO-CONSUMER load_target: this range removed the only YAML use and the only Java reader, but MapCompiler (~216-225) still validates/passes it through and MAP_FORMAT.md (~74) / SCHEMA.md (~349-368) re-document it as 'legacy'. Delete the mechanism (maps are regenerable).

3. HARDCODED P6510: planPrgSlices (~489, also ~360) uses kind.equals("ram") || name.equals("P6510") to widen placement targets — machine geometry in Java. A declarative per-region flag in the descriptor (what load_target could have become) removes the name special case before the next machine (C128 MMU, TED) needs it.

4. DERIVABLE PRG_* PROPERTIES: persistPrgPlacement (~654-658) writes four Program-Info properties where load address, length, and wrapped are all derivable from PRG_SLICES; C64BasicAnalyzer does four Options reads to reassemble them (~111-116, 132). Persist slices only + accessors. Related: load() resolves the entry via the one-arg resolvePrgAddress which re-reads and re-parses the JSON just written (~400) instead of using live locals — and a parse failure silently drops the entry point (caught at ~427).

5. createDirectBlock (~618-634) bypasses MemoryBlockUtils (used by every sibling block path) for non-overlay slices; the raw-Memory path is only needed for slices sharing a pre-created overlay space.
acceptance_criteria: formats section either consumed or removed from yaml+docs; load_target deleted from MapCompiler+docs; P6510 special case replaced by a descriptor flag; single source of truth for PRG placement metadata; build-and-test.sh check green.

title: banktest: c000emutest duplicates emu-recovery harness/fixture and drops two criteria
description:
From /code-review of codex commit fd17727. checkC000EmuRecovery (tools/banktest/VerifyBankTest.java ~289-311) copy-pastes checkEmuRecovery's (~180-222) recipe — same EmulationRecovery construction, StopConditions.dirtyWatch+instructionFuel(10_000), IoPolicy.volatileBlocks, recoveredBytes, expected {1..8} — but silently drops the emu-not-suspect and emu-dirty-covers-target criteria the original asserts, so the new golden fixture verifies strictly less without that being visible. Likewise mkprgloadtest.py c000_emu_payload() (~50-63) duplicates mkemutest.py build() byte-for-byte except three operand bytes.

Fix: extract a shared verifyEmuRecovery(idPrefix, entry, payloadAddr) mirroring the existing verifyDecryptRecovery pattern (~340), restore the two dropped criteria to the c000 variant (then bless the expected dump), and parameterize mkemutest.build() by load address so mkprgloadtest imports it.

Minor same-file cleanups to fold in: blockAt() duplicates overlayAddr() resolution with a different missing-space policy (~1364 vs ~1432); the two fileOffset overloads can delegate (~1347/1355); checkPrgPlacement/checkPrgWrap compute describeBlock/bytesAt/fileOffset twice per block (println + criterion).
acceptance_criteria: One shared emu-recovery verifier used by both tests; c000emutest asserts suspect+dirty-coverage criteria; one payload builder parameterized by address; full build-and-test.sh check green (bless expected diffs after review).

title: C64BasicAnalyzer efficiency: per-byte address resolution and full re-work on every added() round
description:
From /code-review of codex commit fd17727. Two confirmed efficiency regressions in C64BasicAnalyzer.java:

1. PER-BYTE RESOLUTION (~lines 139, 210-213): the ByteSource lambda and the line-text loop resolve a placed Address per byte (LoadedSlice scan + AddressFactory.getAddressSpace string lookup + Address alloc + Memory.getByte), replacing the previous single bulk Memory.getBytes. ~100K+ round trips for a large PRG per invocation. The lambda also re-implements the file's own placedAddress() helper verbatim (~262-266) instead of calling it — if the fallback policy changes, the walker and annotation pass diverge. Fix: bulk-read each slice once into byte[], serve the walker from arrays; make the lambda call placedAddress().

2. NO EARLY-OUT (~line 163): the AnalyzerRunLog flag only suppresses one log line; every added() invocation still re-runs the full BASIC walk, DescriptorSupport.openGdt() disk I/O, PetsciiMapper.load(), and re-types/re-comments every line — all no-ops after the first run. As a byte-analyzer it re-fires whenever bytes are added (e.g. per DECRYPTED_ overlay). Fix: early-return (or skip the annotation phase) when the run-log/persisted state shows the work is done and inputs unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Walker reads via bulk getBytes per slice; lambda delegates to placedAddress(); repeat added() rounds skip gdt/petscii I/O and re-annotation; banktest BASIC fixtures still pass.
close_reason: Bulk-read byte cache replaces per-byte resolvePrgAddress+getByte in the walker and line-text loop; session-local RunStamp gate skips redundant added() rounds before any walk/GDT/petscii work. Full gate green, BASIC/PETSCII goldens byte-identical. Commit f2d43c0.

title: C64BasicAnalyzer: SYS argument >65535 wraps into bogus zero-page function
description: From /code-review of codex commit fd17727. renderLine (C64BasicAnalyzer.java ~359-371) accumulates the SYS decimal literal into a long with no bound check then casts to int, and markSysEntry (~285) masks with & 0xFFFF. A SYS literal above 65535 — ILLEGAL QUANTITY on real hardware — silently creates an external entry point, sys_entry label, and function at the wrapped address. Repro: '10 SYS 65600' -> function created in zero page at $0040. Fix: range-check the parsed value (0-65535) and skip/bookmark out-of-range SYS targets instead of masking.
acceptance_criteria: SYS >65535 produces no function/entry; ideally a warning bookmark; existing valid SYS fixtures unchanged.
notes: Fixed by c04ceae: SYS decimal accumulation now rejects values above 65535 before conversion, routes invalid arguments to a Note bookmark, and never wraps through markSysEntry. Dedicated c64basicoverflowtest verifies SYS 65536 yields note=true and functionAt0000=false. Focused basic-dialects suite reverified PASS on 2026-07-18.
close_reason: Fixed by c04ceae; overflow regression passes with no wrapped function and a warning Note

title: Commodore 128 machine descriptor and BASIC 7 import path
description: After PET/BASIC 4 bring-up, add a real C128 consumer for grm-1.6.1. Add a schema-2 C128 descriptor and import/loader path covering the native C128 BASIC 7 environment, reuse the CBM platform/dialect configuration established by PET, model copyright-safe ROM slots and the CPU-visible memory needed for deterministic BASIC program analysis, and add a headless fixture exercising BASIC 7 including prefixed tokens. Scope must state any deferred MMU/banked-memory fidelity explicitly rather than silently claiming full C128 hardware coverage.
design: Implement after grm-1.8. BASIC 7 is treated as a dialect superset in token-data/config architecture, while C128 hardware differences remain explicit descriptor/loader concerns.
acceptance_criteria: C128 descriptor compiles to map/GDT; loader/import path recognizes and places a native-mode PRG according to the explicitly scoped descriptor; copyright-safe ROM slots and core IO/MMU representation are present; deterministic focused headless golden proves placement and descriptor application; canonical full suite passes. BASIC 7 enum/prefix selection and detokenization are explicitly deferred to dependent grm-1.6.1.
notes:
Implementation scope: original unexpanded C128 after Z80-to-8502 native-mode handoff, static default MMU CR $00 / BASIC BANK 15 view only. Use bundled 6510:LE:16:default for the 8502-compatible $0000/$0001 port model. Recognize structurally valid BASIC PRGs at $1C01 that fit visible bank-0 RAM. Represent typed $D500-$D50B MMU and labels at always-decoded $FF00-$FF04, CPU-visible VIC-IIe/SID/VDC/CIA/color I/O, and logical visible ROM extracts. Explicitly defer dynamic MMU/common RAM/P0-P1 relocation/bank 1/RAM-under-ROM/function ROM/C64 mode/Z80/VDC RAM and BASIC 7 token decoding.
Final implementation additionally models physical bank-0 RAM occupants beneath BASIC/editor/KERNAL ROMs so a genuine linked BASIC PRG can span $1C01-$FEFF; dynamic MMU switching, runtime access chronology, and RAM-under-ROM write behavior remain deferred. Focused golden passes placement, prefix-byte preservation, ROM, MMU shadow/volatility, and 8502/VIC-IIe/SID/MMU/VDC/CIA type criteria; canonical full suite passes.
close_reason: Implemented scoped native C128 descriptor and loader with bank-0 BASIC placement through $FEFF, logical ROM slots, typed core IO/MMU, MMU-shadow symbols, deterministic headless golden, and full-suite regression coverage.

title: Commodore PET machine descriptor and BASIC 4 import path
description: Bring up a real PET consumer before grm-1.6.1. Add a schema-2 PET descriptor for a representative BASIC 4 machine, including CPU-visible RAM/IO/ROM layout, PETSCII/BASIC configuration seams, generated map/GDT artifacts, and an import/loader path suitable for tokenized BASIC programs. Keep ROMs copyright-safe via user-supplied slots. Hardware facts must be sourced and documented; add a deterministic headless fixture that proves program placement and descriptor application. This prerequisite should establish the reusable CBM platform shape that C128 can extend without hard-coding BASIC dialect logic in Java.
design: Implement PET first as requested by the user. Prefer descriptor composition/shared fragments for reusable CBM definitions; choose and document one concrete PET model/BASIC 4 memory map rather than claiming incompatible PET variants.
acceptance_criteria: PET 4032 descriptor compiles to map/GDT; loader/import path recognizes and places a PRG according to the descriptor; copyright-safe ROM slots and core IO/register types are represented; deterministic focused headless golden proves placement and descriptor application; canonical full suite passes. BASIC 4 dialect selection/detokenization is explicitly deferred to dependent grm-1.6.1.
notes:
Implementation scope fixed to the later 12-inch CRTC PET 4032: MOS 6502, 32 KiB, 40-column graphics keyboard, BASIC 4 ROM map; excludes early/non-CRTC 4032-9, 4032B business keyboard, 4016/8032/8096/8296/SuperPET. PRG placement target is . Architecture: shared descriptor-driven CBM PRG loader base with thin C64/PET opinions; PET loader conservatively claims structurally valid  PRGs; compiled descriptor path persisted as future grm-1.6.1 dialect seam; BASIC 4 tokens/detokenization remain deferred.
Final implementation: PET 4032 uses physical SCREEN_RAM $8000-$83FF plus documented SCREEN_MIRROR $8400-$87FF alias limitation; conservative tokenized PRG recognition at $0401; shared CBM loader preserves legacy C64 Program Info keys and external-entry behavior; fixed-region ROM slots validated and formats preserved in compiled maps. PET focused golden passes 10/10 criteria; affected C64/PET regressions and canonical full suite pass.
close_reason: Implemented PET 4032 descriptor, shared descriptor-driven CBM PRG loader, fixed ROM slot/schema support, typed PET IO, and deterministic headless golden; full suite passes.

title: Decide c64ref sourcing: git submodule + build-time generation vs committed generated files
description: grm-hnm adds a Python generator (tools/gensymbols/) that converts mist64/c64ref reference data into machines/generated/c64ref-*.yaml symbol files. Decide how c64ref is sourced for the build: (a) CURRENT APPROACH -- generator + COMMITTED generated/*.yaml; c64ref is a manual/dev-time input (cloned ad hoc to D:/git/c64ref), the generated YAMLs are committed static files (matching the existing committed generated/*.yaml pattern), regenerated by manually re-running the generator when c64ref updates; the build does NOT depend on c64ref being present. (b) SUBMODULE -- add mist64/c64ref as a git submodule and run the generator as a Gradle task at build time, so symbols are always regenerated from pinned-upstream source; pros: always in sync, reproducible from source, no stale committed artifacts; cons: couples the build to submodule checkout (network/size), a large reference repo vendored, generator must run every build, licensing/provenance of the vendored data travels with the repo. Trade-off is build reproducibility/freshness vs build simplicity + reviewable committed artifacts. Consider licensing (c64ref is clean-ish but individual source texts have book provenance) and whether upstream churns. Defer until the generator + first generated sets (grm-hnm) land, then choose. User-requested capture 2026-07-13.

title: C64 loader: option to import fully pre-analyzed/labeled/commented ROM (not just raw bytes)
description: Beyond grm-mbm (which loads raw KERNAL/BASIC/CHARGEN ROM BYTES into initialized blocks), offer an option to import the ROM already DISASSEMBLED, ANALYZED, LABELED, and COMMENTED -- so the user gets a fully-annotated KERNAL/BASIC without re-running analysis or hand-annotating. NEEDS STRATEGIZING (design doc first): (1) SOURCE of the annotated data -- a Ghidra GZF/archive export of a pre-analyzed ROM Program; a c64ref-derived labels+comments dataset applied over the loaded bytes (ties to the c64ref symbol work); a saved sidecar (VICE .sym + comments, or CSV) of labels/comments/disasm ranges; or a bundled reference Program. (2) MECHANISM -- overlay saved analysis (functions/labels/comments/disassembly markup) onto the loaded ROM blocks at import, vs shipping a separate pre-built Program the loader references. (3) PROVENANCE/LICENSING of the annotation source (KERNAL disassembly comments may be encumbered -- cf. c64_ghidra/Leemon concerns noted in grm-1.2). (4) COMPOSITION with grm-mbm raw-ROM load and grm-1.7.1 dual-home (byte-mapped copies would inherit the ROM's annotations for free). Likely a loader option + an analysis-applier, or an offered .gzf. User idea captured 2026-07-13; strategize before implementing.

title: C64 loader: optionally populate KERNAL/BASIC/CHARGEN ROM regions from user-supplied ROM files
description: Today the c64.yaml ROM regions ($A000-$BFFF BASIC, $E000-$FFFF KERNAL, CHARGEN) are created but NOT populated with bytes (the copyrighted ROMs are not bundled), so ROM code is undisassemblable and ROM-sourced data is unavailable. Add an OPTIONAL path for the user to supply their own ROM dump files at load time, which the loader reads into the corresponding ROM regions as initialized blocks. Mechanism options: Ghidra Loader options (Loader.getDefaultOptions -> user-visible import options carrying file paths), or a post-load script/analyzer that reads paths from a config and Memory.setBytes/createFileBytes into the ROM blocks. Keep it optional: absent ROM files -> current behavior (uninitialized ROM regions), no regression. Benefits: (1) ROM routines (KERNAL/BASIC entry points) become disassemblable and callable-into from user code; (2) ENABLES the ROM-sourced dual-home case in grm-1.7.1 -- the canonical CHRGET->$73 fixture needs the BASIC ROM CHRGET source bytes present so a createByteMappedBlock at $0073 can share them. Until this lands, grm-1.7.1 must start with the PRG-internal copy case (source in the loaded program) rather than CHRGET-from-ROM. Relates to C64PrgLoader / DescriptorSupport region creation and machines/c64.yaml ROM region definitions. Filed at user request during grm-1.7.1 (2026-07-13).
notes: 2026-07-13 IMPLEMENTED + headless-tested (commit 5c60bca). C64PrgLoader initializes BASIC/KERNAL/CHARGEN ROM blocks from user-supplied dumps. New RomFileOption (editable path text field per user request -- type/paste directly -- plus Browse via local-filesystem GhidraFileChooser, NOT DomainFileOption's project DataTreeDialog). getDefaultOptions/validateOptions add 3 ROM-path options (existence + exact size 0x2000/0x2000/0x1000). createWindowOccupant -> createRomBlock initializes a FileBytes-backed block (FileByteProvider, since RandomAccessByteProvider is deprecated-for-removal) when the occupant descriptor image has a supplied path; else uninitialized (unchanged, backward compatible). Persistence: paths saved to ghidra Preferences (retromachines.c64.{kernal,basic,chargen}RomPath) + pre-filled next import -- GUI ONLY; headless/CLI neither reads nor writes prefs (gated on !SystemUtilities.isInHeadlessMode()) per user requirement. CLI: each option carries the FULL -loader-<name> arg (Loader.COMMAND_LINE_ARG_PREFIX; LoaderArgsOptionChooser.choose matches the whole flag against Option.getArg() case-insensitively -- a bare arg name is silently 'unsupported', caught by the headless test). TEST: banktest romload imports romload.prg with -loader-{kernal,basic,chargen}Rom pointing at synthetic 8192/8192/4096-byte pattern files; asserts each block initialized with its pattern (KERNAL b0=00/b3A2=A2 = CHRGET location, BASIC b0=55, CHARGEN b0=AA). Verifies the CLI option path directly; full suite green, no golden drift. REMAINING (manual, not headless-automatable): GUI verification of the Browse button, editable-field UX, and Preferences pre-fill/save across imports -- these use verified Ghidra patterns (DomainFileOption structure, GhidraFileChooser, GhidraFileChooser.savePreferences model) but need a running GUI to confirm.

C64PrgLoader loads user-supplied BASIC/KERNAL/CHARGEN dumps into initialized FileBytes blocks; RomFileOption editable field + local GhidraFileChooser; paths persisted to ghidra Preferences (GUI only, not CLI/headless); full -loader-<name> command-line args. Commit 5c60bca. Unblocks grm-1.7.1 Tier-A CHRGET dual-home.

title: grm-1.7.2 tier 2: test emulation-assisted decrypt of a rolling/computed-key loop
description: C64DecryptLoopAnalyzer.apply() already routes a ROLLING/COMPUTED KeyModel (EOR keytab,X etc.) with AUTO confidence to the grm-edg EmulationRecovery harness (dirty-watch on the target range, IoPolicy.volatileBlocks) and materializes the read-back bytes via the shared overlay path -- but NO banktest fixture exercises this path, so tier 2 is wired but unverified. Add a rolling-key decrypt .prg fixture (e.g. LDA base,X / EOR keytab,X / STA base,X / DEX / BPL with a JMP into range and a small key table) + a VerifyBankTest branch asserting the emulated recovery produces the correct plaintext overlay and, if the loop reads only initialized RAM, a NOTE (not SUSPECT/WARNING) bookmark. Also cover the SUSPECT path: a loop whose key derives from an IO/uninitialized read should still recover bytes but get a WARNING bookmark (provenance.suspect()). Parent grm-1.7.2 tier 1 is done+tested (commit 2d3815f); this closes the tier-2 verification gap.
close_reason: Tier-2 emulation-assisted decrypt verified end-to-end for BOTH outcomes. Rolling-key happy path (EOR keytab,X, initialized RAM): analyzer routes to grm-edg EmulationRecovery, runs the loop in the p-code emulator during analysis, reads back plaintext 01..08 under dirty-watch, materializes DECRYPTED_2019 with a trusted NOTE. Suspect path (EOR $DC00,X CIA register): emulator answers the hardware read with a policy value, provenance logs an IO read, analyzer recovers bytes (=ciphertext) but downgrades to a WARNING. Deterministic; full banktest suite green in check mode, no existing golden changed. Commits 58d3c03 (rolling), 2aa079b (suspect). (Force-closed: the blocking dep was the parent feature grm-1.7.2 this task verifies; verification is complete.)

title: C64 memory map: let a PRG load at any RAM address, not just RAM_MAIN ($0800-$9FFF)
description: The c64.yaml descriptor's load_target region RAM_MAIN is only $0800-$9FFF, so C64PrgLoader can only carve a PRG into the base address space when its load address falls in that window. A PRG loading elsewhere in real C64 RAM -- e.g. $C000 (the 4K RAM block), or RAM-under-ROM ($A000-$BFFF BASIC, $E000-$FFFF KERNAL) or RAM-under-IO ($D000-$DFFF) -- conflicts with the base block already mapped there and the loader falls back to placing the PRG in a NEW OVERLAY space instead of base RAM. Consequences: (1) the program's bytes are not where a naive base-space consumer expects them; surfaced concretely by grm-edg's EmulationRecovery fixture, whose $C000-loaded PRG landed in an overlay so EmulatorUtilities.loadProgram (which copies each block into ITS space) left base $C000 uninitialized -> immediate decode fault. Worked around by loading the fixture at $2000 (inside RAM_MAIN), but that is a fixture band-aid, not a fix. Rethink the C64 RAM modeling so a PRG can load at ANY RAM address: options to weigh -- (a) model all RAM regions ($0000-$9FFF, $C000-$CFFF, and the RAM-under-ROM/IO banks) as load_target-eligible base RAM so createRamMainSplit can carve the PRG wherever it lands; (b) make the loader prefer carving PRG into whichever base RAM region contains the load address rather than only the single load_target region; (c) represent the C64's RAM-vs-ROM/IO banking so RAM-under-ROM loads map correctly. Relates to C64PrgLoader.createRamMainSplit / createPrgBlock and c64.yaml region layout. Discovered during grm-edg (2026-07-12).
design:
Use the existing home-in-base plus alternate-overlay representation, but replace the singleton RAM_MAIN carve with a descriptor-derived, 16-bit PRG routing plan.

1. Treat import as static CPU-address image placement, not KERNAL LOAD emulation. Accept payload lengths 1..65536. Destination of payload byte i is (loadAddr+i)&$FFFF. Reject >65536 before Program mutation because destinations repeat. Split wrapping input into at most two ordered source spans: [loadAddr,$FFFF] from FileBytes offset 2, then [$0000,end] from the following file offset. Preserve file order/source offset in segment metadata.
2. Partition each span at descriptor memory boundaries. Eligible physical targets are direct top-level kind:ram regions, the direct kind:ram occupant of each enumerated bank window, plus the special P6510 region for bytes at $0000/$0001. Nested IO subregions (including COLOR_RAM) are not PRG RAM targets. Reject uncovered or ambiguously covered ranges before mutation.
3. Create FileBytes once. Materialize every slice as a real initialized FileBytes-backed block at the span-derived source offset, with uninitialized prefix/suffix fragments for its target. Always-visible RAM ($0002-$9FFF and $C000-$CFFF) stays in base. RAM beneath BASIC/IO/KERNAL goes into RAM_A000/RAM_D000/RAM_E000 occupant overlay space. Preserve initial BASIC/IO/KERNAL in base and preserve overlay-space names for BoardBankAnalyzer.
4. If the image touches $0000/$0001, initialize those bytes in the P6510 region while preserving IO permissions, volatility, and R6510 typing. Emit a prominent warning/property: this records address-visible register values only; it does not simulate loader chronology, infer bank state from $01/DDR, or change descriptor initial banking. A load starting at either register gets load-start metadata/label but no executable function entry.
5. Eliminate the separate createPrgBlock conflict-fallback path. Use direct Memory creation or assert conflict-free placement; MemoryBlockUtils's initialized helper silently creates an unrelated overlay on conflict, which caused this bug.
6. Persist original load address, payload length, wrapped flag, and ordered slice records (file offset, length, address space, start) in Program Information. Keep PRG as the first slice name when practical, but migrate C64BasicAnalyzer from its single-base-block assumption. Skip BASIC sniff/detokenization for wrapped images because its monotonic interval model is not meaningful there.
7. Place entry label/function at the first slice's real address space: base:$C000 for visible RAM, RAM_A000::$A000 under BASIC, etc. Warn for an entry hidden by initial bank state. The original load address remains the placement origin even when later bytes wrap.
8. Update SCHEMA/MAP_FORMAT: C64 placement is derived from direct physical RAM targets; singleton load_target is a legacy RAM_MAIN implementation detail. formats.prg.placement:load_address remains authoritative.

Reject a single 64K base RAM block: it displaces initial BASIC/IO/KERNAL and regresses references such as JSR $FFD2. Also reject a 64K physical overlay plus byte-mapped CPU views for this bead: Ghidra 12.1.2 byte-mapped blocks report isInitialized=false and EmulatorUtilities.loadProgram skips them; listings/symbols and emulator writes do not share alias identity. Revisit a true physical RAM space only with first-class L4/context-aware resolution.

Acceptance: preserve $0801 behavior; add $C000 EmulationRecovery; $A000/$D000/$E000 placement and home-in-base checks; base/base and base/window boundary slicing; wrap fixtures $FFFE+2 (no wrap), $FFFE+3, and $FFFC+8 (RAM_E000 -> P6510 -> ZEROPAGE) with exact FileBytes offsets; exactly 64KiB accepted; 65537 rejected without partial layout; touching $01 leaves banking.initial_state/home occupants unchanged. Document the rare representation limit for instructions/fallthrough straddling a base/overlay boundary.
notes:
2026-07-15 design investigation completed with three lower-tier read-only reviews (loader/map, architecture/beads, Ghidra block APIs). Consensus: generalized direct carving is the smallest hardware-truthful solution. Related beads considered: grm-edg (originating $C000 acceptance case), grm-1.7.1 (byte-mapped dual-home work; coordinate loader surface), grm-hqa (future snapshot import can reuse RAM routing), grm-wkk/grm-5tl (future L4 architecture, not blockers), grm-rua (default block noise only), grm-54p/grm-mbm (ROM coexistence), and closed grm-5tl.14/grm-1.3 (singleton load_target and home-in-base decisions being refined). No new dependency is required.
2026-07-15 user correction: real PRGs can wrap past $FFFF and place takeover vectors in low RAM (e.g. around $0300). Design revised to support modulo-64K static placement for payloads up to 64KiB instead of rejecting wrap. Wrapped $0000/$0001 bytes are retained as P6510 register values with a warning; full loader/banking chronology remains explicitly out of scope.
close_reason: Implemented descriptor-derived arbitrary C64 PRG placement with FileBytes-backed base/underlay slices, modulo-64K wrap through P6510 and low RAM, persisted placement metadata, overlay-aware BASIC analysis/entries, documentation, and regression fixtures for A/C/D/E placement, wrapped takeover-vector bytes/source offsets, home occupants, and C000 emulation. Full banktest suite passes.

close_reason: GO. Spike proved a gradle 'test' target on Ghidra's own shipped scaffolding works headless against the binary install: 'gradle test' green, 11 methods, 0 skipped. Pure JUnit for pure logic (BankStateTest 6 tests/0.001s; MapCompilerParsingTest 3/0.08s incl gson+snakeyaml) and AbstractGenericTest+ProgramBuilder('6502:LE:16:default') for Program fixtures (BankStrategyProgramTest 2/1.535s -- Application bootstrap + real RegisterWriteBankSwitchStrategy->StoredValueScanner path; bare ProgramBuilder disassembly gives STA $01 its write ref, no analysis pass needed). title: Testing strategy: golden-image E2E + unit-level framework + suite partitioning
description:
High-level testing strategy for the extension. CURRENT STATE (assessed 2026-07-12, mostly fine for now): end-to-end golden-image regression via tools/banktest/run-banktest.sh check|bless — python generators synthesize test PRGs/ROMs, analyzeHeadless imports with the real loaders, VerifyBankTest.java (~1000 lines) checks criteria and diffs normalized behavior dumps against expected/; build-and-test.sh adds per-worktree isolated extension installs; sibling checkers for petscii and bit algebra. No JUnit anywhere — subagents repeatedly burn time hunting for a framework that does not exist.

THREE QUESTIONS this epic resolves:
(1) UNIT LAYER: would a framework (JUnit via Ghidra's own extension test support — AbstractGenericTest, ProgramBuilder program-fixture classes, gradle test integration) simplify test creation long-term for unit-level testing (MapCompiler parsing, StoredValueScanner bit algebra, strategy dispatch) IN ADDITION TO — not replacing — the E2E golden suite? E2E stays the acceptance authority: it exercises the real loader+analyzer stack headlessly, which unit fixtures cannot.
(2) PARTITIONING/SPEED: split the suite into related chunks (c64-banking / nes-banking / basic+petscii / bit-algebra / per-tool) so that during active development a subset relevant to the current change runs fast and often, while FULL suite passing still gates final acceptance and commits. Needs a selection mechanism (per-chunk driver args or tags) + a documented convention for which chunk covers what.
(3) LEGIBILITY: document the strategy (docs/testing.md + AGENTS.md pointer) so agents and contributors find the harness instead of searching for junit/gradle-test scaffolding that is not there.

Guiding principle: same priority order as everything else — use existing infrastructure first (Ghidra ships JUnit test scaffolding for extensions), mirror how Ghidra's own tree tests analyzers where applicable, roll our own only with recorded justification.
close_reason: All 5 children complete. Testing strategy established: 3 tiers (pure JUnit / AbstractGenericTest+ProgramBuilder / E2E golden image), suite partitioned into selectable chunks (full 'all' gates acceptance), documented in docs/testing.md + AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md pointers, all bespoke main()+JavaExec verifiers migrated to JUnit @Test, and the JUnit suite exposed as its own fast 'unit' chunk while E2E golden remains the out-of-process acceptance authority.

title: EmulationRecovery harness: bounded PcodeEmulator run + dirty-set capture + descriptor-driven IO policy
description: Shared bounded-emulation core decided by the grm-1.7.4 survey (docs/smc-survey.md par.6): given entry address + stop conditions (breakpoint set / exit-range / dirty-watch / instruction fuel / wall-clock) + IO policy sourced from the board descriptor (IO regions -> readUninitialized + beforeLoad behavior), run the interpreted PcodeEmulator over the current Program image (EmulatorUtilities.loadProgram) and return {dirty address set, recovered bytes, stop reason, provenance log incl. IO-read and uninitialized-RAM warnings}. Callers decide materialization (patch / overlay / byte-mapped block / new Program). Serves grm-1.7.2 tier 2, grm-1.7.3 generic uploader tier, and future banking L4 emulator integration (same PcodeEmulationCallbacks layer as vision-board-banking.md par.7.1). NOT JitPcodeEmulator (SMC-unsafe passages).
notes: 2026-07-12 IMPLEMENTED + TESTED. Shipped retromachines.EmulationRecovery + support types (src/main/java/retromachines/): EmulationRecovery (core), StopConditions (fuel/wallclock/exit-range/dirty-watch), StopReason, IoPolicy (interface + volatileBlocks(Program) default deriving IO-ness from descriptor-set block volatility), ProvenanceLog (IO_READ/UNINIT_RAM_READ/WARNING/INFO + suspect()), RecoveryResult (dirty AddressSetView + per-range readback + recoveredBytes(start,len)). Uses interpreted ghidra.pcode.emu.PcodeEmulator (NOT Jit -- SMC-safe by re-decode). API verified against the actual 12.1.2 install (Emulation-src.zip), NOT the D:/git/ghidra checkout which is 12.2. KEY CORRECTNESS FINDING: the concrete BytesPcodeExecutorStateSpace calls the Address-based dataWritten and the AddressSetView-based readUninitialized (via PcodeEmulationCallbacks.Wrapper injecting thread; null for shared state) -- overriding the other members of each overload pair compiles but silently never fires. Capture is gated by a 'capturing' flag flipped true only after loadProgram+initializeRegisters so setup writes don't pollute the dirty set; register/unique writes filtered by isMemorySpace(). TEST (option b per grm-32f, since JUnit/ProgramBuilder test jars are not shipped in the public install): tools/banktest/mkemutest.py generates a constant-EOR in-place decrypt .prg; VerifyBankTest.java emurecoverytest branch drives the harness and asserts stop=DIRTY_WATCH, recovered=01..08, not suspect, dirty covers target; golden tools/banktest/expected/emurecoverytest.dump (STEPS 39). Full suite green in check mode. NOTE: fixture loads at $2000 (inside RAM_MAIN) because the C64 map only carves PRGs into base space within $0800-$9FFF; a $C000 load lands in an overlay that loadProgram copies to a different space -> filed grm-dvx to let PRGs load at any RAM address. Unblocks grm-1.7.2 tier 2.
close_reason: EmulationRecovery bounded-emulation harness implemented and tested end-to-end. retromachines.EmulationRecovery + StopConditions/StopReason/IoPolicy/ProvenanceLog/RecoveryResult, on interpreted PcodeEmulator (SMC-safe), API verified against the real 12.1.2 install. Dirty-set capture uses the two callback overloads the concrete state actually invokes (Address dataWritten + AddressSetView readUninitialized via the thread-injecting Wrapper), gated post-load. Descriptor-sourced IO policy via block volatility feeds provenance (IO/uninit-RAM reads -> suspect()). Regression: banktest emurecoverytest fixture (constant-EOR decrypt .prg) green in check mode (stop=DIRTY_WATCH, recovered=01..08, not suspect). Follow-up grm-dvx filed for C64 any-address PRG load. Unblocks grm-1.7.2 tier 2 and grm-1.7.3 generic uploader tier.
