title: SelectDataBankSwitchStrategy: override depositHelperArgument (route via tracked select at call-site in-state)
description: Found during grm-6a7.2: a bare data-write-only MMC3 helper (STA $8001 with arg in A) is classified a helper with argReg='A' and the WHOLE select-data mechanism width, and call-site recovery uses depositHelperArgument's DEFAULT (deposit across full width) because SelectDataBankSwitchStrategy does not override it — misrepresenting the call as writing select+prg_mode+r6+r7 at once. Correct behavior mirrors serial-shift's override, but with a twist: the target depends on the TRACKED SELECT at the call site's in-state, not the switch site's address — the override signature receives the switch site but the deposit must dispatch on the caller's in-state select value (check what recoverCallArgument passes; may need the call-site in-state plumbed into depositHelperArgument — evaluate whether the existing signature suffices [switchSite + argValue + stateMask] or needs an inState parameter added with a default-preserving overload). Select known -> deposit only the targeted field (ownedMask = that field); select unknown -> ownedMask = r6|r7 with nothing known (honest poison); CHR select -> ownedMask=0 no-op. Fixture: extend nesmmc3test2 (H's callers already set up the known/unknown select contexts — add criteria on the recovered annotation values).
notes: Filed 2026-07-11 from grm-6a7.2 report item 3. Interacts with grm-6a7.2's requiresOnEntry (a proper override reduces the over-wide effectMask that also feeds modifiedMask). USER ASSESSMENT (2026-07-12): bare data-write-only helpers are probably rare-to-nonexistent in real MMC3 games -- a JSR wrapping a single STA wastes cycles when you're racing the beam, so real helpers almost certainly set select+data together. Still worth implementing for mask-width precision (the over-wide default effectMask pollutes summaries/modifiedMask even for the common two-write helper shape). Treat as precision cleanup, not an expected real-game bug; keep P3.
close_reason: Implemented SelectDataBankSwitchStrategy.depositHelperArgument override with state-routed dispatch. Signature grew a field-local inState param (BankSwitchStrategy interface + default + SerialShift override, which ignores it -- its routing is address-keyed); BoardBankAnalyzer.recoverCallArgument localizes runDataflow's outState into the helper mechanism's field space and passes it down. Override: even switchSite (select-write helper) deposits select+mode fields from the arg byte; odd (data-write helper) dispatches on fieldValueIfFullyKnown(inState, selectField) -- known+tracked routes to that one target field (ownedMask = field alone), known+CHR = verified no-op (ownedMask=0, no comment/no warning), unknown = honest poison of all configured target fields only (never select/prg_mode). Fixture nesmmc3test2 extended with CallerC (CHR no-op) and CallerD (R7 routing); criteria G4-G7 added; G1-G3 unchanged. Golden re-blessed for nesmmc3test2 only: e107 went from the fabricated select=2 to fully-known select=6/r6=2; e128's false select=3 comment gone (wholly-unknown deposit takes warning branch; pre-existing requiresOnEntry warning bookmark stands). RESIDUAL (per-item-6 check): requiresOnEntry/modifiedMask function-summary width is built from each function's own switch sites' effectMask, not CallEffect.ownedMask, so H's own summary stays mechanism-wide -- unaffected by this fix, still the grm-6a7.2 over-approximation. Suite: SUITE OK (check), 12/12, all pre-existing goldens byte-identical.

title: PETSCII mapping core: data-driven byte->display-string API (unblocks BASIC detokenizer)
description: The subset of grm-1.4 that grm-odt.1 (BASIC detokenizing analyzer) needs — scoped deliberately to unblock it without the NES/SNES tile-table half or Ghidra Charset registration (those stay on the parent). Deliverables per the design inputs recorded on grm-1.4: (1) a Java-callable PETSCII byte->display-string API (e.g. PetsciiMapper), usable outside Ghidra's charset/string-search machinery, for programmatic comment-text building; (2) both charset variants (unshifted/graphics and shifted/lowercase) selectable per call; (3) a STABLE escaped rendering convention for control/graphics bytes ({CLR}, {RVS ON}, {c-A}-style — pick, document, freeze: it lands in golden dumps); (4) mapping data lives in a DATA file (machines/generated/ or data/, following basic-tokens.yaml / c64ref precedent), not hardcoded Java, and is shaped so future Ghidra Charset registration (parent bead) reads the same source; (5) screen codes explicitly OUT of scope here (separate mapping, parent bead). Include a small unit-test-style verification (builder-adjacent or a tiny JUnit if the repo has test infra — check; if none, a verify main() like GdtBuilder's pattern). API should be reachable from analyzer code (src/main/java/retromachines/).
design: BRIEF (scouted 2026-07-11; petcat escape tables archived at scratchpad/petscii-escapes.md). ESCAPE CONVENTION: adopt VICE petcat's SHORT ctrl1[]/ctrl2[] bracket names verbatim ({wht},{down},{rvon},{clr},{F1}..{F8},...) for $00-$1F/$80-$9F, and petcat's {$xx} lowercase-hex fallback for EVERYTHING else non-printable — including the $A0-$FF graphics range (do NOT invent names; do NOT use petcat's cbmkeys[] key-combo names — input-oriented, not glyph-oriented). Interop win: our detokenized comments re-tokenize through petcat. MUST re-pull petcat.c from canonical VICE (vice-emu.sourceforge.io or vice-emu GitHub mirror) to verify ctrl1/ctrl2 verbatim BEFORE freezing — this lands in golden dumps. UNICODE POLICY v1: none — ASCII bracket escapes only (U+1FB00 legacy-computing glyphs deferred as a future optional toDisplayUnicode(); font/rendering nondeterminism is a golden-stability risk). DATA PATH: machines/generated/petscii.yaml (source of truth, both variants, screen codes explicitly excluded) -> NEW small build tool (sibling of MapCompiler — MapCompiler is hard-bound to schema-2 machine descriptors, confirmed trap, do not reuse) -> gitignored data/petscii.map JSON -> runtime Application.findDataFileInAnyModule + gson (DescriptorSupport.loadMap pattern; consider generalizing its private JSON-load helper). Wire buildPetsciiMap into buildExtension deps; add artifact to .gitignore. API: final class PetsciiMapper, flat in retromachines/ (package is flat, no util/), enum Variant {UNSHIFTED_GRAPHICS, SHIFTED_LOWERCASE}, toDisplayEscaped(int,Variant) + toDisplayEscaped(byte[],Variant), cached load(), zero Ghidra-type deps beyond Application/gson. VERIFY: repo has NO JUnit — follow tools/bitalgebra/BitAlgebraEquivalence pattern exactly (standalone main() + own sourceSet + verifyPetsciiMapper gradle task), EXHAUSTIVE 0x00-0xFF x 2 variants (non-null everywhere, petcat-named bytes match frozen table, fallback format exactly {$xx}).
notes: Filed 2026-07-11 at user request ('work on grm-1.4, getting it far enough along to unblock odt.1'). Queue: next unit after the in-flight grm-hsv.2 helper fix lands.

PetsciiMapper: flat retromachines/, Variant enum, load() via existing DescriptorSupport.loadMap (already generic — no new helper) + loadFromMapFile(File) verifier seam. ASCII-divergence policy: $5C(£)->backslash, $5E->^, $5F->_ (petcat verbatim); $60-$7F/$A0-$FF uniformly {$xx}. title: SMC: survey — Ghidra Debugger/p-code emulator leverage for self-modifying code recovery
description: Research bead, feeds all three use-case children: what can Ghidra's Debugger-era machinery (PcodeEmulator, TraceRmi, emulation scripts, 'Emulate' UI) do for us headlessly and programmatically in 12.1+? Questions: (1) can we run a bounded p-code emulation of a copy/decrypt loop over program bytes WITHOUT a live target (pure emulator, no gdb/frida), capture resulting memory, and write it back into the static Program (or a Trace snapshot converted to Program view)? (2) what are the fuel/termination controls (max instructions, memory faults on unmapped IO reads — retro code touches IO registers constantly; need a fault policy: zero-fill vs abort)? (3) is Trace/snapshot the right persistence for 'memory image after boot-init ran', navigable alongside the static view? (4) precedents: existing Ghidra scripts/plugins doing emulation-assisted unpacking (search ghidra repo + community, e.g. malware-unpacking workflows — same problem shape as C64 decrypt-on-the-fly). Deliverable: written findings on the epic + go/no-go per use case (static vs emulated vs manual).
notes: Filed 2026-07-11. Do this survey FIRST when epic work starts — it decides the approach split for all three children.

Verdicts: 1.7.1 static (byte-mapped blocks), 1.7.2 emulation-assisted pilot on PcodeEmulator, 1.7.3 static-first (.spc + IPL parse; SPC700 sleigh NOT in stock Ghidra). title: SMC: SNES SPC700 upload — cross-processor code extraction to a separate Program
description: Use case 3: SNES games upload SPC700 sound-driver code/data through the APU IO ports ($2140-$2143 handshake protocol) into the sound processor's OWN 64K address space and run it there. Different processor (SPC700 vs 65816), different address space — Ghidra Programs are single-language, so the right deliverable is arguably a SEPARATE Program: recognize/parse the upload (boot-ROM IPL handshake protocol blocks: address+length+data records, well documented on fullsnes/nesdev-adjacent references), extract the transferred image, and materialize a new SPC700-language Program in the project (headless: Program creation API; GUI: an action/script), cross-linked to the source Program (bookmarks/comments at the upload site naming the generated Program and vice versa). STRONG GME TIE-IN: this is exactly the AKAO SNES sound-driver code (FF2/FF3/CT dumpspc.pl lineage in game-music-extraction) — the extracted Program is the disassembly target for the music-driver reverse engineering that motivates the whole toolchain. Design questions: one Program per upload session vs per unique image (games re-upload variants); IPL protocol variants vs game-specific upload loops (AKAO games use their own uploader after boot); where the 'separate Program' convention gets documented for other cross-CPU cases (C64 1541 drive code upload is the same shape!).
notes: 2026-07-12 (user direction) DELIVERABLE SHAPE CORRECTION: output is a SINGLE SPC700 Program (one 64K sound-RAM image) alongside the SNES ROM (65816) Program — NOT one Program per uploaded image. A typical game runs the IPL MULTIPLE times to load separate portions of the SAME SPC700 RAM (e.g. one IPL load transfers the SPC700 driver code, another static instrument/sample data, another filter/echo settings). Recovery model = accumulate ALL IPL transfers into the one SPC700 RAM image at their target addresses (same shape as a fully-populated .spc snapshot). Each ROM-side upload site gets a bookmark cross-linking to the target range it populated. One-language-per-Program still puts SPC700 in its own Program (separate from 65816 ROM), but exactly ONE per game, built from N uploads. Updated docs/smc-survey.md par.5 (grm-1.7.3 Deliverable shape bullet) to match.

title: SMC: run-from-elsewhere — ROM->RAM copy recognition and dual-home code mapping
description: Use case 1: code copied from ROM to RAM and executed there (NES games copy hot loops/NMI stubs to RAM; C64 BASIC copies CHRGET to zero page $73 for speed; C64 games copy loaders under ROM shadows). The 'easy' one-to-one case: recognize the copy loop (source range, dest range, length — the same StoredValueScanner/idiom machinery the banking strategies use can find LDA abs,X/STA abs,X bounds), then materialize the destination as an initialized block populated with the source bytes, with provenance comments and cross-space references bridging call sites to the RAM copy (and ideally back-references to the ROM master). Design questions: loader-time (descriptor hints: 'this region is copied to X at boot' as DATA, e.g. CHRGET) vs analyzer-time (detect copy loops generically); relocation/patching during copy = NOT one-to-one — detect and warn rather than mis-map; interaction with banking overlays (source may live in a banked window). Start with descriptor-hinted static case (CHRGET as the canonical fixture), generalize to detected copies after.
notes:
2026-07-24: First increment COMPLETE + pushed (commit abb41da): the automatic copy-loop recognizer (C64CopyLoopAnalyzer) with dual-home byte-mapped overlay materialization, materialize/disassemble decoupling (data vs code), LoopIdioms shared substrate, and TransferSpec neutral core. Full acceptance gate green. Kept in_progress: remaining planned work is now sub-beads grm-1.7.1.1 (manual command front-end) and grm-1.7.1.2 (descriptor copied_to / CHRGET Tier A). Related follow-ups: grm-chu, grm-r6f, grm-1.7.5.
2026-07-25 (grm-chu): materialization was EXTRACTED out of C64CopyLoopAnalyzer into a new front-end-agnostic TransferMaterializer, and the default placement changed from byte-mapped overlay to in-place carve (split x2 -> convertToInitialized -> setBytes) in the base space. The analyzer is now recognition-only and emits TargetKind.SAME_SPACE, letting the materializer choose placement. This matters for the two open children: grm-1.7.1.1 (manual command) and grm-1.7.1.2 (descriptor hint) should both call TransferMaterializer.materialize rather than reimplementing anything -- grm-1.7.1.2 in particular runs from the LOADER, not an analyzer, which is why the extraction was necessary. Decision record: docs/smc-inplace-vs-overlay.md; decision bead grm-7da.
close_reason:
All planned increments done; both children closed. The subsystem now has four front-ends over one materializer, reached through the public RunFromElsewhere facade: the auto recognizer (CopyLoopAnalyzer, machine-neutral), the descriptor copied_from directive, the manual GhidraScript, and the GUI plugin.

Validated on a real target end to end: The Legend of Zelda's 0x1270-byte PRG-RAM routine is materialized IN PLACE at $6C90 in the base space, so the game's 389 JSR / 87 JMP call sites into it resolve natively with no bridging -- which was grm-chu's entire motivation.

The load-bearing lesson, recorded in docs/smc-runfromelsewhere-design.md section 6: the recognizer materializes ONLY with a jump into the destination proving the payload is code. The permissive rule survived C64 fixtures but produced false positives on 3 of 4 real NES ROMs, snapshotting runtime buffers (including over the stack page). It was affordable to tighten only because the deferred-call case it protected finally has its own front-ends.

Remaining follow-ups are separate beads: grm-r6f (reference retargeting, now narrowed to the overlay path only) and grm-bqs (destination inside a banked window).

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
2026-07-25 (facade): commit b6328fa adds RunFromElsewhere, the public entry point all four front-ends now go through -- the recognizer, the descriptor directive, the manual script, and the GUI plugin. TransferSpec/TransferMaterializer stay package-private deliberately: the record has grown a field per front-end (now 12 components) and publishing it would make every future field a source-breaking change. Callers build a fluent Request instead.

Two things the facade adds that the analyzer never needed, because two of the four front-ends take their input from a human or a YAML file rather than from real instruction operands:
- VALIDATION. Bad length, out-of-space range, entry point outside the copy -> a SKIPPED Result carrying the reason, plus a log line. Never a silent overlay in the wrong place.
- Result.alreadyPresent. The materializer returns SKIPPED for both 'already done' and 'failed', and telling them apart matters because re-running after supplying a ROM IS the documented recovery path.

Also landed in b6328fa: originLabel parameterizes the provenance text (three front-ends, only one has a loop, so 'copy loop -> COPY_xxxx' could not stay hard-coded); a null provenanceSite is now legal and logs instead of bookmarking, which is docs/smc-inplace-vs-overlay.md section 6's 'log note only' rule; TransferPlacement.NEW_BLOCK for a wholly unmapped destination (grm-1.7.6 item 3); and the C64CopyLoopAnalyzer -> CopyLoopAnalyzer rename + language-based gating.

Full acceptance gate green with ZERO golden churn -- the widened analyzer gate fired no false positives on any existing NES/PET/C128 fixture.

title: CBM BASIC dialect expansion: BASIC 4 (PET) + BASIC 7 (C128) token lists and analyzer parameterization
description: Add the per-dialect extension lists to the shared token data file (BASIC 4: $CC+ disk keywords CONCAT/DOPEN/DCLOSE/RECORD/HEADER/COLLECT/BACKUP/COPY/APPEND/DSAVE/DLOAD/CATALOG/RENAME/SCRATCH/DIRECTORY; BASIC 7: $CC+ single-byte additions PLUS $CE/$FE two-byte prefixed tokens as per-prefix lists building BASIC_V7_TOKEN_CE/_FE enums) and the types: entries in future pet.yaml / c128.yaml machine descriptors. Analyzer side: the line-walker consumes dialect config from the descriptor (which enums, which prefix pages) — per grm-odt.1's (bytes consumed, name) token-lookup interface. GATED ON: pet/c128 machine descriptors existing (separate machine-bringup work, not this bead).
notes:
Filed 2026-07-11 as part of the grm-1.6 epic promotion. Do not start until a second CBM machine descriptor exists.
2026-07-18 user authorized prerequisite order: PET first (grm-1.8), then C128 (grm-1.9), then this dialect-expansion bead. grm-1.9 depends on grm-1.8; this bead now depends on grm-1.9.
Implementation design: preserve C64BasicAnalyzer class identity but select dialect from compiled formats.prg.basic metadata via Retro Machine Map. Metadata names primary GDT token enum, optional ordered CE/FE prefix enums, and PETSCII variant. PET uses BASIC_V4_TOKEN; C128 uses BASIC_V7_TOKEN plus per-prefix enums; C64 explicitly selects BASIC_V2_TOKEN. Generic lookup returns bytes-consumed and preserves invalid/truncated prefix pairs raw. Authoritative VICE petcat behavior also corrects DATA rendering: raw until an unquoted colon, then normal token scanning resumes.
Implemented descriptor-driven CBM BASIC dialect analysis. Added PET BASIC 4 and C128 BASIC 7 token enums (including CE/FE prefix pages), generic GDT-backed lookup, dialect metadata for C64/PET/C128, DATA/quote/REM semantics, strict 16-bit literal SYS handling, and cross-dialect golden fixtures covering raw/invalid/truncated prefixes and SYS expression/overflow rejection. Validation: focused basic-dialects gate PASS; full build-and-test.sh check PASS; final independent review found no correctness issues.
close_reason: Closed

title: CBM BASIC program support: token data, detokenizing analyzer, dialects 2/4/7
description: Umbrella for making Ghidra genuinely understand tokenized CBM BASIC programs across the dialect family: BASIC 2 (C64/VIC-20), BASIC 4 (PET), BASIC 7 (C128). Pillars: (1) dialect-layered token DATA shipped as .gdt enums (shared $80-$CB base = single transcription; per-dialect extension lists fork above $CB with conflicting values; BASIC 7 adds $CE/$FE two-byte prefixed tokens -> per-prefix enums); (2) a line-walking detokenizing ANALYZER (line-link/line-number structure, token typing outside quoted/REM contexts, detokenized line comments, SYS-entry detection replacing the loader's wrong entry-function-at-load-address wart); (3) DIALECT parameterization — which enum(s)/walker rules apply comes from the machine descriptor, so PET/C128 support = data + descriptor, not new Java; (4) PETSCII rendering (grm-1.4's C64 half) as the string-literal/REM display layer inside detokenized comments. The BASIC analyzer is a primary design-driving CONSUMER of grm-1.4: it needs a Java-callable byte->display-string PETSCII mapping (shifted/unshifted), not just Ghidra charset registration for string search.
notes: Promoted from grm-odt.1 to an epic at user request 2026-07-11 ('promote the basic analyser to its own epic and flip any dependencies that make sense'). grm-odt (token enum foundation, in flight) and grm-odt.1 (analyzer) re-parented here. Cross-cutting dep: analyzer depends on grm-1.4 for PETSCII; grm-1.4's design must take the detokenizer's requirements as input (recorded on grm-1.4).
close_reason: All 3 children complete and verified: grm-odt (dialect-layered token enums in .gdt), grm-odt.1 (line-walking detokenizing analyzer with SYS-entry fix), grm-1.6.1 (BASIC 4 PET + BASIC 7 C128 dialect parameterization from descriptor metadata, incl. CE/FE prefix enums). PETSCII pillar's consumer-facing half (PetsciiMapper, shifted/unshifted, escaped control rendering) is delivered and gate-verified (verifyPetsciiMapper + basic-petscii/basic-dialects fixtures green in full suite 2026-07-19). Remaining related work tracked outside epic scope: grm-52z (analyzer efficiency, code-review), grm-1.4 (charset registration for string search + NES .tbl half), grm-0bh (BASIC ROM symbols).

title: C64: BASIC line-walking analyzer — detokenized comments, token typing, SYS entry fix
description: Phase 2 of grm-odt (scouted 2026-07-11): new C64BasicAnalyzer extends AbstractAnalyzer (NOT BoardBankAnalyzer — that base is banking-flow specific), gated on C64PrgLoader.NAME + program entry == the descriptor load_target region start (derive 'is BASIC-start PRG' from c64.yaml, do NOT hardcode $0801). Walk classic line structure from load address: 2-byte next-line link, 2-byte line number, tokenized bytes to $00 terminator; program ends at $0000 link. Per line: apply BASIC_V2_TOKEN (phase-1 enum, looked up from the .gdt by name and enumerated into a value->name map — no parallel Java token table, single source of truth) to token bytes OUTSIDE quoted strings; type link+linenum words; EOL/pre comment with the detokenized line text. GOTCHAS from scouting: quote-tracking state machine (PETSCII control/graphics bytes >= $80 inside quotes are NOT tokens); REM lines store the REM token then RAW untokenized text to EOL (must not token-decode); embedded control chars. ALSO FIX pre-existing loader wart: C64PrgLoader marks a function at the raw load address even for BASIC PRGs (line-link bytes, not code) — suppress for BASIC-start PRGs and instead parse a SYS <addr> line if present, marking THAT as the real ML entry (scope SYS parsing explicitly: simple decimal literal only). TEST: tools/banktest-pattern fixture — hand-tokenized 3-4 line .prg (FOR/PRINT/NEXT/SYS 2064) via mkbasictest.py, VerifyBasicTest checks token annotation, line structure, comment text, $0000 terminator, SYS entry; golden dump.
notes: Split from grm-odt 2026-07-11 per scout plan. Depends on phase-1 enum landing (consumes BASIC_V2_TOKEN from the .gdt). Est 1-2 days; medium risk (quote/REM state machine). DIALECT NOTE (2026-07-11): the analyzer must be dialect-parameterized from the start — which token enum(s) it consumes should come from the machine descriptor (c64.yaml -> BASIC_V2_TOKEN; future pet.yaml -> BASIC_V4_TOKEN, c128 -> BASIC_V7_TOKEN + two-byte prefix handling), not hardcoded. BASIC 7 two-byte tokens will need the walker to consume prefix+byte pairs — design the token-lookup interface around (bytes consumed, name) rather than byte->name.
close_reason: C64BasicAnalyzer shipped: line-link walker (shared C64BasicWalker, also used by the loader's BASIC-start sniff), petcat-compatible detokenized PRE comments via PetsciiMapper, link/linenum typed as words, token bytes left undefined (comment carries meaning). Tokens consumed from the .gdt archive DTM (BasicV2TokenLookup; dialect-agnostic (bytesConsumed,name) interface, BASIC-7-prefix-ready). Loader wart fixed: BASIC-start PRGs no longer get a function at the load address; the analyzer marks the SYS <decimal> target instead. TWO CORRECTIONS vs the brief: (1) DATA text IS tokenized in real BASIC 2 (the DATA GOTO gotcha) — no DATA protection branch, verified against petcat/ROM behavior; (2) naive BASIC-start detection false-positived on pure-ML fixtures (stray $00 made one bogus line) — caught by the suite, fixed by requiring the FIRST line to parse cleanly. c64basictest = 11th fixture (B1-B5: exact line renders incl. {clr}/{$a0}/{lgrn}, REM not decoded, SYS entry at 0x842, no function at 0x801); 10 pre-existing goldens byte-identical. Deferred to grm-1.6.1: dialect lists, two-byte prefixes, SYS expressions, variant override (documented in docs/basic-analyzer.md).

title: MMC1: nes-mmc1.yaml descriptor + registry wiring + end-to-end fixture
description: Design B/C-Tier-1 on parent grm-hsv: machines/nes-mmc1.yaml (ines_mappers:[1]; serial-shift mechanism with multi-field targets; layouts keyed off prg_mode: modes 2/3 = fix-first/fix-last 16K windows, modes 0/1 = single PRG32 window — confirm 32K window shape needs no third window-shape concept). Loader materializes (layout x bank) cross product (128K titles = 8 banks; ~2x8 real overlays). Tier 1 placement = normal two-level tracked-state lookup, NO upfront per-bank options (retires GhidraNes BankAddressOption by construction). End-to-end Metroid-shaped fixture (reset dance then never touch Control again -> prg_mode=3 known nearly everywhere).
notes: Materialized from parent design 2026-07-11 (design sub-bead 4). Gated on the serial-shift/findIdioms bead. HANDOFF from grm-hsv.1 (2026-07-11): (1) 32K modes (prg_mode 0/1) need PRG[(prg_bank>>1)*0x8000] — evalExpr supports only literals/last/second_last/+-*; add shift-or-divide grammar (+ MapCompiler validation) OR a derived field aliasing prg_bank bits 1-4; do NOT ship modes 0/1 as PRG[0] on the real board (real games use 32K modes). (2) FF1 trampoline (JSR SwapPRG_L -> JMP SwapPRG): calledHelper resolves via getFlows() and does NOT follow one level of JMP — trampoline call sites lose argument recovery unless added. (3) Metroid mailbox commit values resolve unknown -> honest WARNING at MMCWriteReg3; helper-call-argument recovery (LDA #imm/JSR SwapPRG pattern) should still resolve Zelda-style sites — verify HelperModel handles a helper whose write-5 is the switch site (argReg='A'). (4) Keep initial_state prg_mode=3 (reset-dance convention, all surveyed games). (5) Loop matcher is trip-5 only — extend to 4+pre-STA only if a real title needs it. (6) Synthetic serialtest board is mapper 222 (unassigned range); real board = ines_mappers:[1].
close_reason: Real MMC1 board shipped end-to-end. machines/nes-mmc1.yaml (ines_mappers:[1]): all four prg_mode layouts byte-accurate — evalExpr gained >> (right-shift, *-precedence, left-assoc; MapCompiler validator mirrored; baseline diff proved all 9 existing maps byte-identical) so 32K modes map PRG[(prg_bank>>1)*0x8000]. Modes 0/1 identical-window-sets handled correctly by existing runtime (separate per-mode lookups; verbose but correct). Metroid-shaped fixture (LDA #imm/JSR SwitchBank helper idiom, CHR chain no-poison, mode 3->2 transition engineered via byte-identity: prg_bank=7 makes mode-2 switchable WC000 map the same PRG[last] bytes the fixed window had). EXPOSED+FIXED latent engine bug: recoverCallArgument positioned helper args with the mechanism-wide (effectMask,lsb) — wrong for multi-target mechanisms. Fix: BankSwitchStrategy.depositHelperArgument default method returning HelperDeposit(ownedMask, value) — ownedMask distinguishes touched-unresolved (poison) from untouched (preserve); default reproduces historical behavior byte-for-byte; serial-shift override decodes target from switch site and deposits through its field list; ownedMask=0 = verified no-op (CHR helpers can't poison). HelperModel carries strategy+switchSite; helper-call comments render from mechanism-window stateAfter (no more spurious '?'). nesmmc1test = 10th fixture, M1-M10 PASS; 9 pre-existing goldens byte-identical. Real-ROM acceptance gate (Metroid/Zelda/FF1, manual, CI-excluded) now unblocked — FF1 trampoline arg-recovery still a known gap (on bead notes).

title: MMC1: findIdioms hook + serial-shift strategy + fixtures
description: Design A + B on parent grm-hsv. (1) New optional BankSwitchStrategy hook findIdioms(Program, Function) -> List<IdiomMatch(exitEdgeTarget, resultState)>, default empty; BoardBankAnalyzer runs it per function like findHelpers and folds matches into the switchResults-shaped map (containment property: merge/annotate/retarget/helper propagation unchanged). PROTOTYPE THE HOOK SHAPE FIRST — if it doesn't fold into switchResults it ripples back. (2) SerialShiftBankSwitchStrategy: bit-7-set write anywhere $8000-$FFFF = reset (prg_mode->3 known, ORs control with $0C); fully-unrolled 5x STA/LSR chain walked statically (writes 1-4 null, write 5 full BankState; target from write-5 addr bits 14:13, value reassembled); canonical STA/LSR/DEY/BNE loop via findIdioms (sole loop-body write to range + shift of same reg + trip-count 5 or 4+preloop; seed from ONE backward scan of pre-loop load; commit on loop EXIT edge). Params: multi-field-per-target deposit — targets {0:{fields:[{mirroring,shift 0,bits 2},{prg_mode,shift 2,bits 2}]}, 3:{fields:[{prg_bank,shift 0,bits 5}]}} — strategy-opaque, no compiler change. Source loop matcher shapes from REAL commercial MMC1 disassemblies (Metroid/Zelda), not wiki-invented. Fixtures: unrolled, inlined loop, JSR'd loop, bit-7 reset alone, table-driven-unresolvable (WARNING), CHR-write recognized-but-discarded. Bit-7 partially-known must NOT silently assume reset (explicit fixture).
notes:
Materialized from parent design 2026-07-11 (design sub-bead 3; sub-bead 2 mode-register-class skipped — MMC1 needs none per Design B, MMC3's is co-emitted in select-data).

REAL-GAME IDIOM SURVEY (2026-07-11, scratchpad/mmc1-idioms.md; Zelda1/FF1/Metroid disassemblies verified mapper 1): (1) ALL THREE games use the FULLY UNROLLED 5xSTA/4xLSR chain — NONE use the counted STA/LSR/DEY/BNE loop the design treated as canonical. PRIORITY INVERSION: the static unrolled-chain walker is the PRIMARY pattern (covers all surveyed titles); the findIdioms loop matcher is SECONDARY (keep — synthetic fixture + unsurveyed titles — but do not gate acceptance on it). (2) FF1 writes to NON-CANONICAL addresses inside each register's 8K window ($9FFF/$BFFF/$DFFF/$FFF9) — design's 'target from write-5 addr bits 14:13' already handles this; make the fixture cover a non-canonical address. (3) Zelda's reset = ORA #$FF then STA to ALL FOUR register addresses (four consecutive reset writes — each is an independent bit-7 reset, must not confuse the chain walker). (4) FF1 reaches the unrolled helper through a JMP trampoline (JSR SwapPRG_L -> JMP SwapPRG) — check findHelpers/Ghidra thunk handling follows it. (5) Value provenance: Zelda = immediates (easy); FF1 = value computed via ROL/AND/ORA well before the JSR (backward scan may fail -> honest WARNING); Metroid = DEFERRED mailbox (call sites write a pending var; a per-frame dispatcher does the real writes with AND/ORA-composed value -> unresolvable -> WARNING, expected degrade; the dispatcher itself is the switch site, call sites are not). A pure peephole matcher misses real call sites in 2 of 3 games — acceptance expectations for hsv.2 should reflect that (fixed windows + reset-dance prg_mode=3 still give most of the value).
close_reason: SerialShiftBankSwitchStrategy landed with ZERO engine changes — the planned findIdioms hook proved unnecessary: runDataflow probes computeSwitch on every instruction, so the strategy claims the counted loop's closing BNE as the switch site and the commit flows through the existing switchResults fold (strictly better containment than the hook). Primary recognizer = survey-informed unrolled 5xSTA/LSR bidirectional chain walk (breaks on non-chain instr, control-flow join into any link, X/Y store, RMW); write-5 target from ITS OWN addr bits 14:13 (FF1 $FFF9 non-canonical fixture-proven); quad-resets classified independently before chain logic. Key empirical fix: StoredValueScanner treats shifts as opaque, so preceded-by-LSR-A stores get bit 7 known-clear STRUCTURALLY. Loop matcher: trip-5 STA/LSR/DEX|DEY/BNE, poison suppression by delegating body-membership to the same branch matcher (recognizers cannot disagree). Synthetic board nes-serialtest.yaml on mapper 222 (101 is NOT safe — NESdev duplicate-assignment, not reserved); 4-value prg_mode layouts; 32K modes mapped PRG[0] pending evalExpr shift/divide (grm-hsv.2 flag). nesserialtest = 9th fixture, 16 criteria incl. honest WARNING paths (table seed, partial bit-7 not misread as reset). SUITE OK, 8 pre-existing goldens byte-identical.

title: MMC3: overlay-scale measurement at SMB3 scale (evidence for RFC #9349)
description: Design C on parent grm-6a7: measure overlay-interim pain at 512K/64-bank scale (~128-256 overlays worst case). Metrics: block/space count, import+analysis wall clock vs UxROM baseline, refsAdded, qualitative UI navigability. Record in docs (vision doc M3 section or docs/mmc3-overlay-scale.md), mirror into our Ghidra Discussion #9349. Needs real acceptance titles (SMB3/Crystalis/Kirby) loading — manual, CI-excluded.
notes: ROM located (user, 2026-07-12): H:/emulators/nes/roms/Super Mario Bros 3 (PRG 1) (U).nes. CAUTION: analyzeHeadless.bat chokes on parentheses in filenames (documented in run-banktest.sh) -- copy/rename to a parenthesis-free path before importing.
close_reason: Measured overlay scale on real ROMs (Ghidra 12.1.2, CI-excluded): overlay spaces = 3N-1 for N in-range 8K PRG banks, deterministic at load time. UxROM baseline 7 -> MMC3 512K (Mega Man 4) 191 = ~27x blow-up. Cost is structural/navigational, not compute (analysis ~1s even at 191 overlays); static resolution INTO overlays is idiom-dependent and often ~0 (Crystalis 0 refs/12 warns into 95 spaces). Correction: SMB3 is 256K/32 banks/95 overlays (bead title's '512K/SMB3 scale' conflated PRG with total ROM incl CHR); true 64-bank title is Mega Man 4; Kirby unavailable. Recorded in docs/mmc3-overlay-scale.md + RFC + vision doc; draft #9349 comment handed to user. New: OverlayScaleMeasure.java + measure-overlay-scale.sh (manual runner).

title: MMC3: function-level bank-state summaries (requires-on-entry WARNING only)
description: Design D on parent grm-6a7: per-function FunctionBankSummary(requiresOnEntry, effectOnExit); effectOnExit read off Phase-1 outStates at RTS/RTI merged; requiresOnEntry backward over call graph bottom-up on SCCs. M3 scope = requires-bits derivation + violation WARNING bookmarks ONLY; NO back-propagation into Phase-1 (M4+). Context: MMC3 select+data helpers store TWICE so HelperModel argReg reconciliation nulls out — current helper propagation degrades for MMC3 until this lands (expected gap, document). Fixture: two-write helper called from consistent + violating contexts; WARNING only on violator.
notes: Materialized from parent design 2026-07-11 (design sub-bead 4). Optional sub-bead 6 (two-write helpers in findHelpers) folded here if needed.
close_reason: Function-level bank-state summaries landed as read-only Phase 3 in BoardBankAnalyzer (M3 scope: WARNING bookmarks only, NO Phase-1 back-propagation). FunctionBankSummary(exitState, modifiedMask, requiresOnEntry): own consumption = per-SwitchResult effectMask & ~inKnown & ~effectKnown for non-cacheable strategies (the ~effectKnown term keeps immediate-only C64 register-write sites requirement-free — verified empirically); exitState read off RTS/RTI retained in-states for free; call-graph propagation by chaotic bottom-up fixpoint (monotone bit-union, recursion-safe, no explicit Tarjan); indirect calls documented conservatism. Dedupe: Phase-2 alreadyWarned set; the new warning is provably non-duplicative (existing call-switch warning fires on arg-resolution failure, this one on callee dispatch precondition — orthogonal, G3-verified). nesmmc3test2 = 12th fixture: data-write-only helper H, CallerA (select known, no warning) vs CallerB (poisoned select, WARNING at JSR only). 11 pre-existing goldens byte-identical, zero new warnings on them. Scope cuts documented: retarget-derived requirements (source b), value-level requirements, back-prop = M4+. Also SURFACED (filed separately): select-data lacks a depositHelperArgument override — bare data-write helpers deposit across the whole mechanism width via the default.

title: MMC3: select-data strategy (select+prg_mode co-emission, even/odd-over-range), fixture
description: Design A + Design B resolution (a) on parent grm-6a7: new SelectDataBankSwitchStrategy. Even-address store in $8000-$9FFE range = bank select: resolve byte via existing scanner, deposit bits 0-2 into 'select' field AND bit 6 into 'prg_mode' (co-emission from the same recovered byte; keeps first-match-wins engine loop unchanged). Odd-address store = data: if inState select fully known and targeted field tracked (6->r6, 7->r7) overwrite only that field; select unknown -> poison r6 AND r7; select known 0-5 (CHR) -> leave r6/r7 UNTOUCHED (per-frame CHR swaps must not poison PRG — THE easy-to-get-wrong case, fixture it); data unrecoverable with known select -> only targeted field unknown. Recognizer is (addr&1) over the WHOLE $8000-$9FFF range (sketch's fixed select_address/data_address params are wrong vs hardware mirroring — fix machines/sketches/nes-mmc3.yaml and promote to machines/nes-mmc3.yaml, ines_mappers:[4]). Fixture: synthesized mapper-4 ROM in mknesbanktest.py (immediate select/data pairs, cross-bank JSR through r6-switched window, CHR-select-no-poison case, mode-1 swap); goldens; existing 7 fixtures byte-identical. Note grm-ezl sets[] contiguity: order state fields so this mechanism's fields pack contiguously.
notes: Materialized from parent design 2026-07-11. Parent grm-6a7 design sub-beads 2+3 folded together per design.
close_reason: SelectDataBankSwitchStrategy landed: even/odd-over-range recognition, select+prg_mode co-emission from one recovered byte (no separate mode mechanism), inState-echo no-change contract (CHR selects 0-5 leave r6/r7 untouched — fixture-proven), unknown-select poisons both PRG targets only. BoardBankAnalyzer injects params._field_layout (field-local lsb/width per sets: field from board.fieldSpecs()) — additive, single-field strategies unaffected, 7 pre-existing goldens byte-identical. machines/nes-mmc3.yaml promoted from sketch (mirrored range + co-emission fix; second_last maps keyword already existed). nesmmc3test = 8th suite fixture; golden also gives invariant hoisting its first coverage (WA000_B*/WE000 unqualified vs W8000_M0_B*/W8000_M1/WC000_M1_B*). Known gap: two-write select+data helpers degrade findHelpers — grm-6a7.2's scope. All 8 fixtures SUITE OK.

title: Release-build strategy on GitHub (Actions matrix across supported Ghidra versions)
description: Set up automated release builds for ghidra-retro-machines on GitHub. Reference sketch = kylewlacy/GhidraNes (.github/workflows/): a reusable _build.yml (on: workflow_call) building with a matrix of ~19 Ghidra versions (10.3 through 12.1) via the antoniovazquezblanco/setup-ghidra@v2.1.0 action (installs Ghidra + exports GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR env var), temurin Java 21, gradle -PGHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR=..., then renames dist/*.zip to ghidra_<ver>_<sha>_<date>_<name>.zip and uploads as artifacts; release.yml triggers on tag push v*, calls _build, downloads merged artifacts, and creates a DRAFT release with gh release create --generate-notes + gh release upload; ci.yml reuses the same _build on ordinary pushes. Adaptations needed for GRM: (1) our build.gradle checks the GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR env var FIRST, which is exactly what setup-ghidra sets — so CI works naturally, no -P needed; (2) matrix should start narrow (12.1.x we actually support) and grow deliberately — sleigh compile + GDT JavaExec tasks may not be version-portable as far back as GhidraNes goes; (3) consider running tools/banktest/run-banktest.sh (analyzeHeadless, works on ubuntu) as a CI quality gate before release assets are published. TRIGGER MECHANISM IS OPEN: user finds tag pushing clunky as a downstream fork — evaluate alternatives: workflow_dispatch with a version input (workflow tags + drafts the release itself, one button in the UI), 'release: published' trigger (draft the release in the UI first, action builds+attaches assets), or push-to-release-branch. Pick whichever makes cutting a release a single low-ceremony step.
design: TRIGGER DECIDED (user, 2026-07-12): workflow_dispatch to start. release.yml takes a version input (e.g. '0.3.0'), runs the _build matrix, then tags and creates the DRAFT release itself (gh release create --generate-notes + upload assets) -- one button in the Actions UI, no local tag push. Tag creation happens IN the workflow from the dispatched ref, so the fork's local clone never needs to push tags. Keep the trigger swappable: structure release.yml so switching to 'release: published' later is just changing the on: block + reading the version from the release tag instead of the input. ci.yml on ordinary pushes reuses the same workflow_call _build.
notes:
Requested by user 2026-07-11. GhidraNes workflow files fetched and verified 2026-07-11 (repo kylewlacy/GhidraNes, default branch main). setup-ghidra action needs auth_token: secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN to avoid API rate limits when downloading Ghidra releases.

VERSION-SUPPORT POLICY (user, 2026-07-11): Ghidra will install/keep using an extension built against a different version — it does NOT proactively check compatibility, so a mismatched build may work or break depending on API drift. For the extensions we care about (mostly loaders), the biggest breakage so far is the 11->12 breaking change to the Loader load() method signature. HARD FLOOR = Ghidra 12.0: we will NOT support the <=11 load() API — working around it is a pain (see how GhidraNes contorts to span both). So the matrix may be a small subset, possibly even one build serving several versions. PROCEDURE: check back-support starting at 12.0 and work FORWARD, running the banktest suite against each release to find the true minimum version that works (compat = suite passes, not just compiles). If we find critical dependencies on behavior introduced post-12.0 (candidates to check: ImporterSettings record shape, CommentType enum, SleighCompile invocation, MemoryBlockUtils signatures), DISCUSS each with the user before deciding to work around it vs. raising the floor — do not silently add compat shims.

title: Reconstruct testing procedure for safe parallelization (isolated trees/Ghidra infra, efficient rebuilds)
description: Today the build/test loop is serialized through shared mutable infrastructure, which makes parallel subagent work (now the standing preference) risky: (1) the built extension is installed by delete+unzip into the single per-user Extensions dir (%APPDATA%/ghidra/ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC/Extensions/) — two agents installing different builds clobber each other, and an open Ghidra GUI locks the jar; (2) tools/banktest/run-banktest.sh uses shared work/project dirs under one tree; (3) a single working tree means concurrent code edits collide. Rework so N agents can build+test independently: git worktrees (or EnterWorktree) per agent; per-agent Ghidra 'installation' or at least per-agent extension install + headless project dirs — investigate whether analyzeHeadless can point at an alternate extensions dir (e.g. ghidra.user.settings.dir / -vmargs user-dir override) so one shared read-only Ghidra install serves many isolated setting dirs, which is far cheaper than duplicating the 1GB+ install; per-agent scratch/work dirs keyed by worktree. Constraint: keep the rebuild loop reasonably fast — full gradle buildExtension per iteration is already the dominant cost, so prefer solutions that share gradle caches across worktrees and avoid re-unzipping more than needed. Deliverable: updated run-banktest.sh / helper script(s) + documented procedure agents can follow without stepping on each other.
notes: Requested by user 2026-07-11. Motivated by the new user-level 'use subagents whenever it makes sense' policy — current single-install test flow is the main thing forcing serialization. Remember headless gotcha: project path must contain no dot-prefixed path element.
close_reason: Landed: tools/banktest/build-and-test.sh (one-command build -> per-worktree isolated extension install under build/ghidra-home via -Dapplication.settingsdir/-Dapplication.cachedir + GHIDRA_HEADLESS_JAVA_OPTIONS -> suite), run-banktest.sh BANKTEST_SETTINGS_BASE hook, CLAUDE.md Build & Test procedure. Verified: main-tree SUITE OK, stamp-skip on second run, isolated settings dir demonstrably used (pass/fail tracked isolated zip while shared %APPDATA% copy present), two worktrees ran concurrently both SUITE OK. Bonus fixes the worktree smoke test flushed out: settings.gradle pins rootProject.name (worktree dir name broke loader discovery via jar name); build.gradle buildExtension now depends on buildPetsciiMap (fresh checkouts shipped a zip missing data/petscii.map -> silently broken C64 BASIC detokenizer; was masked by stale artifact in main tree).

title: C64 BASIC tokens as a Ghidra enum (or similar data type)
description: Idea parked for later: represent the C64 BASIC V2 token set ($80 END ... $CB GO, plus the two-byte extensions if we ever cover BASIC 7/other dialects) as a data type the extension ships — most likely an enum in the generated .gdt (via the YAML types: mechanism / headless GDT builder), so tokenized BASIC program text in a PRG/disk image can be annotated readably in the listing. Open questions: plain enum vs. a typedef'd byte with an analyzer that walks BASIC line links (line-link/line-number/token-stream structure) and comments/detokenizes; where it hooks in (C64PrgLoader for BASIC-start PRGs?); whether symbols/types in machines/c64.yaml is the right home. No urgency — capture only.
design: PLAN (scouted 2026-07-11, read-only exploration). PHASE 1 = THIS BEAD: (1) GdtBuilder (tools/gdtbuilder/src/main/java/gdtbuilder/GdtBuilder.java) supports only kind: struct|flags; add third kind 'enum' — new branch in buildTypes() + buildEnum() mirroring buildFlags() but reading values: [{value,name,comment}] with EnumDataType(name,size) + add(name,value,comment); no bit-shift logic; topo-sort/archive plumbing untouched. (2) machines/c64.yaml types: add BASIC_V2_TOKEN, kind: enum, size: 1 — 76 contiguous tokens $80 END .. $CB GO, hand-transcribed with provenance comment (C64 Programmer's Reference Guide / c64-wiki token table; same 'inline seed' pattern as the KERNAL symbols). No gaps, no 2-byte extensions in stock V2 (BASIC 7 dialects out of scope). (3) docs/SCHEMA.md: document enum kind alongside flags (bitmask vs sequential distinction); check MAP_FORMAT.md types: section. VERIFY: buildC64Gdt + builder's verifyArchive() output shows BASIC_V2_TOKEN with 76 members; spot-check 0x80=END, 0xCB=GO. Rendering mechanics already proven: R6510_PORT_BITS (flags enum) renders symbolically via applyStructType/DataUtilities.createData. NOTE pre-existing loader wart found during scouting: C64PrgLoader marks a function at the raw load address even for BASIC-start PRGs ($0801 = line-link bytes, not code) — fix belongs to phase 2, not here. PHASE 2 = separate follow-on bead (C64BasicAnalyzer line-walker).
notes: Requested by user 2026-07-11. Scoped 2026-07-11 to phase 1 (enum only); phase 2 analyzer = grm-odt.1. DIALECT EVOLUTION REQUIREMENT (user, 2026-07-11, mid-implementation): eventual support for CBM BASIC 2, 4, AND 7 — craft BASIC 2 support so the evolution is natural, maximizing shared data/code. Dialect model: $80-$CB base (76 tokens END..GO) is IDENTICAL across 2/3.5/4/7 = the shared single source of truth; ABOVE $CB dialects FORK with conflicting value assignments (BASIC 4: $CC+ = disk keywords CONCAT/DOPEN/DLOAD/...; BASIC 3.5/7: same values = RGR/RCLR/...) so data model = shared base list + per-dialect extension lists with explicit values, NOT linear inheritance; BASIC 7 adds TWO-BYTE tokens ($CE/$FE prefix + second byte) — not implemented now, but data-file shape must accommodate (per-prefix lists building as separate per-prefix enums, since a 1-byte Ghidra enum can't hold them). Implementation shape: token data in a SHARED data file (following GdtBuilder struct source: precedent), composed by the enum kind; acceptance = adding BASIC 4 later is one extension list + one types: entry in a future pet.yaml, zero re-transcription. Enum names dialect-qualified (BASIC_V2_TOKEN / _V4_ / _V7_).
close_reason: Phase-1 delivered with the dialect-evolution design baked in: GdtBuilder gains a third types: kind 'enum' (explicit value: required — token tables start at 0x80; duplicate names/values rejected since EnumDataType would silently alias; verifyArchive now prints enum member counts). Token data lives in shared machines/generated/basic-tokens.yaml (top-level lists: map; basic2-base = 76 entries $80 END..$CB GO, canonical order independently verified value-by-value) composed via source:+lists: on the types: entry — adding BASIC 4/7 later = one sibling list + one types: entry in pet/c128.yaml, zero re-transcription (grm-1.6.1). Member names keep EXACT BASIC keywords incl. punctuation (INPUT#, TAB(, +, STR$ — Ghidra enum member names empirically unrestricted); YAML 1.1 gotcha found+fixed: bare ON parses as boolean, quoted, documented in SCHEMA.md. buildC64Gdt verify shows BASIC_V2_TOKEN (enum, 76 members); suite SUITE OK all 8 fixtures, goldens byte-identical. Follow-on: grm-odt.1 analyzer (blocked on grm-1.4 PETSCII).

title: Analyzer: consume layouts — mode-qualified clamp + two-level retargeting; nesmodetest fixture + golden
description: BoardBankAnalyzer: BoardModel.parse carries layouts (per layout: mode FieldSpec + value from when:, windows as fixed(mode-only) or switchable(bank field)); clampToResidence parses NAME_M<m>_B<v> (pins mode AND bank fields) and NAME_M<m> (pins mode); retargetReferences after enumerated+flat paths: resolve mode = modeField.valueIn(effective) → select layout → find window covering offset → fixed: skip if home mode else ref NAME_M<m>; switchable: bank = field.valueIn(effective), skip if home (mode,bank) else ref NAME_M<m>_B<v>; on_write=mechanism write refs still skipped. Wire nesmodetest into run-banktest.sh + VerifyBankTest checkNesModetest: must assert (a) cross-mechanism preserve — after bank latch, mode knowledge survives (comment shows both fields known); (b) switchable retarget in non-home bank W8000_M0_B1; (c) mode-varying fixed retarget W8000_M1 after mode switch; (d) switchable retarget in swapped layout WC000_M1_B<v>; (e) residence clamp inside a mode-qualified overlay. Bless golden after review. ACCEPTANCE: existing 6 goldens byte-identical; new golden reviewed line-by-line before bless.
close_reason: Analyzer consumes layouts: BoardModel.parse drives all computed windows off DescriptorSupport.planWindows (enumerated C64 windows keep the raw JSON walk; hoisted invariant layout windows now reach ComputedWindowModel for free); new ModeWindowModel per (window, mode) instance with bankField null = fixed; clampToResidence pins mode+bank from _M<m>_B<v> names and mode from _M<m>; retargetReferences adds the two-level mode->window->bank lookup with the same on_write/home-skip rules as flat windows. nesmodetest wired into suite (7th fixture): F1 switchable retarget, F2 mode-varying fixed retarget (JMP reclassified CALL by Ghidra non-returning analysis - legitimate), F3 bank write inside mode-qualified overlay retargeting into the swapped layout (proves residence clamp + cross-mechanism preservation + two-level lookup, structurally >=3 analyzer rounds), F4 pure-effect comments, F5 overlay disassembly. Golden reviewed line-by-line; 6 existing goldens byte-identical; MAP_FORMAT.md documents runtime naming + behavior. Known polish item: annotation shows the pure mechanism effect, so the other field reads 'assumed from initial' even where flow/clamp knowledge exists.

title: Loader + shared plumbing: realize memory.layouts[] windows (mode-qualified placement)
description: DescriptorSupport gains: shared banking.state FieldSpec parsing (moved from BoardBankAnalyzer's private record); layout normalization — a window name present in EVERY layout with identical compiled JSON is hoisted mode-invariant into the flat path, else mode-varying; runtime requires single-field when: per layout for mode-varying windows (log-skip otherwise; MMC1/MMC3 both single-field); OverlayNaming builders/parsers for NAME_M<m> (mode-varying fixed) and NAME_M<m>_B<v> (mode-varying switchable). NesRomLoader realizes layouts: invariant windows via existing path; mode-varying → one instance per (layout) for fixed exprs, per (layout x in-range bank) for switchable; the single home instance (when matches initial_state, bank==initial field value) is the plain base-space NAME block, every other instance is an overlay with the qualified name. New machines/nes-modetest.yaml synthetic 2-mode test board (memory-latch bank field 2 bits + memory-latch prg_mode 1 bit at distinct latch ranges; layouts: mode0 = W8000 switchable + WC000 fixed last, mode1 = swapped; ines mapper chosen unassigned/test — verify NesBoardRegistry wiring), compiled into data/machines. mknesbanktest.py gains nesmodetest.nes (64K PRG, mapper matching). ACCEPTANCE: existing 6 goldens byte-identical; manual headless import of nesmodetest shows the expected block set (2 base + 8 mode-qualified overlays + regions); suite wiring deferred to the analyzer sub-bead.
close_reason: Loader-side layouts realization landed: DescriptorSupport gains shared StateField parsing (parseStateFields/initialState/findField), planWindows normalization (single-mode-field validation, JSON-identity invariant hoisting into the flat path), and OverlayNaming mode-qualified forms (_M<m>, _M<m>_B<v>) with strict digits-only parsers. NesRomLoader split into realizeInvariantWindow (old semantics, switchable guard generalized to any single state field) + realizeVaryingWindows (home = initial mode + initial bank value in base space as plain NAME, all other instances mode-qualified overlays). New synthetic machines/nes-modetest.yaml (mapper 100, NESdev test-reserved; two memory-latch mechanisms on disjoint fields; two swapped-role layouts) + nesmodetest.nes generator in mknesbanktest.py. Headless smoke test: block set exactly as designed (W8000/WC000 base + W8000_M0_B1..B3, W8000_M1, WC000_M1_B0..B3 overlays); multi-mech bank comments already appear; no _M refs yet (analyzer bead grm-qvi). All 6 existing goldens byte-identical. Note: data/machines/*.map are gitignored buildMap artifacts, only YAML committed.

title: Engine: multi-mechanism state — position strategy deposits by sets[] field, preserve other fields across switches
description: Prerequisite discovered during grm-5tl.18 design: BoardBankAnalyzer.runDataflow line ~438 does outState = switched — a mechanism's computeSwitch result REPLACES the whole tracked state, and findHelpers/recoverCallArgument assume a result spans board.mask(). Works today only because every shipped board has ONE mechanism covering ALL state bits. A 2-mode board (bank latch + mode latch) needs: (1) configureStrategies pairs each strategy with positioning derived from its mechanism's sets[] (lsb of first sets field, effectMask = union of positioned field masks; pass effectMask>>lsb to configure() as stateMask so strategies stay field-local); (2) fold: positioned deposit = result << lsb; outState = inState with only effectMask bits overwritten (known+bits); (3) switchResults store the positioned deposit; annotation uses the inState-overwritten state (identical strings for single-mech boards); (4) HelperModel carries effectMask+lsb; fully-known test against effectMask not board.mask(); helper call fall-through preserves bits outside effectMask; recoverCallArgument masks by field width and positions by lsb; mixed-mechanism helper degrades conservatively; (5) lift the memory-latch M2 first-field-only javadoc constraint. ACCEPTANCE: all formulas reduce exactly to old behavior when effectMask==board.mask() and lsb==0; all 6 banktest goldens byte-identical.
close_reason: Implemented multi-mechanism state positioning: configureStrategies derives (effectMask,lsb) per mechanism from sets[] (contiguity-checked, no-sets falls back to whole-mask/lsb0); strategies now compute in field-local [0,width) space (inState narrowed via toFieldLocal, results repositioned via position); fold overwrites only the mechanism's own bits (overwrite helper), preserving other fields' knowledge; switchResults/CallSwitch store pure positioned effects so annotation+warning semantics are unchanged; HelperModel carries effectMask/lsb with conservative union degrade for mixed-mechanism helpers; recoverCallArgument resolves field-local and repositions. All 6 banktest goldens byte-identical (SUITE OK). sets[] already emitted in runtime maps — no MapCompiler change needed.

title: M3 prerequisite: consume memory.layouts[] at runtime (loader + analyzer mode-dependent windows)
description: Both MMC1 (grm-hsv) and MMC3 (grm-6a7) research (2026-07-10) found the same gap: memory.layouts[] (mode-dependent window sets, schema v2) is SCHEMA-COMPLETE BUT ENGINE-ABSENT. MapCompiler validates and emits layouts (buildLayouts, cross-validating when: keys against banking.state) — but NesRomLoader.load() reads only top-level windows[] (a layouts-only board like the nes-mmc3.yaml sketch would create ZERO PRG blocks), and BoardBankAnalyzer's BoardModel/clampToResidence/retargetReferences know only flat windows()/computedWindows(). Scope: (1) loader — layouts-aware placement: per-layout window realization across (mode value x bank value), home block = layout matching initial_state's mode + its home bank; naming keeps WINDOW_B<v> when a window's shape doesn't vary by mode, WINDOW_M<mode>_B<v> when it does; MMC1's 32K mode is a DIFFERENT window (own name, bank LSB ignored), not a merge of the 16K windows — confirm no third window-shape concept is needed. (2) analyzer — BoardModel.parse carries layouts; clampToResidence clamps BOTH mode and bank fields from a mode-qualified overlay; retargetReferences resolves active layout from the tracked mode field first, then window, then bank (two-level lookup). (3) synthetic banktest fixture: a 2-mode board driven by plain memory-latch/register-write mechanisms (decoupled from serial-shift/select-data risk) with a cross-bank JSR through both layouts; existing 5 goldens must stay byte-identical. Risk MEDIUM-HIGH: touches loader placement and the analyzer's core window model that UxROM/C64 depend on. Full designs on grm-hsv and grm-6a7.
close_reason: memory.layouts[] now fully consumed at runtime, delivered as three sub-beads: grm-ezl (multi-mechanism state positioning via sets[] - deposits overwrite only their own field bits, preserving other fields), grm-aqf (DescriptorSupport planWindows normalization + OverlayNaming _M forms + NesRomLoader mode-qualified home-in-base placement + synthetic nes-modetest board/fixture), grm-qvi (analyzer mode-qualified clamp + two-level retargeting + 7th suite fixture + golden). All acceptance criteria met: existing goldens byte-identical throughout; cross-bank JSR through both layouts verified end-to-end (nesmodetest F3). M3 gateway open: grm-hsv (MMC1) and grm-6a7 (MMC3) are now unblocked on the layouts side.

title: Fingerprint-gated skip of redundant whole-program re-runs in added()
description: Claim 1 of grm-5tl.13 (full design on parent). added() ignores its set param and re-seeds the full fixpoint from all entry points + functions on every framework re-invocation (phase-2 DisassembleCommand/CreateFunctionCmd side effects trigger these). CRITICAL: the reseed-everything behavior is LOAD-BEARING — it is how bank state reaches newly disassembled overlay code — so neither 'process only set' nor a one-shot guard is safe. Correct scope: static WeakHashMap<Program,Long> fingerprint (functionCount + numInstructions, O(1)), checked at top of added(), written back AFTER phase 2 so the analyzer's own side effects force the next round. All-or-nothing skip only; never cache/diff-merge phase-1 output (annotateBankSwitch never overwrites existing bank-> comments, so partial staleness compounds). Value currently unproven (no perf baseline; fixtures converge in ~1 round) — the acceptance fixture doubles as the value demonstration. Land last of the three children.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture (or log-based assertion) demonstrating >=2 disassembly rounds exists and passes BEFORE the skip logic lands: e.g. an overlay-bank JSR chain 3+ banks deep whose deepest bank annotation still resolves correctly with the skip active. Existing banktest goldens byte-identical.
close_reason: Landed in two commits per acceptance sequencing. (1) 8e23842: nesbanktest2.nes multi-round fixture -- 3-deep overlay JSR chain (RESET->PRG_LO_B2::8005->trampoline1->PRG_LO_B1::8010->trampoline2->PRG_LO_B3::8030) whose deepest REF is structurally impossible in <3 analyzer rounds (trampolines only get disassembled by the previous round's phase-2 flow-follow; mergeAndEnqueue skips undisassembled addresses). Passed BEFORE the skip landed. (2) Fingerprint skip in BoardBankAnalyzer: static synchronized WeakHashMap<Program,RunStamp>, fingerprint = functionCount/numInstructions packed into disjoint bits + mapPath, checked after the mapPath gate (before the JSON load), value captured at ENTRY and stored only after phase 2 completes -- own side effects always unmatch the next framework round, cancelled runs store nothing. All-or-nothing skip; coverage assumptions documented at the field. Full suite (6 fixtures) byte-identical with skip active; F3 deepest-bank REF resolves. Note: analyzer 'running' log lines don't surface at headless INFO level, so round-count evidence is structural (F3) per the acceptance's fixture option. Bonus regression coverage: the fixture's trampolines (two disagreeing latch writes each) capture the known two-write HelperModel degradation as golden Warning bookmarks (grm-6a7 Design D will visibly remove them).

title: runDataflow strategy dispatch: per-call memoization via cacheable() on BankSwitchStrategy
description: Claim 2 of grm-5tl.13 (full design on parent). runDataflow (:426-433) runs every strategy's computeSwitch per dequeue. Research proved MemoryLatch.computeSwitch is fully state-independent (its resolveLoad hook ignores inStateAtStore; resolveStoredValue only forwards that param to the hook) while RegisterWrite's is state-dependent (hook returns inStateAtStore) — so memoize per-address matched-strategy for both, cached RESULT only for cacheable ones. Map<Address,MatchInfo> LOCAL to each runDataflow call (phase 1/2 separation guarantees no mid-fixpoint code changes; discard per call). Add default cacheable()=false to BankSwitchStrategy, MemoryLatch overrides true. Pure memoization — banktest must stay byte-identical. Marginal alone; bundle with grm-5tl.13.1.
notes:
Implemented: added default boolean cacheable() = false to BankSwitchStrategy with javadoc explaining the contract (true iff computeSwitch's result is independent of inState). MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy overrides it to true (resolveLoad only ever resolves loads to a bank-invariant ROM byte, a program-only property; StoredValueScanner's own immediate-value folding is also state-independent). RegisterWriteBankSwitchStrategy left at the false default (its hook returns inStateAtStore).

runDataflow now keeps a local Map<Address,MatchInfo> matchCache (scoped to the call, not a field -- phase 1/2 separation means no instruction appears mid-fixpoint so per-call scoping avoids staleness). MatchInfo(strategy, result): strategy==null records that no strategy's instruction-level predicate matched this address at all; strategy!=null with result==null records a matched-but-non-cacheable strategy (must be re-probed each dequeue); result!=null records a matched cacheable strategy's state-independent value (reused directly, no recompute).

Soundness invariant established by reading both shipped strategies: both gate computeSwitch on an instruction-only boolean predicate (MemoryLatch.writesInRange, RegisterWrite.writesMechanism) and, critically, StoredValueScanner.resolveStoredValue NEVER returns null -- every path either combine()s to a possibly-unknown-but-non-null BankState or returns BankState.unknown() directly. So for both strategies, 'computeSwitch returns non-null' is exactly the instruction-only predicate, independent of inState -- confirmed RegisterWrite.computeSwitch returns unknown() (not null) when writesMechanism(instr) is true but the store register can't be identified, and otherwise always delegates to resolveStoredValue which is non-null. This means caching 'which strategy matched' per address (not just cacheable results) is sound today: on a cache hit for a non-cacheable match, only that one strategy is re-probed with the current in-state (skipping the other strategies entirely), and if that probe ever unexpectedly returns null (a future strategy violating the state-independent-predicate assumption), the code conservatively treats that dequeue as no-match rather than silently mis-caching -- documented as the safety fallback in the runDataflow comment. A genuinely state-dependent match/no-match strategy would need to override this design (not just cacheable()); none exists today.

Verification: gradle buildExtension succeeded, reinstalled, tools/banktest/run-banktest.sh check -> SUITE OK, 5 fixtures, zero golden diffs. banktest1-4 (RegisterWrite, including the helper-call and join-point join paths) and nesbanktest (MemoryLatch, including bus_conflict) both cover the cache paths for cacheable and non-cacheable strategies.
close_reason: 13.1: overlayCoveredRanges AddressSet built at configure() replaces the per-call block scan in bankInvariantRomByte; orchestrator review added a base-space normalization before contains() to preserve the old raw-offset semantics for overlay-resident instruction addresses (reachable on re-runs over phase-2-discovered overlay code, uncovered by fixtures). 13.2: cacheable() on BankSwitchStrategy (MemoryLatch=true) + per-runDataflow-call MatchInfo cache; soundness: resolveStoredValue never returns null, so non-null computeSwitch == instruction-only predicate for both shipped strategies; conservative fallback documented for future state-dependent-match strategies. SUITE OK, 5 fixtures, zero golden diffs.

title: MemoryLatch bankInvariantRomByte: precompute overlay-covered AddressSet at configure()
description: Claim 3 of grm-5tl.13 (full design on parent). bankInvariantRomByte (MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy :145-163) linear-scans all memory blocks per call. Build an AddressSet of base-space shadows of overlay blocks once at configure() — valid for analyzer lifetime since phase 2 never adds blocks — and replace the loop with contains(addr). Verify with a differential unit test (old vs new across synthetic overlay layouts, bitalgebra-style) + banktest byte-identity. Strongest standalone item; land first.
notes: Implemented: MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy now builds an AddressSet overlayCoveredRanges at configure() time (Program is available there), one addRange per overlay memory block using the same base-space offset comparison the old linear scan did (b.getStart()/getEnd().getOffset() mapped into the default address space). bankInvariantRomByte replaced the per-call block-walk with overlayCoveredRanges.contains(addr), O(log n) instead of O(#blocks) per call, called up to 3x per latch-write dequeue. Semantics verified by code-reading equivalence (documented in the field javadoc: loader-placed blocks are fixed before analyzers run and phase 2 never adds blocks, so a configure()-time snapshot is valid for the strategy instance's lifetime) plus the banktest suite as the executable differential check -- nesbanktest exercises MemoryLatch including the bus_conflict branch. Verification: gradle buildExtension succeeded (12.1.2 dist), reinstalled, tools/banktest/run-banktest.sh check -> SUITE OK, 5 fixtures, zero golden diffs (byte-identical output, confirming no behavior change).
close_reason: 13.1: overlayCoveredRanges AddressSet built at configure() replaces the per-call block scan in bankInvariantRomByte; orchestrator review added a base-space normalization before contains() to preserve the old raw-offset semantics for overlay-resident instruction addresses (reachable on re-runs over phase-2-discovered overlay code, uncovered by fixtures). 13.2: cacheable() on BankSwitchStrategy (MemoryLatch=true) + per-runDataflow-call MatchInfo cache; soundness: resolveStoredValue never returns null, so non-null computeSwitch == instruction-only predicate for both shipped strategies; conservative fallback documented for future state-dependent-match strategies. SUITE OK, 5 fixtures, zero golden diffs.

title: NES banktest golden suite (NesRomLoader + banking analyzer end-to-end)
description: grm-5tl.14 research (2026-07-10) confirmed tools/banktest is C64-only: run-banktest.sh imports .prg fixtures via -loader C64PrgLoader, so NOTHING automated exercises NesRomLoader or the NES side of BoardBankAnalyzer (computed windows, _B<v> overlay naming, FileBytes-backed bank blocks, vector-table PlacedWindow handling). Any refactor touching NES load-time layout (grm-5tl.14 part 1 especially) has no regression net beyond manual analyzeHeadless smoke tests. Extend the banktest pattern: mkbanktest.py (or a sibling script) emits a minimal iNES ROM targeting a computed-window sketch board (nes-uxrom.map from gradle buildMap), run-banktest.sh gains a NES loop arm (-loader NesRomLoader), VerifyBankTest/golden dump asserts block names + overlay space names + a bank-switch annotation. Fixture should include at least one non-home bank reference so overlay retargeting is exercised. Also empirically confirm overlay space name == block name (no Ghidra mangling) and record the result as a comment on OverlayNaming (see grm-5tl.14 part 3 trap).
notes:

title: banktest RMW-split fixture for READ_WRITE reference retargeting (grm-5tl.9)
description: grm-5tl.9 split READ_WRITE references across write-under-ROM boundaries (write->onWrite occupant primary, read->read occupant). The existing banktest suite proves the common path is regression-free but does NOT exercise the new RMW-split path. Add a fixture: e.g. INC $A000 in C64 state 7 (BASIC read / RAM_A000 write-under-ROM) and assert a WRITE overlay ref to RAM_A000 plus the read resolving to base BASIC (not misdirected solely to RAM_A000, the pre-fix bug). Note the home/base interaction is subtle (when the read occupant is the home occupant the read stays as the base ref), so design the discriminating assertion carefully.
notes:
Added banktest4 fixture exercising the READ_WRITE reference-split path in BoardBankAnalyzer.retargetReferences.

Fixture (tools/banktest/mkbanktest.py, BANKTEST4): LDA #$37 / STA $01 (bank -> 7, the C64 default: LOROM home occupant = BASIC) / INC $A000 (EE 00 A0, a read-modify-write across the write-under-ROM boundary: read occupant BASIC is home so stays on the base ref; write occupant RAM_A000 via BASIC.on_write is non-home so gets a WRITE overlay ref) / RTS.

VerifyBankTest.java: added checkBanktest4() dispatched via name.contains("banktest4") (checked before banktest2/banktest3/banktest, no prefix-collision risk since none of those names are substrings of banktest4 or vice versa). Three assertions, all discriminating against the pre-fix single-overlay-ref-to-write-target bug:
  D1: primary WRITE overlay ref RAM_A000::a000 exists at 0805.
  D2: no READ overlay ref exists at 0805 (pre-fix, the whole RMW -- including the read -- was misdirected to RAM_A000 as a single ref; this would show up as a READ ref here too, or the WRITE ref's type would encode both).
  D3: exactly 1 overlay ref total at 0805 (rules out an accidental extra ref).
Dump format was NOT changed -- the existing dump (REF ... <space> <RefType> primary=<bool>) already includes RefType, so it was already discriminating; no re-blessing of banktest/banktest2/banktest3 goldens was needed (confirmed via git diff: empty, only banktest4.dump added as new file).

Verification: gradle buildExtension (GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR override to 12.1.2) -> reinstalled extension -> tools/banktest/run-banktest.sh check showed D1/D2/D3 all PASS and produced dump 'COMMENT 0803 bank -> 7 (BASIC/IO/KERNAL)' + 'REF 0805 -> RAM_A000::a000 WRITE primary=true' (no READ ref line) -> manually inspected -> blessed banktest4.dump -> re-ran check -> SUITE OK, all 4 fixtures pass, other 3 goldens untouched.

Pre-fix-would-fail argument: pre-fix retargetReferences emitted a single overlay ref per instruction keyed off writeTarget only (no read/write split), so for INC $A000 in state 7 it would add ONE overlay ref to RAM_A000 with the ref's isRead()/isWrite() flags coming from the original READ_WRITE RefType, i.e. still isRead()==true. That ref is what D2 checks for and fails on (readOverlay would be non-null, pointing to RAM_A000 rather than nothing/base). Also D3's count would still be 1 by coincidence in this single-ref case, but D2 alone is the discriminating criterion: pre-fix the read is misdirected to RAM_A000 instead of correctly resolving to base-space BASIC.

(2) C64PrgLoader.java:140 hardcodes region name RAM_MAIN to trigger carve-around-load; move to a descriptor flag (e.g. load_target: true) - the class javadoc claims nothing is hardcoded. (3) the <window>_B<value> overlay naming is a stringly-typed contract built at NesRomLoader:284 and parsed at BoardBankAnalyzer:486/724; centralize construction/parsing on the shared model. design:
REFINED DESIGN (research 2026-07-10, anchored to ddbaf5f). Land as ONE bead, THREE commits, order: Part 3 -> Part 1 -> Part 2 (Part 3 first so Part 1's unified NES code calls OverlayNaming from the start; Part 2 last so failures are attributable after the risky layout change proves clean).

PART 3 — centralize <window>_B<value> naming (smallest, do first).
Sites (grep-verified): construction at NesRomLoader.java:319 (name + "_B" + v) and BoardBankAnalyzer.java:767 (computed.name() + "_B" + bankValue, builds the lookup name in retargetReferences); parse at BoardBankAnalyzer.java:487-496 (clampToResidence: startsWith(w.name()+"_B") + substring + parseInt in try/catch). Prose-only mentions in javadoc are fine as-is.
Design: static nested class DescriptorSupport.OverlayNaming with bankBlockName(String window, int value) and Integer parseBankValue(String window, String spaceName) (null on non-match or NumberFormatException — replaces the inline try/catch). ~20 lines + 3 call-site edits.
TRAP (key one): addOverlayRef resolves the overlay space by EXACT name (getAddressSpace(targetSpaceName), miss = silent logged skip at BoardBankAnalyzer.java:784-787). Ghidra auto-uniquifies colliding overlay space names, so a name collision at block-creation time would silently break retargeting downstream. Mitigation: add a one-line sanity check in NesRomLoader at block creation — compare created MemoryBlock.getName() against the intended OverlayNaming name and log loudly on mismatch. Also verify empirically during the NES smoke test that space names equal block names; document the finding on OverlayNaming.

PART 1 — unify home-in-base window placement (largest).
Current: NesRomLoader.java:263-330 (computed windows: evaluate maps.expr per field value, home = v == initialValue, FileBytes-backed createWindowBlock at 438-449, refuses occupant windows at 275-280 with "C64 loader's job" log); C64PrgLoader.java:155-194 (enumerated occupants: homeState row from banking.states matching initial_state, createWindowOccupant at 309-334, uninitialized blocks, io-kind occupant only materialized when home via createIoSubregions).
Design: DescriptorSupport gains
  @FunctionalInterface WindowCandidate { MemoryBlock place(Program, AddressSpace, boolean isHome, long start, long length, MessageLog); }
  record NamedCandidate(String name, WindowCandidate candidate) {}
  static void placeHomeInBaseWindow(Program, AddressSpace, long start, long length, List<NamedCandidate>, String homeName, MessageLog)
Shared piece is strictly "N named things, one is home -> home non-overlay in base space, rest overlays" (preserves the home-in-base invariant from SCHEMA.md / project memory). Stays loader-local: NES expr evaluation/checkRange (filter out-of-range BEFORE building candidates), PlacedWindow vector bookkeeping; C64 states-table lookup, io-kind carve (its closure is a no-op returning null when non-home — helper must tolerate null from place()). homeName-not-found: helper accepts it; caller logs (wording differs per loader). NES candidate naming calls OverlayNaming.bankBlockName (Part 3 dependency).
Effort: ~40 lines DescriptorSupport, ~30-line delta per loader (net reduction). RISK: load-time layout must be byte-identical — block names, ranges, isOverlay flags, FileBytes offsets, comments.

PART 2 — RAM_MAIN hardcode -> load_target descriptor flag (small, land last).
Current: C64PrgLoader.java:141-150 dispatches on name equals "RAM_MAIN" -> createRamMainSplit (244-283; falls back to one plain block if PRG doesn't fit; else splits region into up to two uninitialized blocks around the PRG). Class javadoc (44-52) claims nothing hardcoded — currently false.
ADDITIONAL HARDCODE the original finding missed: createRamMainSplit line 274/280 names split blocks String.format("RAM_MAIN_%04X", ...) — fix to region.get("name") + "_%04X" in the same commit (same root cause).
Layering: (1) machines/c64.yaml RAM_MAIN region gains load_target: true; (2) MapCompiler.buildRegions (~192-216) adds copyIfPresent(region, r, "load_target") alongside readable/writable/executable; (3) MAP_FORMAT.md regions section + SCHEMA.md get a short paragraph (it's a loader-behavior flag, not a permission — own paragraph, not under Block permissions); (4) loader dispatch becomes region.has("load_target") && getAsBoolean().
Validation: MapCompiler rejects MORE THAN ONE load_target region (build-time shape error) but does NOT require one — "needs a load target" is a loader property (NES boards correctly have zero); C64PrgLoader logs clearly if it finds none.

VERIFICATION: gradle compileJava (GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR=D:/ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC env var — NOT -P, env var wins in this build.gradle); gradle buildMap + validateSketches (Part 2); tools/banktest run-banktest.sh check after EVERY part (C64 end-to-end: block creation, overlay naming, retargeting — catches Part 1/2 C64 regressions).
COVERAGE GAP: banktest is C64-only; NOTHING automated exercises NesRomLoader/NesBankingAnalyzer. Part 1/3 NES changes need at minimum a manual analyzeHeadless smoke against nes-uxrom.map comparing block names/ranges/perms/overlay-space names pre/post. Proper fix tracked separately (see NES banktest bead).
