title: Banking analyzer efficiency: avoid whole-program re-analysis + memoize strategy dispatch
description: BoardBankAnalyzer: (1) the AddressSetView set param is never used; every added() re-seeds from all entry points/functions and re-runs the full fixpoint, and phase-2 side effects trigger framework re-runs -> up to O(N x wholeProgram). Cache phase-1 output across re-runs or gate on whether set changed reachable state. (2) computeSwitch runs every strategy on every worklist dequeue; the writesInRange/writesMechanism predicate is instruction-only (state-independent) -> compute the mechanism-write candidate set once; memory-latch computeSwitch is fully state-independent and memoizable per address. (3) MemoryLatch.bankInvariantRomByte linear-scans all memory blocks per call (O(banks)); build an overlay-covered interval index at configure(). Correctness-sensitive; needs care + banktest verification. Deferred from /simplify.
design:
REFINED DESIGN (research 2026-07-10, anchored to ddbaf5f). All three claims verified against current code. Split into three child beads (this bead becomes the tracker); recommended landing order: claim 3 -> claim 2 -> claim 1. No perf baseline exists — banktest fixtures are 20-90 byte correctness fixtures; all three costs are theoretical at current sizes and become real only on 32KB-512KB images with many re-run rounds.

CLAIM 3 (child a) — bankInvariantRomByte overlay index. STRONGEST STANDALONE.
Current: MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.bankInvariantRomByte (:145-163) linear-scans all blocks per call (:150-156); called <=~3x per latch-write dequeue (resolveLoad hook :89-97 within MAX_BACKWARD_SCAN=16, plus busConflict branch :113-121).
Design: at configure(), build an AddressSet overlayCoveredRanges = union of base-space shadows of every overlay block (blocks are loader-placed before analyzers run and phase 2 never adds blocks — snapshot stays valid for analyzer lifetime). bankInvariantRomByte becomes block-checks + overlayCoveredRanges.contains(addr) (O(log n)). Effort small; risk very low; identical semantics. Verify: unit test old-vs-new across synthetic overlay layouts (bitalgebra-style differential), plus banktest byte-identity.

CLAIM 2 (child b) — strategy dispatch memoization. CHEAP, MARGINAL ALONE — bundle with claim 3.
Current: runDataflow loop :426-433 runs every strategy's computeSwitch per worklist.poll (:418). Verified: writesInRange (:128-137) and writesMechanism (:71-74) are instruction-only. KEY REFINEMENT: MemoryLatch computeSwitch (:100-126) is PROVABLY state-independent — its resolveLoad hook ignores inStateAtStore, and StoredValueScanner.resolveStoredValue uses inStateAtStore ONLY to forward to hooks.resolveLoad (:171). RegisterWrite computeSwitch (:96-106) DOES return inStateAtStore from its hook — state-dependent, NOT memoizable per address.
Design: (1) Map<Address, MatchInfo> switchCache LOCAL to each runDataflow call (never a field — discard per call, zero staleness; phase 1/2 separation means no code appears mid-fixpoint, worklist never sees newly disassembled addresses). MatchInfo = {matchedStrategy, cachedResult-if-cacheable}. (2) default boolean cacheable() {return false;} on BankSwitchStrategy; MemoryLatch overrides true. (3) On dequeue: cacheable hit -> reuse result; non-cacheable hit -> invoke only the known-matched strategy (skips other predicates); miss -> existing loop, populate. Note mergeAndEnqueue (:458-473) only re-enqueues on state change, so dequeues per address are bounded by lattice height — payoff is a small constant factor. Risk low: pure memoization, banktest must be byte-identical.

CLAIM 1 (child c) — redundant whole-program re-runs. CORRECTNESS-SENSITIVE; GATED ON A FIXTURE.
Current: added() (:144-336) never reads set; runDataflow (:391-456) seeds from ALL entry points + ALL functions (:401-409); phase 1 runs twice when helpers found (:284, :290); phase 2's addOverlayRef fires DisassembleCommand (:812) / CreateFunctionCmd (:816) -> AutoAnalysisManager re-invokes added() with the delta set -> full reseed+fixpoint again. Up to O(rounds x wholeProgram).
CRITICAL INSIGHT: the reseed-everything behavior is LOAD-BEARING — it is how bank state reaches newly disassembled overlay functions (their callers are outside the delta set). "Only process set" is WRONG; a one-shot guard is WRONG (would silently under-annotate cross-bank calls discovered after round 1). Correct scope: skip the ENTIRE re-run iff nothing relevant changed.
Design (fingerprint-gated all-or-nothing skip): static WeakHashMap<Program, Long> keyed by Program identity; fingerprint = functionCount + numInstructions (O(1) reads; safe over-approximation — this analyzer only changes those via its own phase-2 side effects). At top of added() (after mapPath/banking gates): fingerprint match -> log + return true. Write back the fingerprint AFTER phase 2 (so its own side effects force the next round to run). Never cache/diff-merge phase-1 output — annotateBankSwitch (:625-665) never overwrites existing bank-> comments (:658-664), so a stale partial merge would worsen an existing (orthogonal, pre-existing) staleness quirk; all-or-nothing recompute avoids it entirely.
HARD PREREQUISITE before landing: a fixture engineered to require >=2 disassembly rounds (e.g. overlay-bank JSR chain 3+ banks deep) asserting the deepest bank still resolves under skip logic, or a log-based assertion counting full-work runs — current fixtures converge in ~1 round and can't prove the skip doesn't fire early. Document the fingerprint's coverage assumptions at the cache field (future context_register-reading changes could invalidate it silently).

VERIFY (all): GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR=D:/ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC gradle compileJava; banktest run-banktest.sh check byte-identical. Claim 3 also wants a NES/memory-latch fixture (shipped fixtures are C64/register-write — ties into grm-5tl.17).
notes: Split 2026-07-10 after research: this bead is now the tracker holding the full design; implementation lives in children .13.1 (overlay index — land first), .13.2 (dispatch memoization — bundle with .13.1), .13.3 (fingerprint skip — correctness-sensitive, gated on a multi-round fixture per its acceptance criteria; land last). Note: shipped banktest fixtures are all C64/register-write, so .13.1 would ideally get a memory-latch (NES) fixture — ties into grm-5tl.17.
close_reason: Tracker complete: all three children landed and verified against the golden suite. .13.1 overlay-coverage AddressSet index + .13.2 strategy-dispatch memoization (3c89f59), .13.3 fingerprint-gated re-run skip with its multi-round acceptance fixture (8e23842 + this commit).

title: Extract descriptor parsing from the ~200-line added() into BoardModel.parse()

design:
REFINED DESIGN (research 2026-07-10, anchored to commit ddbaf5f).

EXTRACTION BOUNDARY: added() spans lines 144-336 and does 14 jobs. title: Collapse per-bit loops in StoredValueScanner to bit-parallel algebra
description: StoredValueScanner.java:188-233. combine() and fullyDeterminedByAccumulator() are per-bit for-loops that are pure bit algebra. fullyDeterminedByAccumulator == ((~aAcc | oAcc) & mask) == mask (one line). combine == knownMask = mask & (oAcc | ~aAcc | base.knownMask()); bits = mask & (oAcc | (aAcc & base.bits())). Deferred from /simplify because the derivation wants a unit-test pass to confirm (bit-priority oAcc>aAcc-clear>base must be preserved). Add a focused unit test first, then collapse. Quality-only, no behavior change intended.
notes: Done. Collapsed combine() and fullyDeterminedByAccumulator() to bit-parallel one-liners, gated by a new exhaustive equivalence check (tools/bitalgebra/BitAlgebraEquivalence.java + 'gradle verifyBitAlgebra', a new no-dep bitAlgebraCheck source set). The check CAUGHT A BUG in the bead's proposed derivation: 'bits = mask & (oAcc | (aAcc & baseBits))' omits the & baseKnown gate, so it sets result bits in UNKNOWN positions (known=0), diverging from the loop and breaking BankState.equals() (which findHelpers' const-merge relies on). Correct form: bits = mask & (oAcc | (aAcc & base.knownMask() & base.bits())) & 0xFF. knownMask = mask & (oAcc | ~aAcc | base.knownMask()) & 0xFF. fullyDetermined = ((~aAcc|oAcc)&mask)&0xFF == mask&0xFF. Proof is complete (bitwise-independent -> 256 enumerated per-bit cases) + 20M-case fuzz. Behavior also still guarded end-to-end by VerifyBankTest banktest2 C1/C2/C4/C6.
close_reason: Collapsed to verified bit-parallel forms; exhaustive equivalence check added (gradle verifyBitAlgebra). Caught+corrected an error in the bead's own derivation.

title: iNES parse ignores NES 2.0 and is vulnerable to DiskDude flags7 corruption
description: NesRomLoader.java:103. mapper = (h[7]&0xF0) | ((h[6]&0xFF)>>4) unconditionally merges flags7 high nibble; prgBanks = h[4]&0xFF ignores NES 2.0 size/mapper extension. NES 2.0 signaled by (h[7]&0x0C)==0x08, never checked. Failure: (a) a mapper-0 ROM with classic DiskDude! corruption in bytes 7-15 has h[7] high nibble 0x40 -> read as mapper 0x40, wrong/absent board; (b) NES 2.0 image with mapper>=256 or PRG>4MB truncated. Fix: detect NES 2.0 header and honor/ignore flags7 accordingly. Verdict PLAUSIBLE.

title: M3: MMC3 — select-data + mode-register strategies, mode-swapped windows
description: Per docs/vision-board-banking.md M3: select-data strategy ($8000 even selects target state field R0-R7, $8001 odd writes it — model R6/R7 PRG fields; CHR fields deferred with PPU space) + mode-register ($8000 bit 6 swaps which of $8000/$C000 is switchable vs second-last-fixed). 8K banks: overlay-interim L4 hits ~64 overlays on one window per layout — measure and record the pain as evidence for the M5 core hook (RFC #9349). Function-level bank-state requirements + call-graph propagation land here (large MMC3 libraries need it). Acceptance targets: SMB3, Crystalis, Kirby's Adventure.
design:
DESIGN (research 2026-07-10, anchored to current engine post grm-5tl.12 refactor). Sub-bead split at bottom; shared prerequisite with grm-hsv flagged.

HEADLINE ENGINE GAP: memory.layouts[] is SCHEMA-COMPLETE BUT ENGINE-ABSENT. MapCompiler validates and emits layouts (cross-validating when: keys against banking.state), but NOTHING consumes them: BoardModel.parse reads only top-level windows[]; NesRomLoader.load reads only windows[] and hardcodes "bank field = first state field". nes-mmc3.yaml declares windows: [] with everything in layouts: — today's loader would create ZERO PRG blocks. Layout consumption is the shared prerequisite for BOTH MMC3 and MMC1 (grm-hsv says verbatim "mode-dependent layouts from schema v2") — file ONCE as a shared bead.

STATE BUDGET: prg_mode(1) + R6(6) + R7(6) = 13 bits of the 31-bit cap — no pressure. Real ceiling found instead: StoredValueScanner.combine masks & 0xFF (single 6502 register scale). Strategies must resolve the stored byte at <=8-bit scale locally then shift into board-state position (both existing strategies do this); passing a 13-bit board mask into resolveStoredValue would silently truncate — implementation pitfall, not schema limit.

MMC3 FACTS THAT MATTER STATICALLY: $8000-$9FFE EVEN = bank select (bits 0-2 target R0-R7; bit 6 PRG mode; bit 7 CHR — defer); $8001-$9FFF ODD = data to selected register. Mode 0: $8000=R6, $A000=R7, $C000=second-last fixed, $E000=last fixed. Mode 1: $8000<->$C000 swap. 8K granularity. MIRRORING: any even/odd address in the whole range works — the sketch's select_address:0x8000/data_address:0x8001 params are WRONG vs hardware; recognizer must be (addr & 1) over the range. Fix the sketch in sub-bead 2.

DESIGN A — select-data strategy (SelectDataBankSwitchStrategy):
- computeSwitch(program, instr, inState) ALREADY receives inState — no interface change needed for state-dependent dispatch.
- select = a genuine 3-bit tracked field of banking.state, written by even-address stores via existing resolveStoredValue machinery (bits 0-2). Odd-address store: if inState's select fully known and in targets {6:R6, 7:R7} -> recover byte, overwrite ONLY that field's bits (computeSwitch returns the whole new state, not a delta — merge inState's other fields back in, like MemoryLatch does).
- POISON POLICY (refined from bead text): select UNKNOWN -> R6 AND R7 both unknown (either could be written). Select KNOWN but 0-5 (CHR, untracked) -> leave R6/R7 UNTOUCHED — this case is per-frame-frequent in real code (CHR animation swaps); blanket poisoning would destroy PRG state constantly. Data byte unrecoverable with known select -> only the targeted field goes unknown. Test this CHR case explicitly.
- Table-driven loops (LDA table,X) resolve unknown at local scan — but those are the CHR idiom; PRG switches (only 2 registers) are typically direct immediate pairs, which the backward scan handles natively. Helper rescue is sub-bead 4/6 territory.

DESIGN B — mode register + layouts:
- CONFLICT: runDataflow's strategy loop is FIRST-MATCH-WINS (break on first non-null), but a $8000 write must update both select (bits 0-2) and prg_mode (bit 6). Resolution (a): select-data strategy co-emits the mode bit from the same recovered byte (params gain mode_bit -> prg_mode mapping) — narrowest fix, no engine change. Alternative (b) engine merges multiple strategies' field updates — bigger, defer until a board actually needs independent composition; record the limitation.
- Loader: layouts-only boards need per-layout window realization with MODE-QUALIFIED overlay names (same address range, different modes = unrelated content: e.g. W8000_M0_B<v>). Home block = layout matching initial_state's mode + that mode's home bank. Analyzer: ComputedWindowModel keyed by (mode value, window) not name alone; clampToResidence/retargetReferences look up the active layout from the effective state's mode field first.
- YAML: sketch's layouts:/when:{prg_mode:0|1} shape is already right; the gap is 100% runtime consumption.

DESIGN C — overlay scale + RFC evidence: RFC #9349 = OUR OWN posted ghidra GitHub Discussion (docs/rfc-banked-memory.md is source of record; cites upstream #6651/#5913/#7052/#2546/#1332). Measurement: MMC3 fixture at SMB3 scale (512K = 64 banks; 2 switchable windows x 64 banks, POSSIBLY x2 modes if placement differs per mode -> ~256 overlays worst case, confirm empirically). Metrics: block/space count, wall-clock import+analysis vs UxROM baseline, refsAdded, qualitative UI navigability. Record in docs (vision doc M3 section or docs/mmc3-overlay-scale.md), mirror into Discussion #9349.

DESIGN D — function-level bank-state (Phase 1.5): per-function FunctionBankSummary(requiresOnEntry, effectOnExit); effectOnExit = read-off of Phase-1 outStates at RTS/RTI merged; requiresOnEntry = backward property over call graph (bottom-up over SCCs; lattice already monotone/finite so terminates). Existing findHelpers/HelperModel is the single-write special case — NOTE: MMC3 select+data helpers store TWICE, so HelperModel's argReg reconciliation nulls out and current helper propagation degrades for MMC3 (expected temporary precision gap until this lands). M3 SCOPE: requires-bits derivation + violation WARNING bookmarks ONLY (read-only annotation); NO back-propagation/narrowing of Phase-1 state (mutual fixpoint, termination risk) — that's M4+.

SUB-BEADS (proposed):
1. layouts-runtime [SHARED with grm-hsv, blocks both; HIGH risk] — loader + analyzer consume layouts[]; mode-qualified overlay naming; synthetic 2-mode banktest fixture (two memory-latch fields + layouts, decoupled from select-data).
2. select-data-strategy [MEDIUM] — Design A + mode-bit co-emission (B resolution a) + sketch mirroring fix; cheap fixture (LDA #6/STA $8000/LDA #n/STA $8001/JSR); unit-testable standalone, end-to-end gated on 1.
3. mode-register-strategy — fold into 2 (co-resident on same address; Design B ties them).
4. function-summary-propagation [HIGH risk] — Design D, after 2; fixture: two-write helper called from consistent + violating contexts, WARNING only on violator.
5. overlay-scale-measurement [LOW risk, LAST] — Design C, needs 1+2 landed and acceptance titles loading.
6. (optional) select-data-idiom-hardening — two-write helper support in findHelpers if 2 reviews large; coordinate with 4.

RISKS: first-match-wins composition (above); layouts-only loader path completely unexercised today; mode-qualified naming may double overlay counts; HelperModel degradation between beads 2 and 4 (expected, document); CHR-select non-poisoning is THE easy-to-get-wrong case.

Intentionally kept in_progress: parked pending Chris updating the upstream discussion (RFC #9349 — the overlay-scale evidence from grm-6a7.3 feeds the M5 core-hook case). Not stale/stranded; blocked on an external (Chris-owned) upstream action, not on further code here.

title: M3: MMC1 — serial-shift strategy, mode layouts, bank-placement inference
description: Per docs/vision-board-banking.md M3: serial-shift strategy (5 sequential writes deliver one bit each; bit-7 write resets the sequence) as an instruction-sequence state machine over the dataflow engine; mode-register strategy for MMC1 control (PRG modes: 32K / fix-first / fix-last); mode-dependent layouts from schema v2. Flagship for BANK-PLACEMENT INFERENCE: MMC1's 16K banks fit either $8000 or $C000 — assign windows by following flows (recovered switch values, self-reference consistency of each bank's absolute refs, vector anchors) with provenance recorded and user override available; no upfront per-bank options (retires the GhidraNes BankAddressOption pattern, BankAddressOption.java:13-80). Acceptance targets: Metroid, Zelda, Final Fantasy (also a GME AKAO-adjacent interest).
design:
DESIGN (research 2026-07-10, NESdev wiki cross-checked live). Sub-bead split at bottom; shared prerequisite with grm-6a7 (layouts runtime) filed separately.

MMC1 FACTS THAT MATTER STATICALLY: any $8000-$FFFF write with bit 7 set clears the shifter AND ORs Control with $0C (prg_mode -> 3, mirroring untouched) — unconditional. Commit = 5 bit-7-clear writes, bit 0 each; address bits 14:13 matter ONLY on write 5 (00=Control, 01=CHR0, 10=CHR1, 11=PRG bank). Consecutive-cycle ignore: emulation-only, do not model. Control: bits 0-1 mirroring, 2-3 prg_mode (0/1=32K, 2=fix-first, 3=fix-last; 3 = reset-dance default), bit 4 CHR (defer). EMPIRICAL KEY: real games do the reset dance once, early, and never write Control again -> prg_mode is fully known (=3) nearly everywhere; placement "inference" is a rare-residual problem, not the main path.

DESIGN A — serial-shift (the crux):
- Bit-7 reset: ordinary single-write computeSwitch (recognize known bit-7 via existing backward scan; emit prg_mode=3 known, mirroring knownness pass-through). NO engine change.
- Fully-unrolled 5x STA/LSR: five DISTINCT static instructions; strategy statically walks the chain, returns null for writes 1-4, full BankState at write 5 (target from ITS address bits 14:13, value reassembled from the chain). NO engine change.
- CANONICAL LOOP (STA/LSR/DEY/BNE, inlined or JSR'd) — REJECTED APPROACH: shift-register position as hidden BankState fields fails PROVABLY: the loop-head join merges position 0 (entry) with 1-4 (back-edge) -> per-bit AND-agree makes position permanently unknown on the FIRST merge (monotone-shrinking within a pass) -> honest strategy must poison every commit -> 100% of the majority idiom unresolvable. Loop unrolling also rejected (p-code trace replay = emulator territory; listing-level duplication fights Ghidra).
- WORKABLE: idiom recognition, extending the findHelpers precedent one level down. New optional hook on BankSwitchStrategy — findIdioms(Program, Function) -> List<IdiomMatch(exitEdgeTarget, resultState)>, default empty — run per function like findHelpers; BoardBankAnalyzer folds matches into the same switchResults-shaped map, so merge/annotate/retarget/helper propagation need NO further changes (the load-bearing containment property). Recognize: STA-to-range as sole loop-body write + shift of same reg + counted dec-branch trip=5 (or 4+preloop); seed value resolved by the existing scanner applied ONCE to the pre-loop load; commit attached to the loop's EXIT edge (STA's own outState stays no-change).
- Honest degrade: table-driven/memory-seeded values -> existing WARNING path. CHR0/CHR1 targets: structurally recognized, zero tracked fields (verify "recognized but discarded" with a fixture).

DESIGN B — mode handling: MMC1 DOES NOT instantiate a mode-register mechanism — mirroring/prg_mode arrive inside the serial Control byte. serial-shift params need multi-field-per-target deposit:
  targets: {0: {fields: [{name: mirroring, shift: 0, bits: 2}, {name: prg_mode, shift: 2, bits: 2}]}, 3: {fields: [{name: prg_bank, shift: 0, bits: 5}]}}  # 1,2 (CHR) omitted
Params are strategy-opaque pass-through in MapCompiler — no compiler change. Layouts schema (memory.layouts[]/when:) is ALREADY compiled+validated; the gap is runtime consumption (shared bead). MMC1-specific layout wrinkle: 32K mode (0/1) is a genuinely DIFFERENT window (PRG32_B<v>, bank LSB ignored), not a merge of the two 16K windows; confirm during the shared bead that this needs no third window-shape concept. Naming: keep WINDOW_B<v> when shape doesn't vary by mode; WINDOW_M<mode>_B<v> only when it does.

DESIGN C — placement inference, two tiers:
- Tier 1 (primary, retires GhidraNes BankAddressOption by construction): loader materializes the (layout x bank) cross product (MMC1 acceptance titles are 128K = 8 banks; mode 2/3 has ONE switchable 16K window -> real count ~banks x 2, inside the tolerable ceiling); analyzer retargeting does the two-level (mode -> window-set -> bank) lookup from TRACKED state. No upfront user options; normal dataflow resolves placement.
- Tier 2 (rare residual, mode/bank partially unknown): (b) self-reference consistency scoring (candidate bank's absolute refs in-range at $8000 vs $C000; raw-byte operand-pattern scan as a pre-disassembly signal only); (c) vector/fixed-window anchors (last/second_last image offsets, like labelVectorTargets); unresolvable -> existing WARNING, never guess.
- Provenance: extend annotateBankSwitch EOL text with evidence tier ("[switch-value flow]" vs "[inferred: self-ref 7/8]"). Override: loader Option string ("bank=N:window" pairs) via PROGRAM_INFO options, matching BOARD_OPTION_NAME precedent. Analyzer-time overlay-block CREATION (for over-budget boards): legal per Memory API but unproven here (analyzer has no FileBytes; byte-array overload via Memory.getBytes) — DEFERRED from M3 explicitly.

SUB-BEADS (proposed order 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5; 2 can parallel 1):
1. layouts runtime [SHARED with grm-6a7 — filed as its own bead; MEDIUM-HIGH risk; existing goldens must not regress]
2. mode-register strategy class [LOW; MMC3 needs it, MMC1 doesn't; register-write-shaped]
3. serial-shift strategy [HIGH — the findIdioms hook is new engine surface; fixtures: unrolled, inlined loop, JSR'd loop, bit-7 reset alone, table-driven-unresolvable, CHR-write-discarded; build loop matcher from REAL commercial MMC1 disassembly patterns, not wiki-invented shapes]
4. nes-mmc1.yaml descriptor + registry wiring (ines_mappers: [1]) [LOW-MED; where the seams meet; end-to-end Metroid-shaped fixture]
5. placement Tier 2 + provenance/override [MED; not required for acceptance-title correctness]
+ manual acceptance gate: Metroid/Zelda/FF1 (real ROMs, CI-excluded per convention).

RISKS: findIdioms hook shape unproven — prototype against landed layouts plumbing BEFORE committing to the descriptor (a hook that doesn't fold into switchResults ripples back); loop-matcher brittleness (DEX vs DEY, 4+1 shapes) — source patterns from real disassemblies; bit-7 partially-known must not silently assume reset (explicit fixture); 32K-window identity question (above).
notes: Design attached 2026-07-10 (research: serial-shift loop idiom requires a findIdioms engine hook — lattice-position-field approach provably fails at the loop-head join; MMC1 needs NO mode-register mechanism, mode bits arrive in the serial Control byte; placement inference demoted to rare-residual Tier 2 since real games fix prg_mode=3 once). Shared layouts-runtime prerequisite = grm-5tl.18. Proposed sub-bead split in design; materialize as children when work starts. Prototype the findIdioms hook shape against landed grm-5tl.18 plumbing BEFORE writing the descriptor.

title: TMode-style bank tracking: model 6510 port as CPU register + per-bit context fields
description:
Adopt the ARM Thumb (TMode) tracking pattern for C64 bank state, per the priority rule: use existing Ghidra infrastructure before rolling our own.

How ARM does it (verified in D:/git/ghidra source):
1. Sleigh models the mode as a REAL CPU REGISTER: ISAModeSwitch (TB). Every mode-changing instruction's pcode writes TB (macro SetThumbMode, ARM.sinc:208-211), so mode changes are ordinary register dataflow visible to SymbolicPropogator, the emulator, and the decompiler.
2. TMode is a 1-bit CONTEXT FIELD controlling decode. Static direct branches stamp the target from sleigh itself via globalset (ARMinstructions.sinc:2416 'TMode done by HAddr24's globalset') — no Java involved.
3. ArmAnalyzer (a ConstantPropagationAnalyzer) bridges dynamic flows: reads the propagator-tracked TB value at computed flows (ArmAnalyzer.java:813) and stamps ProgramContext.setValue(tmodeRegister, target, target, value) (ArmAnalyzer.java:825); future disassembly consumes the context.

Mapping to C64 (hardware-truthful: the 6510 port at $00/$01 is ON THE CPU DIE, not external memory):
- Bundled 6510 sleigh adds a PORT register; specialized constructors for zp opcodes with operand==$01 (STA/LDA/etc $01) read/write PORT instead of memory. Then LDA $01 / AND #$F8 / ORA #$05 / STA $01 is pure register dataflow — whole-value tracking suffices whenever the incoming PORT value is known. SymbolicPropogator failed on this idiom only because the port was modeled as memory.
- c64bank context register gets three 1-bit fields LORAM/HIRAM/CHAREN (c64.yaml already anticipates 'TMode-style' at banking.context_register). RegisterValue natively supports per-bit partial knowledge (value+mask ctor RegisterValue.java:89; combineValues merge :205-233) — C64BankingAnalyzer's PortState(knownMask,bits) is a reimplementation of it.
- initial_state fallback = ProgramContext DEFAULT value on the context register (pspec / setDefaultValue), replacing the hand-rolled 'assumed from initial' logic.

Scope: blocked on bundling the 6510 language (grm backlog). When it lands, refactor C64BankingAnalyzer toward ConstantPropagationAnalyzer + PORT register tracking; keep the mask-algebra backward scan only as fallback for the stock-6502 fallback_language path, or delete it. Genuinely-partial bases (ORA into unknown PORT) still exceed whole-value tracking — per-bit context fields + defaults cover representation and fallback; evaluate whether the residual gap matters on real code.
notes:
Also refines the gib.2/RFC #9349 claim: 'SymbolicPropogator cannot resolve masked idioms' is true only while the port is modeled as memory. Precise upstream framing: whole-value tracking is sufficient once banking mechanisms are modeled as registers (as ARM does); what's missing in-tree is per-bit partial knowledge of VALUES (RegisterValue covers context/storage, not VarnodeContext propagation).
2026-07-07 abstraction refinement (user-driven): the general stack is 4 layers — (1) mechanism register definition [language, only when architecturally on-die]; (2) mechanism-write detection + value recovery [analyzer, strategy-driven]; (3) interpretation into bank state [descriptor data]; (4) application to decode/refs [context + RFC hook, universal]. What makes tracking cheap is layer-2 STATIC IDENTIFIABILITY of mechanism writes, not on-die-ness (Z80 'OUT (n),A' is equally identifiable with no CPU register). PORT-as-register is a per-CPU layer-2 optimization; layers 2-4 are needed by every banked system. See grm-bk6 note for the system-neutral language requirement.

title: BankingAnalyzer: resolve masked RMW bank switches (LDA $01 / AND #imm / ORA #imm / STA $01)
description: Optional improvement (user request, 2026-07-05). The backward scan in C64BankingAnalyzer.resolveStoredImmediate only recognizes a direct immediate load (LDA/LDX/LDY #imm), so the frequent bit-preserving switch idiom — LDA $01; AND #$F8; ORA #$05; STA $01 (preserving cassette bits 3-5) — currently degrades to UNKNOWN + warning bookmark. Two implementation routes: (a) extend the backward scan to evaluate AND/ORA immediate chains symbolically over just the bank bits: after AND #imm the tracked bits are prev&imm, after ORA #imm prev|imm; whenever (andImm & mechanism.mask)==0 the ORA fully determines the new state (state = oraImm & mask) with NO knowledge of the prior value — this covers the canonical idiom statically; chains that leave bank bits dependent on the unknown prior value stay UNKNOWN. (b) heavier: use SymbolicPropogator/VarnodeContext to ask for the register value at the store (handles loads from other addresses, TAX chains etc.) — more coverage, more machinery. Route (a) recommended first; keep (b) as a follow-on if real PRGs show patterns (a) misses. Gotcha reminder: bare immediates come from getOpObjects() Scalar, not CodeUnit.getScalar().
notes:
ORDERING REVISED (user, 2026-07-05): PREFER existing Ghidra register-value-tracking infrastructure over the custom backward scan — try route (b) FIRST: SymbolicPropogator/VarnodeContext (ghidra.program.util; the engine behind ConstantPropagationAnalyzer, confirmed in the gib.2 hook-point research to track register->value/space along flow) to ask for the stored register's value at the STA $01 site; also check whether ProgramContext already holds an analysis-set value there. If the infra route is impractical for our analyzer's position in the pipeline (e.g. constant propagation hasn't run yet at REFERENCE_ANALYSIS.after(), or 6502 coverage is weak), THEN fall back to route (a): extend the backward scan with the AND/ORA mask algebra (bits = (prev & andImm) | oraImm; known iff andImm clears all mechanism.mask bits). Scan route stays documented as the fallback, not the default.
DESIGN (2026-07-07, pre-dispatch): mask-algebra backward scan formalized — maintain (A_acc,O_acc) meaning final=(x&A_acc)|O_acc over unknown prior x; seed A_acc=0xFF,O_acc=0 at the store; stepping BACK over AND #a: A_acc'=a&A_acc; over ORA #o: O_acc'=(o&A_acc)|O_acc; bank bit determined iff A_acc bit==0 or O_acc bit==1; early-stop when all mechanism.mask bits determined (prior register content irrelevant); LDA #imm terminates fully-known with state=((imm&A_acc)|O_acc)&mask. Subsumes the existing immediate-load case. EOR/RMW-in-place stay UNKNOWN. INFRA EXPECTATION to verify: SymbolicPropogator tracks full values, so LDA $01 (memory read) poisons the chain — likely CANNOT resolve the masked idiom; subagent must time-box the infra investigation, report the conclusion, and implement the algebra as the core resolver either way (infra consult optional if trivially feasible).
DESIGN REFINEMENT (user, 2026-07-07): track PORT BITS individually, not just the combined PLA state — LDA $01/AND #$FE/STA $01 (BASIC off via LORAM bit 0) leaves bit0 KNOWN=0 with bits1-2 unknown; per-bit knowledge still determines windows whose occupant agrees across all consistent states. Representation: PortState(knownMask,bits); dataflow merge keeps agreeing known bits (knownMask' = k1&k2&~(v1^v2)). KEY COMPOSITION WIN: when the chain's base load is LDA $01 itself, x = the tracked in-state at the store — so masked RMW from a fully-known state resolves EXACTLY (7 -> AND #$FE -> 6), no heuristic. Bit known iff aAcc bit==0 (forced 0) | oAcc bit==1 (forced 1) | (base==port-load AND in-state bit known). FALLBACK (user): for still-unknown bits, assume initial_state values when resolving occupants; bank comments must distinguish known vs assumed bits; WARNING bookmark only when NO bank bit is known at a mechanism store. Abort composition if backward scan crosses another mechanism write.
close_reason: Implemented + independently re-verified (Ghidra 12.1.2 headless, banktest2 + banktest regression). Per-bit PortState(knownMask,bits) replaces the int state: dataflow merge keeps agreeing known bits only (monotone shrink, terminating); store resolution = backward mask-algebra scan with (aAcc,oAcc) accumulators composing AND#imm/ORA#imm, terminating at LDA#imm (fully known), a load of the mechanism address itself (base = tracked in-state — so LDA $01/AND #$FE/STA $01 from known state 5 resolves EXACTLY to 4), or any clobber incl. crossing calls (review fix: JSR fall-through passes the block-linkage check, so calls must clobber explicitly) and crossing mechanism writes (abort, unsound to inherit). Occupant resolution assumes initial_state for unknown bits (user fallback); partial switches get 'bank -> 7? (...) [known: LORAM=1; assumed from initial: HIRAM,CHAREN]' comments; WARNING bookmark only when NO bank bit is known. INFRA FINDING (step 0): SymbolicPropogator/VarnodeContext track whole register values — LDA $01 (unknown memory) poisons the chain; no per-bit partial-knowledge model exists in-tree, so the mask algebra is necessary, not a workaround. All 6 banktest2 criteria + 4 banktest regression criteria pass.

title: Descriptor schema: per-occupant executable override (CHARGEN font ROM should be x=false)
description: canExecute() in C64PrgLoader derives the execute permission purely from kind (rom->x=true), so the CHARGEN overlay is currently marked executable even though it is glyph bitmap data. Add an optional per-occupant/per-region 'executable:' override to the YAML schema + map compiler + loader (default stays kind-derived), and set chargen executable:false in machines/c64.yaml. Surfaced by the gib.2 RFC execute-mode discussion (2026-07-05): the RFC's analyzer-compat example claims a sensible descriptor marks font ROM non-executable — make our own descriptor do so.
design: DECISION (user, 2026-07-05): Option 1 — kind-derived defaults + sparse per-attribute overrides. Optional boolean fields readable:/writable:/executable: allowed anywhere a kind appears (region, occupant, subregion); kind supplies defaults: ram=r+w+x, rom=r+x, io=r+w (non-x). Rationale/rule for future cases: one-attribute deviation => override; multi-behavior cluster (perms+structs+volatility+storage like io) => new kind. Rejected: new kinds per combo (code change per quirk, taxonomy explosion — option-3-with-worse-ergonomics), required direct perms (abstraction inversion: descriptor states what hardware IS, tools derive treatment; boilerplate; allows kind-contradicting perms). Precedent: MAME address maps (.rom()/.ram() + per-range modifiers). Riders: (a) document kind->defaults table in SCHEMA.md (currently implicit in loader canWrite/canExecute); (b) derive volatile=true for io-kind blocks in loader (MemoryBlock.setVolatile) — stops decompiler folding repeated $D012 reads; (c) set chargen executable:false in machines/c64.yaml. Verify: rebuild + headless smoke shows CHARGEN x=false and IO blocks volatile.
close_reason: Implemented + headless-verified. Sparse readable/writable/executable overrides (kind supplies defaults: ram=r+w+x, rom=r+x, io=r+w) at region/occupant/subregion level across MapCompiler passthrough + loader Perms record/perms() helper; io-kind blocks now marked volatile (setVolatile). c64.yaml: CHARGEN executable:false (headline) + COLOR_RAM executable:false (review catch — kind:ram default would have flipped it x=true vs baseline; 4-bit cells, open-bus fetches; first organic use of the new override). SCHEMA.md gained the kind->defaults table + one-attribute-deviation=>override / multi-behavior-cluster=>new-kind rule; MAP_FORMAT.md documents the passthrough fields. Smoke: CHARGEN x=false, COLOR_RAM x=false vol=false, VIC/SID/CIA/P6510/IO1/IO2 vol=true, baseline otherwise unchanged, Import succeeded.

title: Descriptor-declared matching criteria for game descriptors (deferred identity option)
description:
Deferred from the grm-hb6 identity decision (user chose PRG hash + whole-file SHA-256 for now, 2026-07-31).

IDEA: let a game descriptor declare what it MATCHES (mapper, PRG size, optional byte signature at an offset) so one file can cover a ROM-set variant family -- regional revisions, PRG0/PRG1, bad-dump variants -- instead of one entry per dump. Most expressive and most forgiving of the three identity options considered.

BLOCKERS TO RESOLVE FIRST: ambiguity rule when several descriptors match one ROM, and precedence against an exact-hash match (exact should presumably win). Revisit once there is real hint data and the curated set has enough entries to show whether per-dump fragmentation is actually a problem in practice.

title: Per-game .gdt for types[] (later increment)
description: Types compile per-MACHINE into a .gdt via GdtBuilder (docs/SCHEMA.md:496-500). A per-TITLE type archive is a new build artifact plus a new runtime lookup, so it is deliberately scoped after symbols and comments land. Game-specific structs (level headers, sprite tables, music sequence formats) are exactly the kind of thing a reverse engineer establishes and should not have to re-establish.

title: db3 real ROM: three copy-shaped loops into RAM:0200 recognized but unbounded
description:
Surfaced by grm-phv (2026-07-29) on the db3 (Dragon Ball 3, mapper 16 Bandai FCG) real-ROM
fixture. NOT a regression -- a new observation that the base-reference retargeting made visible.

After MosConstantReferenceAnalyzer landed, db3's REALROM dump gains three CopyLoopAnalyzer
warnings that were not there before:

  e69e [CopyLoopAnalyzer] copy-shaped loop RAM:e7d4 -> RAM:0200 could not be bounded; not applied
  e707 [CopyLoopAnalyzer] copy-shaped loop RAM:e826 -> RAM:0200 could not be bounded; not applied
  e712 [CopyLoopAnalyzer] copy-shaped loop RAM:e7fd -> RAM:0200 could not be bounded; not applied

warnings count 1 -> 4. Everything else in the dump is byte-identical: refs.intoOverlay stays 0,
instrs.inOverlay stays 0, bankComments stays 0, no COPY_ blocks materialized. So nothing is
applied and nothing is wrong -- the recognizer simply gets FURTHER than it used to and then
correctly declines.

WHY grm-phv CHANGED THIS: CopyLoopAnalyzer resolves a loop's source/destination partly through
reference data (StoredValueScanner reads getReferencesFrom; LoopIdioms.overlayWriteTarget reads
write refs). With indexed accesses now referencing the table BASE instead of scattered
base+index addresses, source/dest resolution succeeds on these three loops where it previously
bailed earlier. This is the intended knock-on: better references -> better idiom recognition.

WORTH INVESTIGATING: all three copy into RAM:0200 (a RAM page) from ROM around $e7d4-$e826, and
all three fail the length bound. Likely a dynamically-computed length. If these are real boot
copies, bounding them would materialize three more payloads. Related: grm-2yx already records
db3 reachability problems (its bank-switch routine is never disassembled -- note the pre-existing
first warning, 'no bank-switch write observed ... switch routine may be unreached'), so these
loops may sit in the same unreached region. grm-9a0 (banked sources) may also be relevant.

The db3 golden was blessed to record the new warnings; this bead tracks the underlying question.

title: SMC detection via emulation/debugger + external emulator (VICE) observation
description: Longer-range front-end for the run-from-elsewhere/SMC subsystem: instead of statically pattern-matching copy/upload loops, RUN the code and observe self-modification/copies dynamically. Two tiers: (1) Ghidra p-code emulator / Debugger framework driving the code and capturing writes (builds on the grm-edg EmulationRecovery harness already used by grm-1.7.2 tier 2); (2) external emulator integration -- drive VICE (or an NES/SNES emulator), let it run, and observe the resulting memory image -- as the definitive mechanism for cases too complex to emulate in-process. Feeds the same materialize() core from an observed-transfer front-end. Out of scope for grm-1.7.1; captured for later pursuit.

title: Read jar entry CRCs natively instead of parsing unzip -v text in ext_identity()
description:
Follow-up to grm-lne. Both tools/banktest/run-banktest.sh and realrom-test.sh compute the cache's extension identity by shelling out to 'unzip -v <jar>' and awk-parsing its human-readable table: '$7 ~ /^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}$/ {print $7, $NF}'. That heuristic exists only to skip the header/separator/totals rows and grab the CRC-32 + name columns -- it is brittle (depends on unzip's column layout; $NF truncates names containing spaces) and needs the 'unzip' binary on PATH.

Replace it with a native zip CRC reader that yields (crc, name) pairs directly, no text parsing:
  - Python's zipfile is the natural fit: for zi in zipfile.ZipFile(j).infolist(): print(f'{zi.CRC:08x} {zi.filename}'). run-banktest.sh ALREADY requires Python (PYTHON, for the mk*.py fixture generators), so no new dependency there. realrom-test.sh would gain a Python dependency (today it needs only sha256sum + analyzeHeadless), so gate/fallback accordingly or accept it.
  - Keep the same downstream shape: sort the (crc, name) lines across all installed Extensions jars and sha256 them, so the resulting identity is byte-identical in intent to today's -- purely swapping the CRC *source*, not the key formula. A one-time migration note: switching the reader changes the emitted-line format (e.g. spacing), which changes the identity hash and thus invalidates any existing build/*-cache entries on first run -- harmless (they just re-import once), but worth a comment.

Rationale captured in memory 'gradle-dist-zip-mtime-unstable' (why CRC, not mtime). No behavior change for users; robustness/cleanup only.

title: Speed up golden bless by reusing candidate dump from preceding check run
description: Today build-and-test.sh bless <chunk> and realrom-test.sh bless re-run the full analyzeHeadless import to regenerate goldens, even though a preceding check run already produced the exact candidate dump (and diffed it against the golden). For expensive fixtures -- especially the real-ROM tier where each import is ~1min+ -- this doubles the import cost of the review-then-bless loop. Consider caching the candidate dump from the last check (keyed by fixture inputs + built-extension hash so a stale candidate is never reused) and having bless copy that cached candidate after showing the diff, instead of re-importing. Applies to both tools/banktest/build-and-test.sh (VerifyBankTest dumps) and tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh (RealRomDump). Must preserve the bless-review discipline: still show the diff before accepting, and never bless a candidate whose build/inputs no longer match.
notes: Done in c915ec2. check stashes each candidate dump in a content-addressed cache under build/ (gitignored); bless reuses it when the key still matches, else re-imports. Key = fixture bytes + loader/opts (file args hashed) + dump script + CRC-based extension identity. Extension id must be content-based (unzip -v CRC), NOT the install stamp/mtime: gradle rewrites the dist zip every build so an mtime id never matches across check->bless. Applied to run-banktest.sh + realrom-test.sh. Verified: check->bless reuses all candidates 0 re-imports; dump-script edit forces fresh import; full gate green. realrom path is code-mirrored + syntax-checked but not runtime-tested here (no ROMs).
close_reason: Closed

title: MMC3 bank-> comments show packed composite state value (e.g. 'bank -> 26639?'), hard to read
description: Minor readability finding from grm-hdn (golden smb3.dump). MMC3 bank-> comments render the packed banking.state composite as a single large decimal, e.g. 'bank -> 26639? (select=7,prg_mode=1,r6=0,r7=26)' or 'bank -> 1039?'. The parenthetical field breakdown is correct and useful, but the leading composite number is cryptic for a human (it is the encoded state tuple, not a PRG bank index). Consider suppressing/relabeling the composite for multi-field mode-varying boards, or showing the effective PRG bank per window instead. Low priority; annotations are correct, just not readable at a glance. Many are '?'-uncertain (assumed-from-initial r6/r7), which is expected.
close_reason: MMC3/MMC1/Bandai multi-field bank-> comments now lead with the field tuple (e.g. 'bank -> select=7,prg_mode=1,r6=0,r7=26?') instead of the cryptic packed composite ('bank -> 26639?'). Scoped to computed boards with >1 state field; enumerated (C64) and single-field (UxROM/AxROM/NROM 'bank -> 5 (bank=5)') boards unchanged.

title: Investigate: Ghidra 12.x headless never calls Loader.validateOptions
description:
Surfaced in grm-hsv.3: in Ghidra 12.x, Loader.validateOptions() is invoked ONLY from the GUI import dialogs (ImporterDialog:442, AddToProgramDialog:82, LoadLibrariesOptionsDialog:60) -- the headless/ProgramLoader import path never calls it. grm-hsv.3 worked around this by re-running validation inside NesRomLoader.load() as a safety net. Investigate in depth before trusting validateOptions anywhere else:

1. SCOPE: confirm which entry points do/don't validate -- headless analyzeHeadless, ProgramLoader API, scripting (importFileAsProgram/AutoImporter), batch import. Grep the 12.1.2 source (D:/git/ghidra @ Ghidra_12.1.2_build) for every caller.
2. REGRESSION vs INTENT: did 11.x headless call validateOptions? Is 12.x's ProgramLoader refactor dropping it a deliberate change or a bug? Check release notes / git history / any upstream issue.
3. OUR EXPOSURE: audit our other loaders' validateOptions for headless-bypass risk -- AbstractCbmPrgLoader.validateOptions (ROM-slot file existence/size checks at :220-245) and any symbol-option validation. If those only run in the GUI, a headless import with a bad ROM path could load silently wrong. Decide whether to move/duplicate their checks into load() the way grm-hsv.3 did.
4. PATTERN: settle a project convention -- should all our loaders treat load() as the authoritative validation point (validateOptions = GUI-only UX nicety)? Document it in CLAUDE.md conventions if so.
5. UPSTREAM: if it's a Ghidra regression, consider filing an NSA/ghidra issue.

Refs: memory key 'headless-loader-option-gotchas'; grm-hsv.3 close reason; NesRomLoader.placementError()/load() safety-net pattern.

title: MMC1 Tier-2 self-reference placement inference (deferred from grm-hsv.3)
description: Deferred (c) from grm-hsv.3 (which shipped override + provenance). The rare-residual self-ref scorer: when a switchable bank's placement is unknown from dataflow, score its absolute operand refs in-range at $8000 vs $C000 (raw-byte operand-pattern scan as a pre-disassembly signal only) + vector/fixed-window anchors (reuse last/second_last resolution in DescriptorSupport.evalConstantExpr and the NesRomLoader.labelVectorTargets pattern); unresolvable -> existing WARNING, never guess. Emit '[inferred: self-ref n/m]' provenance in the vocabulary grm-hsv.3 established ('[switch-value flow]' baseline tag already lands in annotateBankSwitch, gated to modeField!=null boards). Needs a purpose-built fixture where placement is genuinely ambiguous AND self-refs disambiguate. Hook points (from grm-hsv.3 exploration): the override already threads BankState+knownMask into BoardBankAnalyzer.retargetReferences and applies in the mode-varying switchable branch -- Tier-2 slots in beside the override as a second fallback when no override is present; annotateOrWarn (knownMask==0 -> WARNING) is the interception chokepoint.

title: C128 loader: mark P8502 prg_placeable so wrapping PRGs can place across $00/$01
description: grm-z15.4 made the CBM PRG loader's additional-placement-target declarative via the prg_placeable region flag and deleted C64PrgLoader's P6510 name hardcode. C128's P8502 io region ($0000-$0001, the 8502 on-die port) is the exact analogue of C64's P6510, but c128.yaml does NOT flag it prg_placeable (left unchanged in grm-z15.4 to preserve C128 behavior, since the C128 loader never had the name hardcode). Consequently a wrapping C128 native PRG that places bytes across $0000/$0001 would fail placement (0 targets) the same way C64 did before. Low priority: wrapping into the 8502 port is a rare/degenerate case. If desired, add 'prg_placeable: true' to the P8502 region in c128.yaml (and add a wrap fixture); the coverage check already tolerates it (C128's ram union would then start at $0000 instead of $0002, still gap-free).
acceptance_criteria: A wrapping C128 PRG placing bytes at $0000-$0001 imports without a placement error; P8502 declared prg_placeable in c128.yaml; c128 map still compiles under the coverage check.

title: banktest: crafted-malformed-map harness for loader degrade paths
description: The C64 PRG loader hardwires its bundled machines/c64.map, so degrade paths that require a malformed/incomplete map (e.g. grm-z15 #4's incomplete-banking window-skip, or a gapped coverage map at import time) cannot be exercised end-to-end by the banktest harness today. Add a mechanism to run a loader against a crafted map: e.g. a tiny bundled machines/test/*.map plus a test-only loader subclass pointing at it, or a harness hook that overrides getMapPath(). Then convert grm-z15.3's inspection-level coverage into a real fixture.
acceptance_criteria: A banktest fixture can import a PRG under a crafted/malformed C64-style map and assert the loader's degrade/validation behavior (clear error or degraded import), covering grm-z15 #4's incomplete-banking path.

title: Decoded CBM BASIC bytes: apply real data types so lines show as analyzed
description: Cosmetic/UX follow-up to the CBM BASIC detokenizing analyzer (epic grm-1.6): the analyzer currently annotates each BASIC line with an EOL comment, but the underlying bytes still render as undefined/undiscovered data in the listing. Touch up the decoded region by applying actual Ghidra data types per line component: (1) line links -> pointers; (2) line numbers -> decimal (unsigned 16-bit LE) words; (3) program 'text' runs (string literals, REM text, and other non-token byte runs) -> Ghidra string data; (4) tokens -> perhaps the appropriate token enum data type (BASIC_V2/V4/V7_TOKEN and the BASIC 7 CE/FE prefix enums), TBD whether per-byte enum data reads well in the listing. Goal: the tokenized BASIC region shows as Analyzed rather than a sea of raw bytes, complementing (not replacing) the detokenized line comments.
acceptance_criteria: BASIC program region in a detokenized fixture listing contains no undefined bytes: line-link pointers, line-number words, typed text runs, token typing decision made (enum or documented why not); existing banktest BASIC golden fixtures updated/blessed accordingly.
notes: References grm-1.4 (first-class PETSCII string support / charset registration): proper PETSCII Ghidra string rendering would make the text-run typing genuinely readable, but the user does not consider it blocking — plain string/byte typing is acceptable until grm-1.4 lands. Recorded as a related (non-blocking) dependency.

title: Add exhaustive C64 PRG size and wrap boundary fixtures
description: Follow up grm-dvx with dedicated integration cases for load $FFFE plus 2 bytes (no wrap), plus 3 bytes (wrap into P6510), exactly 65536 payload bytes accepted with source offsets preserved, and 65537 bytes rejected without a partial Program layout. The implementation already enforces these limits; this bead closes the remaining explicit acceptance-test coverage gap identified in final review.

title: Full C64 BASIC ROM symbol set: needs a clean name-bearing source
description: grm-hnm generated full KERNAL + zeropage symbol sets from c64ref's PRG-guide text, but BASIC ROM ($A000-$BFFF) symbols could NOT be cleanly generated: c64ref's only BASIC-region material is Lee Davison's fully-commented ROM disassembly (src/c64disasm/c64disasm_en.txt) which has (a) free-text COMMENTS, not symbol NAMES, and (b) separate authorship/licensing from the BSD-2 repo wrapper (Davison 2012), i.e. the encumbrance grm-1.2 flagged. So basic-api currently carries only a 2-entry inline seed (BASIC cold/warm start vectors at $A000/$A002 -- pure facts). To build a FULL BASIC symbol set, find a clean name-bearing source: options -- (a) a permissively-licensed BASIC ROM label list (VICE .sym, cc65/KickAssembler C64 BASIC symbol files, sajattack/c64-asm-labels -- but CHECK LICENSE, Leemon-derived); (b) synthesize names from c64disasm HEADINGS if the license is deemed OK (BSD repo wrapper) taking only addresses+short names (facts) not Davison's prose; (c) hand-curate the well-known BASIC entry points. Then emit machines/generated/c64ref-basic.yaml and restore the basic-api source: reference. Low priority (games rarely call BASIC ROM; set is default off). Deferred from grm-hnm 2026-07-13.

title: docs/testing.md + AGENTS.md pointer: make the test harness legible to agents/contributors
description: Document the testing strategy so subagents stop hunting for JUnit scaffolding that does not exist (recurring time sink): what the golden-image E2E suite is, how to run check/bless, what each chunk covers, when to add a unit test vs extend VerifyBankTest criteria vs add a golden fixture, and the bless-review discipline (a diff in expected/ is a behavior change needing review, not an auto-accept). Add a short pointer in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md at repo root so agents find it first.
notes: grm-32f.1 spike outcome (2026-07-23) to document in docs/testing.md: JUnit-via-Ghidra-scaffolding is FEASIBLE and GO. gradle test works headless against the binary install (11 tests green): pure JUnit for pure logic (BankState, MapCompiler -- ~instant), and AbstractGenericTest + ProgramBuilder("6502:LE:16:default") for Program/Instruction fixtures (~1.5s/class Application bootstrap). HARD RULES for the docs: use ProgramBuilder with the shipped 6502 language, NOT ToyProgramBuilder (Toy:*:builder language absent from binary install -> LanguageNotFoundException); JUnit4 + hamcrest from Maven, gradle useJUnit() not useJUnitPlatform(); test source set needs its own testImplementation fileTree(Ghidra libs)+main.output+gdtBuilder.output+snakeyaml+junit. THREE-TIER test taxonomy for the 'when to add which' section: (1) pure JUnit for pure logic; (2) AbstractGenericTest+ProgramBuilder for loader/analyzer/strategy logic needing a Program; (3) bash E2E golden suite (run-banktest.sh) stays the out-of-process acceptance authority for the real import+analyzer pipeline -- NOT replaceable by in-JVM fixtures. Migration of existing verifiers = grm-32f.4; wiring gradle test into the gate = grm-32f.5.
close_reason: Wrote docs/testing.md: the canonical testing guide making the harness legible. Opens with the explicit 'if you're looking for JUnit, read this' note (the recurring agent time-sink). Documents the three tiers (pure JUnit / AbstractGenericTest+ProgramBuilder / E2E golden image), the E2E suite mechanics (mk*.py generators -> build-and-test.sh check -> real-loader analyzeHeadless -> VerifyBankTest dump diff vs expected/*.dump, isolated per-worktree install), the chunk map (grm-32f.2) with the dev-loop-subset vs full-gate-acceptance rule, the JUnit layer constraints from grm-32f.1 (6502 not Toy, JUnit4 useJUnit, testImplementation deps incl snakeyaml, opt-in status), a 'when to add which tier' decision guide, and the bless discipline (a diff in expected/ is a behavior change needing review, never auto-accept). Added pointers at repo root: AGENTS.md (Testing section before the auto-gen beads blocks) and CLAUDE.md (blockquote atop Build & Test). Docs-only; no code, no gate run needed.

title: VICE .vsf snapshot importer: real-hardware memory image into Program
description: Cheap 80% of the 'real emulator fidelity' path from the grm-1.7.4 survey (docs/smc-survey.md par.4): import a VICE snapshot's C64MEM RAM module (documented .vsf format) as/into a Ghidra Program, so decrypt-on-the-fly and hardware-entangled cases (CIA-timer/raster-derived keys) can be recovered from a real accuracy-emulator run instead of policy-valued p-code emulation. Standalone value beyond SMC (general 'analyze the running game's RAM' workflow). Alternative rejected for now: live TraceRmi VICE connector (no community bridge exists; ghidratrace python client is the kit if ever needed — revisit on demonstrated need).

title: NES board descriptors: Bandai FCG family (mappers 16/157/159) + GxROM (mapper 66)
description: Board-coverage work: Bandai FCG family + GxROM descriptors, using the Dragon Ball ROM collection at Z:/nes/db as real-ROM TEST CASES (user, 2026-07-12: the DB games are NOT music-extraction targets themselves -- they are convenient exercisers for these mappers). Mapper census from Z:/nes/db/mappers.txt: 6x mapper 016 (Bandai FCG/LZ93D50), 2x mapper 066 (GXROM), 1x 157 (Datach Joint ROM System), 1x 159 (LZ93D50 + 24C01 EEPROM). GxROM is the easy half: one register at $8000-$FFFF, PRG bits 4-5 select a 32K bank, CHR bits 0-1 -- a single memory-latch mechanism, simpler than the shipped UxROM board. Bandai FCG is a register-file board: registers at $6000-$7FFF and/or $8000-$FFFF (submapper-dependent), $8/$8008 = 16K PRG bank at $8000 (fixed last bank at $C000), regs 0-7 = CHR banks, $A = IRQ control -- shaped like a select-less multi-register variant; likely fits existing register-write strategy with one mechanism per register address, or motivates a small 'register-file' generalization. 157/159 differ mainly in EEPROM wiring (irrelevant to PRG banking) -- one descriptor with ines_mappers [16,159] plus a Datach variant may suffice; verify against FCEU source at Z:/nes/fceu/boards/bandai.c (local reference implementation) and NESdev. Fixture-first per the banktest discipline; real-ROM check against the Z:/nes/db set.
notes: Z:/nes also holds the FCEU emulator source tree (Z:/nes/fceu, boards/ dir = C reference implementations for every mapper) -- useful oracle for ALL future NES board descriptors, not just these.
close_reason: Bandai FCG/LZ93D50 descriptor (mappers 16/157/159) shipped and fully gated: new nes-bandai-fcg.yaml + memory-latch address-decode predicate (addr_mask/addr_match) + nesbandaitest.nes fixture/golden proving the register-file decode (CHR/IRQ sibling writes are non-latches). GxROM half was already done in grm-9ux. Real-ROM acceptance against Z:/nes/db tracked in grm-hdn.

title: MAP_FORMAT.md overlay-naming table: home-mode non-home-bank row contradicts loader behavior
description: Found during grm-hsv.2: docs/MAP_FORMAT.md's four-row naming table says 'Home mode, non-home bank -> NAME_B<bank>' but the loader's actual contract (grm-5tl.18, confirmed by nesmodetest/nesmmc1test goldens: W8000_M0_B1 with home mode 0) is that MODE-VARYING windows always carry the _M<mode> qualifier — plain NAME_B<v> is reserved for windows that don't vary by mode (flat windows[] and invariant-hoisted layouts windows like MMC3's WA000_B<v>). Fix the table row (and re-read the surrounding prose for the same slip). Docs-only; no code change, no golden churn.
notes: Filed 2026-07-11 from grm-hsv.2 agent report item 7b.
close_reason: MAP_FORMAT.md naming table fixed: home-mode non-home-bank row corrected to NAME_M<mode>_B<bank> (mode-varying windows always carry _M once outside home mode+bank; bare NAME_B<v> is reserved for flat and invariant-hoisted windows). Surrounding prose updated with the rationale (same bank under a different mode = unrelated content) and confirming golden citations (nesmodetest W8000_M0_B1, nesmmc3test WA000_B3); also fixed a stray see-below/above reference. Landed as part of the 2026-07-12 docs-consistency pass.

title: annotateBankSwitch caps known/assumed bit spelling at 8 bits — use board mask width
description: Found during grm-hsv.1: BoardBankAnalyzer.annotateBankSwitch iterates bit < 8 when spelling out per-bit known/assumed lists, so boards with >8 tracked state bits (nes-serialtest = 9: mirroring 2 + prg_mode 2 + prg_bank 5) silently omit the high bits (prg_bank.4) from those lists. Effective value and field rendering are correct — cosmetic only. Fix: iterate to the board mask's width. Touching annotation text = golden churn for any fixture whose comments list bits on a >8-bit board; regenerate affected goldens deliberately.
notes: Filed 2026-07-11 from grm-hsv.1 agent report item 4.
close_reason: Fixed: annotateBankSwitch now iterates to the board mask's width (32 - Integer.numberOfLeadingZeros(mask)) instead of a hardcoded 8. Boards with >8 tracked state bits (nes-serialtest=9, nes-mmc3test2=16) now spell all bits in the known/assumed lists. Blessed nesserialtest.dump (+prg_bank.4) and nesmmc3test2.dump (+r6.4,r6.5,r7.0-r7.5). Full gate green.

title: SMC: decrypt-on-the-fly — EOR-decryptor recognition and emulation-assisted image recovery
description: Use case 2: C64 copy-protection-era code stored encrypted and EORed (with itself, a constant, or a rolling key) in place at runtime, then executed. Static listing of the encrypted bytes is garbage; naive disassembly poisons analysis. Approach candidates (evaluate in this order): (a) EMULATION-ASSISTED: recognize the decryptor entry (small, self-contained loop), run it in Ghidra's p-code emulator (Debugger machinery, headless-scriptable) over a snapshot, capture the decrypted range, and write it back as an alternate view (overlay block 'DECRYPTED_xxxx' or patched bytes + provenance bookmark) for static analysis to proceed; (b) STATIC pattern-match of the common EOR-self/EOR-constant loops (feasible for the simple constant case, hopeless for chained/rolling schemes); (c) documented manual workflow (emulator memory dump import). In-place decryption also needs a 'these bytes were replaced' provenance model — decide whether original-encrypted vs decrypted views both stay navigable. Research Ghidra Debugger emulator APIs for headless use as part of this bead; findings feed the epic's static-vs-emulation design tension.
notes: 2026-07-13 TIER 2 NOW VERIFIED (grm-yxn closed). Both emulation outcomes tested: rolling key (initialized RAM) -> trusted NOTE overlay; hardware key (CIA $DC00) -> suspect WARNING overlay. Tiers 1 (constant, inline) and 2 (rolling/computed, emulated) are both implemented AND tested end-to-end through the real import pipeline (commits 2d3815f, 58d3c03, 2aa079b). REMAINING (minor polish, not blocking): (1) tier-3 'refer to manual workflow' -- the suspect WARNING is the 'detect+downgrade' half; adding VICE-snapshot/Debugger referral TEXT to the warning message is trivial follow-up; (2) auto-disassemble the DECRYPTED_xxxx overlay so the recovered payload shows as code (currently bytes only); (3) generalize beyond C64PrgLoader gate if a second platform needs it. Core deliverable (EOR-decryptor recognition + emulation-assisted image recovery) is DONE and tested.
close_reason: Decrypt-on-the-fly SMC recovery complete and tested end-to-end via the banktest suite. C64DecryptLoopAnalyzer recognizes the in-place EOR decrypt loop and recovers the plaintext into a DECRYPTED_xxxx overlay (encrypted original stays navigable), disassembled as code, with provenance bookmarks + cross-link comment. TIER 1 (constant EOR): inline byte XOR (fixture decryptloop). TIER 2 (rolling/computed): routed to the grm-edg EmulationRecovery harness, run in the p-code emulator during analysis, read back under a dirty-watch -- verified for both the trusted outcome (rolling key in RAM -> NOTE, fixture rollingdecrypt) and the hardware-tainted outcome (CIA-register key -> provenance suspect -> WARNING + manual-recovery referral text, fixture suspectdecrypt). TIER 3 (hardware-keyed): detect-and-refer implemented (WARNING bookmark points at VICE .vsf snapshot import / Debugger Copy-Into-Program). Safety: only the clean down-counting LDX/DEX/BPL form with a JMP into range is auto-applied; everything else is a candidate/warning, never rewritten. No false positives (dump() bookmark filter is *BankingAnalyzer-scoped; no existing golden changed). Key impl note: an indexed operand's base is a Scalar not an Address (no static ref for base+index), so indexedBase accepts both. Commits 2d3815f (tier1), 58d3c03+2aa079b (tier2 via grm-yxn), 8da7796 (polish). REMAINING (deferred, non-blocking): generalize beyond the C64PrgLoader gate to a 6502-generic analyzer if a second platform needs it -- YAGNI until then.

title: MMC1: placement inference Tier 2 + provenance + user override
description: Design C Tier 2 on parent grm-hsv (rare-residual when mode/bank partially unknown): self-reference consistency scoring (absolute refs in-range at $8000 vs $C000; raw-byte operand pre-disassembly signal only); vector/fixed-window anchors; unresolvable -> existing WARNING, never guess. Provenance: extend annotateBankSwitch EOL with evidence tier ('[switch-value flow]' vs '[inferred: self-ref 7/8]'). Override: loader Option string ('bank=N:window') via PROGRAM_INFO, matching BOARD_OPTION_NAME precedent. Analyzer-time overlay creation stays DEFERRED from M3.
notes: Materialized from parent design 2026-07-11 (design sub-bead 5). NOT required for acceptance-title correctness — P4.
close_reason: Shipped user placement override + provenance (Tier-2 self-ref split out to grm-hsv.4 per scope decision). OVERRIDE: loader Option 'NES Placement Override' (headless -loader-placement) takes space-separated window:bank pairs (e.g. W8000:5; COLON separator, not '=', because cmd.exe analyzeHeadless.bat splits arg values on '='). Grammar is a shared DescriptorSupport.parsePlacementOverride (window->bank map) both the loader validates and the analyzer reads via a new engine-generic PROGRAM_INFO key 'Retro Machines.Placement Override'. Validation (unknown window / bank>=prgBanks) runs in NesRomLoader.validateOptions AND -- since Ghidra 12.x ProgramLoader never calls validateOptions on the headless path (only GUI dialogs do) -- is re-run as a safety net in load(), which refuses the import on bad input. BoardBankAnalyzer.retargetReferences now takes BankState inState (was int effective) so the mode-varying switchable branch can apply the override ONLY where the bank field is fully flow-unknown ((knownMask & bankField.positionedMask())==0); flow always wins when it knows even one bit. PROVENANCE: annotateBankSwitch appends '[switch-value flow]' gated to modeField!=null boards (MMC1/MMC3/mode/serial -- C64/PET untouched, zero golden churn there); override sites get 'bank -> N [user override]'. TESTS: new nesmmc1overridetest.nes fixture (unresolvable inline chain -> prg_bank unknown -> override fires -> W8000_M3_B5; then known prg_bank=3 -> flow wins -> W8000_M3_B3), 8 criteria O1-O7 PASS; PlacementOverrideParseTest JUnit (unit chunk) covers the grammar incl. '=' rejection; 5 mode-varying NES goldens re-blessed (verified: every diff is EXACTLY a [switch-value flow] append, set-compared). Full gate 'build-and-test.sh check' green. Negative headless path manually verified: bad window/bank -> descriptive error + Import failed.

title: 6510/6502 language: undocumented NMOS opcodes (opt-in variant)
description: grm-bk6 bundled the 6510 language but deliberately left out the NMOS undocumented/illegal opcodes (LAX/SAX/DCP/ISC/SLO/RLA/SRE/RRA/ANC/ALR/ARR/SBX, the undocumented NOP/SKB/SKW forms, and the unstable AHX/SHX/SHY/TAS/LAS/ANE). Games (incl. C64 music/demo drivers) do use the stable ones. NOT a pure win: Ghidra's stock 6502 omits them precisely because defining them makes previously-invalid bytes in DATA regions (tables, sample data) decode as instructions, so speculative disassembly can march through data instead of stopping — hurting code/data separation on exactly the data-heavy drivers we care about. So the design question is inline-vs-opt-in: prefer a separate ldefs variant (e.g. 6510:LE:16:illegal, or a pspec/cspec variant) or an analyzer option so users opt in, keeping the default 6510 clean. Model the stable illegals with correct pcode; model or omit the unstable ones with a comment. Verify: (a) compiles; (b) banktest suite still byte-identical (valid decode unchanged); (c) targeted test that a few illegal opcodes decode with sane pcode. Reference: masswerk 6502 illegal opcodes; MAME m6510/m6502 dtables at /z/git/mame.
close_reason: Shipped 6510:LE:16:undoc and 6502:LE:16:undoc as opt-in variants; defaults untouched. Semantics vendored verbatim from anarkiwi/deity-informant (Apache-2.0, hardware-oracle validated) rather than hand-derived; NOTICE records attribution. Split 6510.slaspec into 6502core.sinc + 6510port.sinc (verified lossless, 40/40 goldens byte-identical) and fixed a pre-existing gap where absolute-mode $0000/$0001 did not route to PORT. Port routing extended to the undocumented opcodes via OP3 plus ZPPORT/ABSPORT operand tables. Both loaders offer the variant as a second non-preferred LoadSpec. 12 new Tier-2 tests (unblocked by grm-2pi) caught a real bug: the inline ':SAX "PORT"' form has no operand, so the target printed invisibly. OUTSTANDING: manual GUI check that both languages appear in the import dialog -- -processor bypasses the LoadSpec list, so no automated test covers it.
